      "content": "\"\"\"clawmetry/approvals.py — cloud-mediated approval policy engine.\n\nWatches the unified DuckDB event store (``clawmetry/local_store.py``) for\ntool calls that match a user-defined approval policy. When a match fires:\n\n  1. POST the request to ClawMetry cloud (`/api/approvals/request`)\n  2. Notify a human (cloud handles delivery — Slack/email/browser link)\n  3. Poll cloud (`/api/approvals/<id>`) every 3 s up to policy.timeout\n  4. On `denied` → abort the agent: gateway `sessions_kill(session_id)` for\n     OpenClaw sessions, the pid-based `process_control.kill_session` engine\n     (same one the Stop button uses) for family runtimes\n     (claude_code/codex/goose/opencode/aider — ids like `claude_code:UUID`)\n  5. On `timeout` → apply policy.on_timeout (default: deny → kill)\n  6. On `approved` → no-op, the action proceeds\n\nPolicies live in `~/.clawmetry/policies.yml`. See README + the in-app\nPolicies tab for the YAML format.\n\nCompanion to vivekchand/clawmetry#667 (issue) and the cloud receiver in\nvivekchand/clawmetry-cloud#337.\n\nBackward-compat NOTE (PRD vivekchand/clawmetry-cloud#779, audit P0 #6):\n  Prior to 2026-05-13 the watcher tail-globbed\n  ``~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/*.jsonl`` directly. That worked only\n  for OpenClaw — Hermes / Codex / Claude Code adapters were invisible to\n  the policy engine. The watcher now reads from\n  ``local_store.query_events()`` which every adapter feeds, so a policy\n  fires regardless of which framework produced the toolCall. The legacy\n  JSONL paths are no longer scanned. If you had tooling that depended on\n  the watcher reading JSONL directly, point it at the DuckDB store\n  (``~/.clawmetry/clawmetry.duckdb``) instead — the same events live\n  there. No flag is provided for graceful migration: the unified store\n  has a strict superset of the old data.\n\nDesign notes:\n  * Stateless watcher — restartable any time, resumes from a single\n    ``approvals_last_ingest_ms`` watermark (the events table's INGEST\n    stamp, not the event ts — see the watermark-race note above\n    ``watch_iteration``) persisted in ``~/.clawmetry/sync-state.json``.\n    The watermark survives daemon restarts, so already-decided approvals\n    are not re-evaluated.\n  * One in-flight approval per (session, tool_call_id). Multiple matches\n    on the same call collapse into one request — important so a session\n    that matches both \"rm\" AND \"outside-tmp\" policies doesn't get\n    duplicate Slack pings.\n  * NO HTTP retry storm — cloud round-trip uses the existing ``_post``\n    helper which already backs off + handles 429s.\n  * Soft-fail in OSS-only mode (no cloud configured): log and pass\n    through. The same code runs in pure-local installs without crashing.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport re\nimport json\nimport time\nimport uuid\nimport logging\nimport threading\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Callable, Optional\n\nlog = logging.getLogger(\"clawmetry-approvals\")\n\n# ── Kill-handler registry ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n#\n# Extension seam for closed-source runtimes (clawmetry-pro packages a handful\n# of them — nanoclaw, picoclaw, hermes …). Each runtime whose \"stop a session\"\n# story doesn't match the openclaw gateway RPC or the family-runtime pid-based\n# ``process_control.kill_session`` can register a callable here at import\n# time; ``_kill_session`` looks it up by the ``\"<runtime>:<id>\"`` prefix and\n# calls it BEFORE falling through to the built-in gateway/process paths.\n#\n# The callable takes the FULL session_id (e.g. ``\"nanoclaw:sess-abc\"``) and\n# returns True when the kill was carried out. Anything raised inside the\n# callable is logged and swallowed — a broken handler must NEVER escape into\n# the daemon loop, so a bad third-party plugin degrades to \"kill returned\n# False\" instead of crashing the approvals watcher thread.\nKILL_HANDLERS: dict[str, Callable[[str], bool]] = {}\n\n\ndef register_kill_handler(runtime: str, fn: Callable[[str], bool]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Register a runtime-specific kill callable. Idempotent overwrite.\n\n    ``runtime`` is the lowercase prefix of a session id\n    (e.g. ``\"nanoclaw\"``, ``\"picoclaw\"``). ``fn(session_id) -> bool``\n    returns True when the kill actually landed. Exceptions raised by ``fn``\n    are logged + swallowed by ``_kill_session``, never propagated.\"\"\"\n    KILL_HANDLERS[(runtime or \"\").strip().lower()] = fn\n\n\n# ── Pre-tool gate-handler registry ──────────────────────────────────────────\n#\n# Mirror of KILL_HANDLERS for the PRE-execution side. A \"gate\" is a\n# runtime-native mechanism that pauses a tool call BEFORE it runs (OpenClaw's\n# `exec-policy preset cautious`, Claude Code's PreToolUse hook, …) — the\n# reactive watcher below can only detect-and-kill AFTER the fact.\n#\n# Each handler is ``fn(want_gate: bool, policies: list[dict]) -> None`` and\n# MUST be:\n#   * idempotent — the watcher calls it every ~2 s with the current posture;\n#   * conservative — only undo what IT installed (state-file pattern, see\n#     _EXEC_POLICY_STATE / claude_code_gate._STATE_PATH), never clobbering a\n#     posture or hook the operator set by hand.\n# Exceptions raised inside a handler are logged and swallowed by\n# ``sync_runtime_gates`` — a broken gate plugin degrades to \"no gate\", it\n# never crashes the watcher thread.\nGATE_HANDLERS: dict[str, Callable[[bool, list], None]] = {}\n\n# Optional per-runtime \"do the active policies want this runtime gated?\"\n# predicate (receives the policies already filtered to that runtime).\n# Runtimes without an entry use the default: any require_approval policy.\nGATE_WANT_PREDICATES: dict[str, Callable[[list], bool]] = {}\n\n\ndef register_gate_handler(runtime: str, fn: Callable[[bool, list], None],\n                          want_fn: \"Optional[Callable[[list], bool]]\" = None,\n                          ) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Register a runtime-specific pre-tool gate callable. Idempotent\n    overwrite, same contract as :func:`register_kill_handler`.\n\n    ``fn(want_gate, policies)`` installs/refreshes the runtime's native\n    pre-execution gate when ``want_gate`` is True and removes ONLY what it\n    previously installed when False. ``want_fn(policies) -> bool`` optionally\n    overrides the default \"any require_approval policy\" want computation\n    (OpenClaw uses this to stay exec-only).\"\"\"\n    key = (runtime or \"\").strip().lower()\n    GATE_HANDLERS[key] = fn\n    if want_fn is not None:\n        GATE_WANT_PREDICATES[key] = want_fn\n\n\ndef _policies_for_runtime(policies, runtime: str) -> list:\n    \"\"\"Policies that apply to ``runtime``: explicit match or unset ('').\"\"\"\n    rt = (runtime or \"\").strip().lower()\n    out = []\n    for p in policies or []:\n        if not isinstance(p, dict):\n            continue\n        prt = str(p.get(\"runtime\") or \"\").strip().lower()\n        if prt in (\"\", rt):\n            out.append(p)\n    return out\n\n\ndef _default_want_gate(policies) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Default want-predicate: any active require_approval policy.\"\"\"\n    for p in policies or []:\n        if not isinstance(p, dict):\n            continue\n        if (p.get(\"action\") or \"require_approval\") == \"require_approval\":\n            return True\n    return False\n\nPOLICIES_PATH = Path.home() / \".clawmetry\" / \"policies.yml\"\n\n# ── Approve-and-remember (session scope) ─────────────────────────────────\n#\n# \"Approve for this session\" decisions live in a small JSON file so BOTH\n# the daemon's reactive watcher and the dashboard's pre-tool hook receiver\n# (different processes) honor them. Entries are keyed on\n# sha256(session_id | canonical tool | extracted command) — the SAME\n# normalisation match_policy uses — and expire after a TTL so a leaked\n# session id can't become a permanent bypass. \"Always allow\" decisions do\n# NOT live here: they become an ``action: approve`` policy row (the\n# existing always-allow mechanism), so they are visible and revocable in\n# the Approvals tab like any other rule.\n_SESSION_ALLOW_PATH = Path.home() / \".clawmetry\" / \"approvals_session_allow.json\"\n_SESSION_ALLOW_TTL_S = 24 * 3600\n\n\ndef _session_allow_key(session_id: str, tool_name: str, args) -> str:\n    import hashlib as _hl\n    cmd = _extract_command(tool_name, args if isinstance(args, dict) else {})\n    raw = f\"{session_id or ''}|{_canonical_tool(tool_name)}|{cmd}\"\n    return _hl.sha256(raw.encode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")).hexdigest()\n\n\ndef _load_session_allows() -> dict:\n    try:\n        if _SESSION_ALLOW_PATH.exists():\n            data = json.loads(_SESSION_ALLOW_PATH.read_text())\n            if isinstance(data, dict):\n                return data\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    return {}\n\n\ndef add_session_allow(session_id: str, tool_name: str, args,\n                      ttl_s: int = _SESSION_ALLOW_TTL_S) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Record \"approved for this session\" for this exact (session, tool,\n    command). Prunes expired entries on every write. Returns the key.\n    Never raises — a failed write degrades to re-prompting, never to a\n    blocked or auto-approved call.\"\"\"\n    key = _session_allow_key(session_id, tool_name, args)\n    try:\n        now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)\n        data = {k: v for k, v in _load_session_allows().items()\n                if isinstance(v, dict)\n                and int(v.get(\"expires_ms\") or 0) > now_ms}\n        data[key] = {\n            \"expires_ms\": now_ms + int(ttl_s) * 1000,\n            \"session_id\": (session_id or \"\")[:120],\n            \"tool\": _canonical_tool(tool_name),\n            \"command_preview\": _extract_command(\n                tool_name, args if isinstance(args, dict) else {})[:140],\n        }\n        _SESSION_ALLOW_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        tmp = _SESSION_ALLOW_PATH.with_suffix(\".json.tmp\")\n        tmp.write_text(json.dumps(data))\n        os.replace(tmp, _SESSION_ALLOW_PATH)\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.debug(\"session-allow write failed: %s\", e)\n    return key\n\n\ndef check_session_allow(session_id: str, tool_name: str, args) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when this exact (session, tool, command) was approved earlier\n    this session and the entry has not expired. Read-only, never raises.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        entry = _load_session_allows().get(\n            _session_allow_key(session_id, tool_name, args))\n        return (isinstance(entry, dict)\n                and int(entry.get(\"expires_ms\") or 0) > time.time() * 1000)\n    except Exception:\n        return False\n\n# Default poll interval when waiting on a decision; cloud has 60-300 s timeouts\n# typically so 3 s gives the user perceived responsiveness without hammering\n# the API.\n_POLL_INTERVAL_SEC = 3.0\n\n\ndef _poll_interval(waited_s: float) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Adaptive decision-poll cadence for long approval windows (7-day\n    default, #4066): snappy while the human is likely mid-tap, gentle for\n    the long tail — a week at 3s would be ~200k requests per approval.\n    3s for the first 2 min, 15s until the first hour, then 60s.\"\"\"\n    if waited_s < 120:\n        return _POLL_INTERVAL_SEC\n    if waited_s < 3600:\n        return 15.0\n    return 60.0\n\n# Track in-flight approvals so we don't re-request on a watcher restart that\n# replays the same toolCall row. Keyed by tool_call_id (or composite when\n# missing — `f\"{session_id}:{ts}\"`).\n_in_flight: dict[str, dict] = {}\n_in_flight_lock = threading.Lock()\n\n\n# ── Policy loading ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n\ndef _load_yaml(text: str) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Tiny YAML subset reader so we don't add PyYAML as a daemon dep.\n\n    Supports the exact shape we document: a top-level list of dicts where\n    each dict has scalar values OR a nested ``match`` dict. No anchors,\n    multi-line strings, or other YAML exotica.\n\n    For anything beyond the trivial format users hit, they can install\n    pyyaml and we'll prefer that — see the import-fallback below.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        import yaml as _yaml  # type: ignore\n        return _yaml.safe_load(text) or []\n    except ImportError:\n        pass\n    # Hand-rolled minimal parser. Documented as \"best-effort\"; users with\n    # complex policies are expected to `pip install pyyaml`.\n    out: list[dict] = []\n    cur: Optional[dict] = None\n    cur_match: Optional[dict] = None\n    for raw_line in text.splitlines():\n        line = raw_line.rstrip()\n        if not line or line.lstrip().startswith(\"#\"):\n            continue\n        if line.startswith(\"- \"):\n            cur = {}\n            cur_match = None\n            out.append(cur)\n            kv = line[2:]\n            if \":\" in kv:\n                k, _, v = kv.partition(\":\")\n                cur[k.strip()] = _yaml_scalar(v.strip())\n            continue\n        if cur is None:\n            continue\n        # Nested ``match:``\n        stripped = line.lstrip()\n        indent = len(line) - len(stripped)\n        if stripped.endswith(\":\") and indent <= 4:\n            key = stripped[:-1].strip()\n            if key == \"match\":\n                cur_match = {}\n                cur[key] = cur_match\n            continue\n        if \":\" in stripped:\n            k, _, v = stripped.partition(\":\")\n            target = cur_match if (cur_match is not None and indent >= 4) else cur\n            target[k.strip()] = _yaml_scalar(v.strip())\n    return [d for d in out if d]\n\n\ndef _yaml_scalar(s: str):\n    if s == \"\" or s in (\"~\", \"null\"):\n        return None\n    if s.lower() in (\"true\", \"false\"):\n        return s.lower() == \"true\"\n    try:\n        if \".\" not in s:\n            return int(s)\n    except ValueError:\n        pass\n    if (s.startswith(\"'\") and s.endswith(\"'\")) or (s.startswith('\"') and s.endswith('\"')):\n        return s[1:-1]\n    return s\n\n\ndef action_label(tool_name: str, command: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The one-line label an approval card leads with.\n\n    ``\"<tool>: <command>\"`` when we know the command, and a bare ``\"<tool>\"``\n    when we do not. The old unconditional join printed the empty preview\n    straight after the colon, so an operator read ``exec: {}`` -- a card that\n    names a tool and then shows punctuation where the command belongs. A\n    reader can tell \"we did not record the command\" from a bare tool name;\n    they cannot tell it from braces.\"\"\"\n    tool = str(tool_name or \"tool call\").strip()\n    cmd = str(command or \"\").strip()\n    return f\"{tool}: {cmd}\" if cmd else tool\n\n\n# Minimum risk level implied by a shipped preset key, used to repair rows\n# whose ``min_risk`` did not survive a round trip through storage. Only\n# presets whose WHOLE definition is the risk gate belong here -- a preset\n# that matches on a command regex needs no entry.\n_PRESET_MIN_RISK: dict[str, str] = {\"risk_high\": \"high\"}\n\n\ndef _compile_policy(p: dict) -> Optional[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Compile a single raw policy dict into a match-ready dict, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = p.get(\"match\") or {}\n    # Cloud-stored policies use top-level fields instead of nested `match`\n    tool = (match.get(\"tool\") or p.get(\"tool\") or \"\").strip()\n    cmd_re_str = match.get(\"command_regex\") or (\n        p.get(\"pattern\") if p.get(\"pattern_type\") == \"command_regex\" else None\n    )\n    cmd_not_re = match.get(\"command_not_regex\")\n    args_re = match.get(\"args_regex\")\n    # Risk-level gate: policy fires only when the CALL classifies at or\n    # above this level (clawmetry/tool_risk.py). Unknown strings are\n    # rejected here so a typo (\"hgih\") can't silently disable the gate.\n    min_risk = str(p.get(\"min_risk\") or match.get(\"min_risk\")\n                   or \"\").strip().lower() or None\n    # Preset rows created through the cloud lost their min_risk on the way to\n    # the database (the cloud policies table had no such column until\n    # 2026-09-06), which turned the shipped \"Require approval for high-risk\n    # actions\" preset -- tool '', pattern '', min_risk 'high' -- into a rule\n    # with NO condition at all: it matched every tool call of every runtime\n    # and buried the operator in approvals for `git status`. A preset carries\n    # its own intent, so recover it from the key rather than trusting a row\n    # that lost a field. Explicit min_risk on the row always wins.\n    if min_risk is None:\n        min_risk = _PRESET_MIN_RISK.get(\n            str(p.get(\"preset_key\") or \"\").strip().lower())\n    if min_risk is not None:\n        from clawmetry.tool_risk import RISK_RANK\n        if min_risk not in RISK_RANK:\n            log.warning(f\"policy '{p.get('name')}' has unknown min_risk \"\n                        f\"'{min_risk}' (want low/medium/high/critical)\")\n            return None\n    try:\n        compiled = {\n            \"name\": p.get(\"name\") or \"(unnamed)\",\n            \"tool\": tool,\n            # Optional per-runtime scoping ('' = applies to every runtime).\n            # Drives the pre-tool gate seam (sync_runtime_gates): a policy\n            # with runtime \"claude_code\" installs the Claude Code PreToolUse\n            # hook but never flips OpenClaw's exec preset, and vice versa.\n            \"runtime\": str(p.get(\"runtime\")\n                           or match.get(\"runtime\") or \"\").strip().lower(),\n            \"command_regex\": re.compile(cmd_re_str) if cmd_re_str else None,\n            \"command_not_regex\": re.compile(cmd_not_re) if cmd_not_re else None,\n            \"args_regex\": re.compile(args_re) if args_re else None,\n            \"min_risk\": min_risk,\n            \"action\": (p.get(\"action\") or \"require_approval\").strip(),\n            \"timeout\": int(p.get(\"timeout\") or 604800),  # default 7d (#4066)\n            \"on_timeout\": (p.get(\"on_timeout\") or \"deny\").strip(),\n        }\n    except re.error as re_err:\n        log.warning(f\"policy '{p.get('name')}' has bad regex: {re_err}\")\n        return None\n    # A gating policy with no tool, no pattern and no risk floor has no\n    # condition: it pauses EVERY tool call on the node. That is a legal thing\n    # to ask for, but it is almost always a row that lost a field on the way\n    # here, so say so once, loudly, naming the policy -- an operator drowning\n    # in approvals should be able to find out why from the daemon log.\n    if compiled[\"action\"] != \"approve\" and not (\n            compiled[\"tool\"] or compiled[\"command_regex\"]\n            or compiled[\"args_regex\"] or compiled[\"min_risk\"]):\n        log.warning(\"policy %r has no tool, no pattern and no min_risk: it \"\n                    \"will pause EVERY tool call on this node\",\n                    compiled[\"name\"])\n        compiled[\"matches_everything\"] = True\n    return compiled\n\n\n# Fingerprint of the last policy set we announced, so a reload that changes\n# nothing stays quiet. None until the first successful load.\n_last_policy_signature: Optional[tuple] = None\n\n\ndef _policy_signature(compiled: list[dict]) -> tuple:\n    \"\"\"Order-sensitive fingerprint of a compiled policy set.\n\n    Compiled entries hold ``re.Pattern`` objects, which do not compare equal\n    across compilations, so fingerprint their source patterns instead.\n    \"\"\"\n    return tuple(\n        (\n            c.get(\"name\"),\n            c.get(\"tool\"),\n            c.get(\"action\"),\n            c.get(\"timeout\"),\n            c.get(\"on_timeout\"),\n            getattr(c.get(\"command_regex\"), \"pattern\", None),\n            getattr(c.get(\"command_not_regex\"), \"pattern\", None),\n            getattr(c.get(\"args_regex\"), \"pattern\", None),\n        )\n        for c in compiled\n    )\n\n\ndef load_policies(api_key: Optional[str] = None) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Load policies from local YAML + cloud (if api_key is set).\n\n    Cloud-stored policies (created from the UI) take precedence and are\n    merged with local YAML policies. This lets non-technical users create\n    rules from the dashboard while power users keep their YAML.\n    \"\"\"\n    compiled: list[dict] = []\n\n    # 1) Cloud-stored policies (UI-created)\n    if api_key:\n        try:\n            cloud = _fetch_cloud_policies(api_key)\n            for p in cloud:\n                if not p.get(\"enabled\", True):\n                    continue\n                c = _compile_policy(p)\n                if c:\n                    compiled.append(c)\n            if compiled:\n                log.debug(f\"loaded {len(compiled)} cloud policies\")\n        except Exception as e:\n            log.debug(f\"cloud policies fetch failed (will use local): {e}\")\n\n    # 2) Local YAML policies\n    if POLICIES_PATH.exists():\n        try:\n            raw = POLICIES_PATH.read_text(errors=\"replace\")\n            for p in _load_yaml(raw):\n                if not isinstance(p, dict):\n                    continue\n                c = _compile_policy(p)\n                if c:\n                    compiled.append(c)\n        except Exception as e:\n            log.warning(f\"failed to read {POLICIES_PATH}: {e}\")\n\n    if compiled:\n        # This runs on every evaluation pass (multiple times a minute). Only\n        # say something at INFO when the policy set actually CHANGED —\n        # otherwise it is 1,300+ identical lines per log file, which buries\n        # the errors an operator is grepping for.\n        global _last_policy_signature\n        signature = _policy_signature(compiled)\n        if signature != _last_policy_signature:\n            _last_policy_signature = signature\n            log.info(f\"loaded {len(compiled)} approval policies \"\n                     f\"(cloud + {POLICIES_PATH})\")\n        else:\n            log.debug(f\"approval policies unchanged ({len(compiled)})\")\n    return compiled\n\n\n_cloud_policies_cache: tuple = (0.0, [])\n_CLOUD_CACHE_TTL = 30.0  # re-fetch from cloud every 30 s\n\n\ndef _fetch_cloud_policies(api_key: str) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"GET /api/cloud/policies with a short TTL cache.\"\"\"\n    global _cloud_policies_cache\n    now = time.time()\n    if now - _cloud_policies_cache[0] < _CLOUD_CACHE_TTL:\n        return _cloud_policies_cache[1]\n    import urllib.request\n    from clawmetry.sync import INGEST_URL\n    req = urllib.request.Request(\n        f\"{INGEST_URL.rstrip('/')}/api/cloud/policies\",\n        headers={\"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {api_key}\"},\n        method=\"GET\",\n    )\n    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:\n        data = json.loads(resp.read())\n    policies = data.get(\"policies\") or []\n    _cloud_policies_cache = (now, policies)\n    return policies\n\n\n# ── Match engine ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n# Harness-agnostic tool categories + command extraction now live in\n# ``clawmetry/tool_risk.py`` (the leaf module the risk classifier, the\n# watcher, replay, and the pre-tool hook gate all share — ONE source of\n# truth so the four surfaces can never drift). Re-exported here because\n# routes/hooks.py, claude_code_gate.py and tests import them from this\n# module.\nfrom clawmetry.tool_risk import (  # noqa: E402,F401  (re-export)\n    _TOOL_CANON, _canonical_tool, _extract_command,\n    classify_tool_call, risk_rank,\n)\n\n\ndef match_policy(policies: list[dict], tool_name: str, args: dict,\n                 context: Optional[dict] = None):\n    \"\"\"Return the FIRST matching policy or None.\n\n    ``context`` is the pre-tool gate's untrusted-content context for the\n    current turn (``prompt_injection.coerce_context``). When present, a\n    ``min_risk`` rule compares against the call's risk raised for that\n    context (``prompt_injection.effective_risk``, REQ-GOV-PIJ-002). Absent,\n    the rating is exactly the call's own.\n\n    Tool-name match is exact (case-insensitive); command/args matches are\n    regex .search() so partial matches count.\n\n    ``action: approve`` (always-allow) rules are evaluated FIRST regardless\n    of list order: a user's explicit \"always allow `git ls-files`\" must\n    outrank the catch-all \"ask before shell commands\" rule that would\n    otherwise pause it (Pushary-style remember-my-choice, cloud #1783).\n    They are narrow, user-authored rules; authoring a broad one is an\n    explicit choice, same as any allowlist.\n    \"\"\"\n    cmd = _extract_command(tool_name, args)\n    args_str = \"\"\n    try:\n        args_str = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True) if isinstance(args, dict) else str(args)\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    ordered = ([p for p in policies if (p.get(\"action\") or \"\") == \"approve\"] +\n               [p for p in policies if (p.get(\"action\") or \"\") != \"approve\"])\n    # Risk is classified at most once per call, and only when some policy\n    # actually gates on it (zero cost for min_risk-free policy sets).\n    call_risk_rank: Optional[int] = None\n    for p in ordered:\n        # Harness-agnostic tool match: a policy authored for ``exec`` matches a\n        # ``Bash`` / ``shell`` toolCall (see _canonical_tool). Falls back to a\n        # plain case-insensitive compare when neither side maps to a category.\n        if p.get(\"tool\") and _canonical_tool(tool_name) != _canonical_tool(p[\"tool\"]):\n            continue\n        if p.get(\"command_regex\") and not p[\"command_regex\"].search(cmd):\n            continue\n        if p.get(\"command_not_regex\") and p[\"command_not_regex\"].search(cmd):\n            continue\n        if p.get(\"args_regex\") and not p[\"args_regex\"].search(args_str):\n            continue\n        if p.get(\"min_risk\"):\n            if call_risk_rank is None:\n                verdict = classify_tool_call(tool_name, args)\n                if context:\n                    from clawmetry.prompt_injection import effective_risk\n                    verdict = effective_risk(verdict, context)\n                call_risk_rank = verdict[\"rank\"]\n            if call_risk_rank < risk_rank(p[\"min_risk\"]):\n                continue\n        return p\n    return None\n\n\ndef replay_policy(policy: dict, rows: list[dict], max_samples: int = 20) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Replay a CANDIDATE policy over historical tool-call events and report\n    what it WOULD have paused — without creating approvals, blocking anything,\n    or touching the cloud (the \"eval before you enable\" loop, CrabTrap-style).\n\n    ``policy`` is a raw policy dict (same shape as ``policies.yml`` / the\n    cloud builder rows — ``_compile_policy`` handles both). ``rows`` are\n    events-table rows in ``query_events`` shape. Pure function: no store\n    access and no network, so callers fetch rows however they like (route\n    handlers go through the daemon proxy) and pass them in.\n\n    Returns ``{ok, policy, scanned_events, scanned_tool_calls, matches,\n    by_runtime, by_tool, samples}`` or ``{ok: False, error}`` on a bad policy.\n    \"\"\"\n    compiled = _compile_policy(policy)\n    if compiled is None:\n        return {\"ok\": False, \"error\": \"invalid policy (bad regex or shape)\"}\n    try:\n        from clawmetry.sync import _runtime_of_session as _rt_of\n    except Exception:  # pure-OSS edge: attribution degrades, replay still works\n        def _rt_of(sid: str) -> str:\n            return \"openclaw\"\n    scanned_events = 0\n    scanned_tool_calls = 0\n    matches = 0\n    by_runtime: dict[str, int] = {}\n    by_tool: dict[str, int] = {}\n    samples: list[dict] = []\n    seen_rows: set = set()\n    for row in rows or []:\n        if not isinstance(row, dict):\n            continue\n        rid = row.get(\"id\")\n        if rid is not None:\n            # The caller merges per-event_type queries; dedup row ids so an\n            # event present in both result sets counts once.\n            if rid in seen_rows:\n                continue\n            seen_rows.add(rid)\n        data = row.get(\"data\")\n        if isinstance(data, str):\n            # Cross-process transports may serialise the data column.\n            try:\n                row = dict(row, data=json.loads(data))\n            except Exception:\n                pass\n        scanned_events += 1\n        sid = row.get(\"session_id\") or \"\"\n        for _tcid, tool_name, args in _extract_tool_blocks(row):\n            if not tool_name:\n                continue\n            args = args if isinstance(args, dict) else {}\n            scanned_tool_calls += 1\n            if match_policy([compiled], tool_name, args) is None:\n                continue\n            matches += 1\n            rt = _rt_of(sid)\n            by_runtime[rt] = by_runtime.get(rt, 0) + 1\n            canon = _canonical_tool(tool_name)\n            by_tool[canon] = by_tool.get(canon, 0) + 1\n            if len(samples) < max_samples:\n                samples.append({\n                    \"ts\": row.get(\"ts\"),\n                    \"session_id\": sid,\n                    \"runtime\": rt,\n                    \"tool\": tool_name,\n                    \"command\": _extract_command(tool_name, args)[:160],\n                })\n    return {\n        \"ok\": True,\n        \"policy\": compiled[\"name\"],\n        \"scanned_events\": scanned_events,\n        \"scanned_tool_calls\": scanned_tool_calls,\n        \"matches\": matches,\n        \"by_runtime\": by_runtime,\n        \"by_tool\": by_tool,\n        \"samples\": samples,\n    }\n\n\n# ── Cloud round-trip ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n\ndef _post_approval_request(api_key: str, payload: dict) -> Optional[dict]:\n    \"\"\"POST to cloud's /api/approvals/request. Returns dict or None on failure.\n\n    We don't reuse `clawmetry.sync._post` because that ships X-Api-Key, but\n    the cloud auth shim only honors `Authorization: Bearer` for /api/* paths.\n    \"\"\"\n    import urllib.request, urllib.error\n    from clawmetry.sync import INGEST_URL\n    try:\n        body = json.dumps(payload).encode()\n        headers = {\n            \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\",\n            \"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {api_key}\",\n        }\n        if payload.get(\"node_id\"):\n            headers[\"X-Node-Id\"] = payload[\"node_id\"]\n        req = urllib.request.Request(\n            f\"{INGEST_URL.rstrip('/')}/api/approvals/request\",\n            data=body, headers=headers, method=\"POST\",\n        )\n        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15) as resp:\n            return json.loads(resp.read())\n    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:\n        try:\n            err_body = e.read().decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")[:200]\n        except Exception:\n            err_body = \"\"\n        log.warning(f\"approval request POST failed: HTTP {e.code} — {err_body}\")\n        return None\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.warning(f\"approval request POST failed: {e}\")\n        return None\n\n\ndef _poll_decision_local(approval_id: str, timeout_s: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Poll the LOCAL DuckDB store for a decision — used by the local-only\n    blocking-approvals path (a self-hosted node without a ``cm_`` cloud\n    token). Same cadence as :func:`_poll_decision` (3 s, 5 s grace past the\n    policy timeout). Returns one of ``approved`` / ``denied`` /\n    ``timeout`` / ``error``.\n\n    The row itself is authored by the ``ingest_approval`` call earlier in\n    ``process_tool_call``; the decision arrives from a POST to\n    ``/api/approvals/<approval_id>/decide`` (routes/policy.py) which flips\n    the row's ``status`` via ``update_approval_decision``. No network, no\n    cloud auth — the whole loop stays inside the box.\"\"\"\n    start = time.time()\n    deadline = start + timeout_s + 5  # 5 s grace past policy expiry\n    last_status = \"pending\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store as _lsm\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.warning(\"approvals(local): local_store import failed: %s\", e)\n        return \"error\"\n    while time.time() < deadline:\n        try:\n            store = _lsm.get_store(read_only=True)\n            rows = store.query_approvals(limit=1) or []\n            row = None\n            for r in rows or []:\n                if r.get(\"id\") == approval_id:\n                    row = r\n                    break\n            if row is None:\n                # ``query_approvals`` with no filters returns most-recent\n                # first — the id we just wrote should be at the top, but a\n                # bursty node might have pushed us off the first page. Fall\n                # back to a wider read one time per poll.\n                for r in store.query_approvals(limit=200) or []:\n                    if r.get(\"id\") == approval_id:\n                        row = r\n                        break\n            if row is not None:\n                last_status = str(row.get(\"status\") or \"pending\").strip()\n                if last_status in (\"approved\", \"denied\", \"timeout\", \"expired\"):\n                    return last_status\n        except Exception as e:\n            log.debug(\"approvals(local): poll error (will retry): %s\", e)\n        time.sleep(_poll_interval(time.time() - start))\n    return last_status if last_status != \"pending\" else \"timeout\"\n\n\ndef _local_blocking_enabled(api_key: Optional[str]) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when the local-only blocking branch should own this approval.\n\n    Two conditions must both hold:\n      1. No ``cm_`` cloud token on this node. An empty ``api_key`` (pure\n         self-hosted) or a license-issued token (``lc_`` /\n         ``clawlic_``/...) both qualify — cloud auth is the ONE thing the\n         cm_ prefix asserts.\n      2. The resolved entitlement allows the ``approval_queue`` feature.\n         Grace mode (default) short-circuits this to True, so a fresh OSS\n         install still sees local blocking; enforce-mode unlicensed nodes\n         return False and the caller falls through to the historical\n         cloud-required behaviour (which soft-fails to OPEN when the\n         cloud is unreachable — no regression for that population).\n\n    Never raises; a flaky entitlement read collapses to False so the\n    caller keeps its existing cloud path.\"\"\"\n    ak = (api_key or \"\").strip()\n    if ak.startswith(\"cm_\"):\n        return False\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import entitlements as _ent\n        return _ent.get_entitlement().allows_feature(\"approval_queue\")\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.debug(\"approvals(local): entitlement read failed: %s\", e)\n        return False\n\n\ndef _poll_decision(api_key: str, approval_id: str, timeout_s: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Poll cloud for the decision. Returns one of: approved/denied/timeout/error.\"\"\"\n    import urllib.request\n    start = time.time()\n    deadline = start + timeout_s + 5  # 5 s grace past policy expiry\n    last_status = \"pending\"\n    while time.time() < deadline:\n        try:\n            from clawmetry.sync import INGEST_URL\n            req = urllib.request.Request(\n                f\"{INGEST_URL.rstrip('/')}/api/approvals/{approval_id}\",\n                headers={\"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {api_key}\"},\n                method=\"GET\",\n            )\n            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:\n                data = json.loads(resp.read())\n                last_status = data.get(\"status\", \"pending\")\n                if last_status in (\"approved\", \"denied\", \"timeout\", \"expired\"):\n                    return last_status\n        except Exception as e:\n            log.debug(f\"poll error (will retry): {e}\")\n        time.sleep(_poll_interval(time.time() - start))\n    return last_status if last_status != \"pending\" else \"timeout\"\n\n\ndef _session_runtime(session_id: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Runtime of a session id (its ``<runtime>:`` prefix, else openclaw).\n\n    Prefers ``sync._runtime_of_session`` (the canonical prefix map) and falls\n    back to a plain prefix parse so this module keeps working if sync isn't\n    importable (pure-OSS unit tests).\"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry.sync import _runtime_of_session\n        return _runtime_of_session(session_id)\n    except Exception:\n        sid = session_id or \"\"\n        i = sid.find(\":\")\n        if i > 0:\n            return sid[:i].lower()\n        return \"openclaw\"\n\n\n# Working directory per session, memoised. An approval card that cannot say\n# WHERE the command would run is asking the operator to approve a `git push`\n# without telling them which checkout. Missing/unknown stays \"\" -- never a\n# guessed path.\n_session_cwd_cache: dict[str, str] = {}\n_SESSION_CWD_CACHE_MAX = 512\n\n\ndef _session_cwd(session_id: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Best-effort cwd for a session id, from the local store. Never raises.\"\"\"\n    sid = session_id or \"\"\n    if not sid:\n        return \"\"\n    if sid in _session_cwd_cache:\n        return _session_cwd_cache[sid]\n    cwd = \"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store\n        store = local_store.get_store(read_only=True)\n        # Family runtimes are stored under the prefixed id, OpenClaw under the\n        # bare one; try what we were handed, then the other half.\n        for cand in (sid, sid.split(\":\", 1)[1] if \":\" in sid else None):\n            if not cand:\n                continue\n            row = store.get_session_location(cand)\n            if row and row.get(\"cwd\"):\n                cwd = str(row[\"cwd\"])\n                break\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.debug(\"approval cwd lookup failed for %s: %s\", sid, e)\n    if len(_session_cwd_cache) >= _SESSION_CWD_CACHE_MAX:\n        _session_cwd_cache.clear()\n    _session_cwd_cache[sid] = cwd\n    return cwd\n\n\n_hooks_marker_cache: tuple = (0.0, frozenset())\n_HOOKS_MARKER_TTL_S = 10.0\n_HOOKS_MARKER_PATH = Path.home() / \".clawmetry\" / \"hooks_installed.json\"\n\n\ndef _hook_covered_runtimes() -> frozenset:\n    \"\"\"Runtimes whose tool calls are pre-execution gated by an installed\n    agent hook (written by ``clawmetry hooks install``, see\n    hooks_claude_code.py). The reactive watcher skips these sessions — the\n    hook already paused the call BEFORE execution, and a phone-denied tool\n    call must not ALSO get its session killed by the detect-after path.\n\n    TTL-cached: watch_iteration runs every ~2s and this must not stat/parse\n    JSON on every pass. Marker keys are runtime names (\"claude_code\").\"\"\"\n    global _hooks_marker_cache\n    now = time.time()\n    if now - _hooks_marker_cache[0] < _HOOKS_MARKER_TTL_S:\n        return _hooks_marker_cache[1]\n    covered: frozenset = frozenset()\n    try:\n        if _HOOKS_MARKER_PATH.exists():\n            data = json.loads(_HOOKS_MARKER_PATH.read_text())\n            covered = frozenset(\n                rt for rt, meta in data.items()\n                if isinstance(meta, dict)\n                and \"PreToolUse\" in (meta.get(\"events\") or []))\n    except Exception:\n        covered = frozenset()\n    _hooks_marker_cache = (now, covered)\n    return covered\n\n\ndef _session_cwd_hint(session_id: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Best-effort working-directory hint for cwd-resolved runtimes\n    (codex/goose/opencode/aider). Family adapters store the agent's cwd in\n    the event ``workspace_id`` column when known; claude_code doesn't need\n    it (per-pid session map). Never raises; '' when unknown.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store\n        store = local_store.get_store(read_only=True)\n        for r in store.query_events(session_id=session_id, limit=1):\n            ws = r.get(\"workspace_id\")\n            if isinstance(ws, str) and (\n                ws.startswith(\"/\") or ws.startswith(\"~\")\n                or (len(ws) > 2 and ws[1] == \":\")\n            ):\n                return ws\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    return \"\"\n\n\ndef _gateway_kill_session(session_id: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Kill an OpenClaw session via the gateway WebSocket RPC.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        # Late import to avoid pulling Flask into the daemon. helpers/gateway\n        # is the OSS package's gateway WS client.\n        import importlib.util as _ilu, sys as _s, os as _o\n        try:\n            import clawmetry as _cm\n            oss_root = _o.path.dirname(_o.path.dirname(_cm.__file__))\n        except Exception:\n            return False\n        helpers_path = _o.path.join(oss_root, \"helpers\", \"gateway.py\")\n        if not _o.path.isfile(helpers_path):\n            return False\n        if \"helpers.gateway\" not in _s.modules:\n            spec = _ilu.spec_from_file_location(\"_oss_gw_for_kill\", helpers_path)\n            mod = _ilu.module_from_spec(spec)\n            spec.loader.exec_module(mod)\n        else:\n            mod = _s.modules[\"helpers.gateway\"]\n        rpc = getattr(mod, \"_gw_ws_rpc\", None)\n        if not rpc:\n            return False\n        # OpenClaw's session-kill RPC name varies: try a few\n        for method in (\"sessions_kill\", \"session_kill\", \"kill_session\"):\n            try:\n                r = rpc(method, {\"sessionId\": session_id})\n                if r is not None:\n                    log.info(f\"killed session {session_id} via gateway {method}\")\n                    return True\n            except Exception:\n                continue\n        return False\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.warning(f\"gateway kill_session({session_id}) failed: {e}\")\n        return False\n\n\ndef _process_control_kill(session_id: str, runtime: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Kill a family-runtime session via the SAME pid-based engine the\n    Stop button uses (``clawmetry/process_control.py``): resolve the session\n    to its live pid (pid-reuse guarded), SIGTERM, escalate to SIGKILL of the\n    descendant tree. Never raises.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import process_control as _pc\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.warning(f\"process_control unavailable for kill of {session_id}: {e}\")\n        return False\n    # The store keys family sessions as '<runtime>:<bare-id>'; the process\n    # maps (e.g. ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json) key by the BARE id.\n    bare = (session_id or \"\").rsplit(\":\", 1)[-1]\n    cwd = _session_cwd_hint(session_id)\n    try:\n        res = _pc.kill_session(runtime, bare, cwd) or {}\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.warning(f\"process_control kill_session({session_id}) raised: {e}\")\n        return False\n    if res.get(\"ok\"):\n        log.info(f\"killed session {session_id} via process_control \"\n                 f\"(pid={res.get('pid')}, detail={res.get('detail')})\")\n        return True\n    log.warning(f\"process_control kill failed for {session_id}: \"\n                f\"{res.get('detail') or res.get('reason') or 'unknown'}\")\n    return False\n\n\ndef _kill_session(session_id: Optional[str]) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Best-effort kill of a denied session, runtime-aware.\n\n    * OpenClaw sessions -> gateway WebSocket RPC (the historical path).\n    * Runtimes registered via :func:`register_kill_handler` (clawmetry-pro\n      plugs nanoclaw / picoclaw / hermes here) -> the registered callable,\n      picked by the ``<runtime>:`` prefix on the session id. Exceptions\n      raised inside the handler are logged + swallowed so a bad plugin\n      degrades to \"handler returned False\", never crashes the watcher.\n    * Family runtimes (claude_code / codex / goose / opencode / aider / ...,\n      session ids like ``claude_code:UUID``) -> the pid-based\n      ``process_control.kill_session`` engine the Stop button uses. The\n      gateway does not know these sessions, so before 2026-07-02 a DENY\n      logged ``killed=False`` and the denied agent KEPT RUNNING (live repro:\n      approval 7d202307907a4f12bd8af5aa17c62c76).\n\n    Fail-safe: if the primary mechanism fails we try the other one, and if\n    neither works we return False (callers log the warning).\"\"\"\n    if not session_id:\n        return False\n    runtime = _session_runtime(session_id)\n    # OpenClaw stays on the gateway path first — the historical behaviour\n    # every existing test asserts (see tests/test_approvals_deny_kill.py).\n    if runtime == \"openclaw\":\n        return _gateway_kill_session(session_id)\n    # Runtime-registered handler wins for anything else. This is the seam\n    # clawmetry-pro drives to kill nanoclaw/picoclaw/hermes sessions that\n    # neither the gateway nor process_control knows about.\n    handler = KILL_HANDLERS.get(runtime)\n    if handler is not None:\n        try:\n            ok = handler(session_id)\n        except Exception as e:\n            log.warning(\"registered kill handler for runtime=%r raised on \"\n                        \"%s: %s\", runtime, session_id, e)\n            ok = False\n        if ok:\n            log.info(\"killed session %s via registered kill handler \"\n                     \"(runtime=%s)\", session_id, runtime)\n            return True\n        # Handler returned falsy → fall through to the built-in family\n        # path (many plugins don't cover every session shape yet).\n    if _process_control_kill(session_id, runtime):\n        return True\n    # Last resort: some wrapped setups register the session with the\n    # gateway anyway. Harmless when it doesn't.\n    return _gateway_kill_session(session_id)\n\n\n# ── Public entry point: process one toolCall event ────────────────────────\n\n\ndef process_tool_call(api_key: str, node_id: str, session_id: Optional[str],\n                       tool_call_id: str, tool_name: str, args: dict,\n                       policies: Optional[list[dict]] = None,\n                       kill_on_deny: bool = True) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Check a fresh toolCall against active policies and (if matched) request\n    a cloud-mediated approval.\n\n    Blocks for up to policy.timeout seconds while waiting for the decision.\n    A policy with ``action: monitor`` never blocks: it records a\n    ``simulated`` approval row (dry-run) and returns immediately.\n    Returns: {decision: approved|denied|timeout|monitored|no_policy|error,\n              policy: <name or None>, killed: bool}\n\n    ``kill_on_deny=False`` is the pre-execution hook path (hooks_claude_code):\n    the hook blocks the ONE denied tool call via the hook protocol, so\n    killing the whole session on deny would be double punishment — the\n    Pushary-style contract is \"deny this call, agent continues\".\n    \"\"\"\n    if policies is None:\n        policies = load_policies()\n    if not policies:\n        return {\"decision\": \"no_policy\", \"policy\": None, \"killed\": False}\n    policy = match_policy(policies, tool_name, args)\n    if not policy:\n        return {\"decision\": \"no_policy\", \"policy\": None, \"killed\": False}\n    # Dedup\n    key = tool_call_id or f\"{session_id}:{int(time.time()*1000)}\"\n    with _in_flight_lock:\n        if key in _in_flight:\n            return _in_flight[key]\n        _in_flight[key] = {\"decision\": \"pending\", \"policy\": policy[\"name\"], \"killed\": False}\n\n    cmd_preview = _extract_command(tool_name, args)[:140]\n    # Call-level risk verdict (tool_risk.py) — stamped into the approval\n    # row's args blob under the namespaced ``_cm_risk`` key so the queue,\n    # the audit feed, and the cloud inbox can render a risk chip without a\n    # schema migration (the raw tool args keys stay untouched).\n    risk = classify_tool_call(tool_name, args)\n    args_with_risk = dict(args) if isinstance(args, dict) else {\"value\": args}\n    args_with_risk[\"_cm_risk\"] = {\"level\": risk[\"level\"],\n                                  \"reasons\": risk[\"reasons\"]}\n    # Same namespaced-key trick for the WHO/WHERE/WHY of the request. Without\n    # it a queue row carried the tool and the command and nothing else, so the\n    # inbox could only print the tail of a session id -- an operator looking at\n    # twenty of them had no way to tell which agent, in which checkout, tripped\n    # which rule. Best-effort audit\n        # row so the decision trail shows WHY it sailed through.\n        try:\n            import hashlib as _hl\n            from clawmetry import local_store as _lsm\n            _lsm.get_store().ingest_approval({\n                \"id\": approval_id,\n                \"owner_hash\": _hl.sha256((api_key or \"\").encode()).hexdigest(),\n                \"requestor_session_id\": session_id,\n                \"action\": action_label(tool_name, cmd_preview),\n                \"args\": args_with_risk,\n                \"status\": \"auto_approved\",\n                \"decision_reason\": (f\"always-allow rule '{policy['name']}' \"\n                                    \"matched\"),\n                \"created_at\": time.strftime(\"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\", time.gmtime()),\n            })\n        except Exception as _aae:\n            log.debug(\"auto-approve persist failed: %s\", _aae)\n        try:\n            from clawmetry import audit as _audit\n            _audit.audit_event(\n                \"approval.auto_approved\", actor=\"policy\", target=tool_name,\n                result=\"approved\", source=\"approvals\",\n                metadata={\"approval_id\": approval_id,\n                          \"policy\": policy[\"name\"],\n                          \"session_id\": session_id,\n                          \"command\": cmd_preview})\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n        result = {\"decision\": \"approved\", \"policy\": policy[\"name\"],\n                  \"killed\": False, \"approval_id\": approval_id, \"auto\": True}\n        with _in_flight_lock:\n            _in_flight[key] = result\n        return result\n\n    if (policy.get(\"action\") or \"\") == \"monitor\":\n        # Dry-run mode: record what WOULD have paused so the audit feed shows\n        # it, but never block the agent, never round-trip the cloud, never\n        # kill. Args may be ``input`` /\n    # ``arguments`` / ``args`` depending on the adapter.\n    if not out and isinstance(data.get(\"tool_calls\"), list):\n        if data.get(\"role\") in (None, \"assistant\"):\n            for blk in data[\"tool_calls\"]:\n                if not isinstance(blk, dict):\n                    continue\n                name = _blk_name(blk, data.get(\"tool_name\"))\n                if not name:\n                    continue\n                out.append((\n                    str(blk.get(\"id\") or \"\"),\n                    str(name),\n                    _blk_args(blk),\n                ))\n    # Case E: OpenClaw v3 assistant turns — ``event_type='model.completed'``\n    # with ``data.toolMetas = [{id, name, input}]`` (sync._parse_v3_event).\n    # This is the CURRENT on-disk OpenClaw shape; without this branch the\n    # watcher only ever saw the legacy ``message.content[]`` layout.\n    if not out and isinstance(data.get(\"toolMetas\"), list):\n        for blk in data[\"toolMetas\"]:\n            if not isinstance(blk, dict) or not blk.get(\"name\"):\n                continue\n            out.append((\n                str(blk.get(\"id\") or \"\"),\n                str(blk.get(\"name\")),\n                _norm_args(blk.get(\"input\")),\n            ))\n    # Case F: NemoClaw toolkit rows — ``event_type='tool.call'`` with a\n    # flat ``data = {name, input}``.\n    if not out and str(row.get(\"event_type\") or \"\") == \"tool.call\" \\\n            and data.get(\"name\"):\n        out.append((\n            str(data.get(\"id\") or \"\"),\n            str(data.get(\"name\")),\n            _norm_args(data.get(\"input\") or data.get(\"args\")),\n        ))\n    return out\n\n\ndef _query_new_events(created_after: int, after_id: Optional[str],\n                      limit: int) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Fetch candidate event rows from the local store by INGEST order.\n\n    One indexed keyset query covers all of ``_TOOL_EVENT_TYPES`` (the\n    conceptual \"assistant turn\" lands under ``\"message\"`` / ``\"assistant\"``\n    / one ``\"tool_call\"`` row per invocation depending on the adapter).\n    Rows come back oldest-ingested first with their ``created_at`` stamp.\n    \"\"\"\n    from clawmetry import local_store\n    try:\n        store = local_store.get_store(read_only=True)\n    except Exception as e:\n        # Daemon may have closed the store, or DuckDB optional dep missing\n        # in a pure-OSS install. Either way the watcher should no-op rather\n        # than crash the loop.\n        log.debug(f\"approvals: local_store unavailable ({e})\")\n        return []\n    try:\n        return store.query_events_by_ingest(\n            created_after=created_after, after_id=after_id,\n            event_types=_TOOL_EVENT_TYPES, limit=limit)\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.debug(f\"approvals: query_events_by_ingest failed: {e}\")\n        return []\n\n\ndef watch_iteration(api_key: str, node_id: str,\n                    policies: Optional[list[dict]] = None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"One pass over the unified event store, in INGEST order. Returns the\n    count of toolCalls dispatched to ``process_tool_call`` (each in its own\n    thread).\n\n    The cursor is ``events.created_at`` (insert stamp), NOT the event's own\n    ``ts`` — a family session ingested minutes after its events' timestamps\n    is still evaluated (the 2026-07-02 watermark race). Each iteration\n    re-scans a bounded lookback window behind the watermark (indexed, never\n    a full-table scan) to absorb stamp-vs-commit skew; ``seen_recent_ids``\n    guarantees each row is dispatched exactly once across polls AND daemon\n    restarts (it is persisted with the watermark). ``process_tool_call``'s\n    ``_in_flight`` map dedups at the (session, tool_call_id) level as the\n    final belt-and-braces, so an already-decided approval is never re-fired.\n    \"\"\"\n    if policies is None:\n        policies = load_policies()\n    if not policies:\n        return 0\n\n    # Lazy-prime the watermark from disk on first iteration. Subsequent\n    # iterations use the in-memory copy.\n    with _state_lock:\n        if _state[\"last_ingest_ms\"] is None:\n            persisted_ms, persisted_ids = _read_persisted_watermark()\n            # First-ever start (or upgrade from the legacy ts watermark):\n            # anchor to \"now\" so we don't replay the entire event history.\n            # The lookback window below still covers anything ingested in\n            # the last minute (e.g. during a daemon restart).\n            if persisted_ms is None:\n                persisted_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)\n                _persist_watermark(persisted_ms, {})\n            _state[\"last_ingest_ms\"] = persisted_ms\n            _state[\"seen_recent_ids\"] = persisted_ids\n        watermark = int(_state[\"last_ingest_ms\"])\n        seen: dict = dict(_state[\"seen_recent_ids\"])\n        resume_cursor = _state.get(\"resume_cursor\")\n\n    processed = 0\n    max_ingest = watermark\n    saw_rows = False\n    # If the previous iteration hit the page cap, resume from where it stopped\n    # so we advance past row 2,000 instead of rescanning the same first 2,000\n    # rows forever (see #3558).  Otherwise start from the lookback window.\n    if resume_cursor is not None:\n        cursor_ca, cursor_id = resume_cursor\n    else:\n        cursor_ca = max(0, watermark - _INGEST_LOOKBACK_MS)\n        cursor_id = None\n    hit_page_cap = False\n    for _page in range(_MAX_PAGES_PER_ITERATION):\n        # ``limit=500`` per page matches the PRD spec; the page cap bounds\n        # one iteration's work (the next 2 s poll picks up the rest).\n        rows = _query_new_events(created_after=cursor_ca, after_id=cursor_id,\n                                 limit=500)\n        if not rows:\n            break\n        saw_rows = True\n        for row in rows:\n            eid = str(row.get(\"id\") or \"\")\n            ca = row.get(\"created_at\")\n            ca = int(ca) if isinstance(ca, (int, float)) else watermark\n            if ca > max_ingest:\n                max_ingest = ca\n            # Exactly-once inside the lookback window: skip rows already\n            # dispatched on a previous poll (or before a daemon restart —\n            # the map is persisted alongside the watermark).\n            if eid and eid in seen:\n                continue\n            # Mark every examined row (even without toolCall blocks) so the\n            # window re-scan never re-extracts it.\n            if eid:\n                seen[eid] = ca\n            sid = row.get(\"session_id\") or \"\"\n            # Runtimes whose tool calls are pre-execution gated by an\n            # installed hook (hooks_claude_code) are skipped here: the hook\n            # already paused/denied the call BEFORE it ran, so the reactive\n            # detect-and-kill path firing seconds later would double-punish\n            # (phone-denied one call → watcher kills the whole session).\n            # Row is already in `seen`, so the watermark still advances.\n            if _hook_covered_runtimes() and \\\n                    _session_runtime(sid) in _hook_covered_runtimes():\n                continue\n            for tool_call_id, tool_name, args in _extract_tool_blocks(row):\n                if not tool_name:\n                    # No tool name → no policy can match. Skip rather than\n                    # bother process_tool_call.\n                    continue\n                # Run in a background thread so a long approval timeout\n                # doesn't stall the watcher loop.\n                t = threading.Thread(\n                    target=process_tool_call,\n                    args=(api_key, node_id, sid, tool_call_id, tool_name,\n                          args if isinstance(args, dict) else {}, policies),\n                    daemon=True,\n                )\n                t.start()\n                processed += 1\n        if len(rows) < 500:\n            break\n        # Strict keyset continuation from the last row — pages always make\n        # progress even when hundreds of rows share one millisecond stamp\n        # (a single flush batch does).\n        last = rows[-1]\n        last_ca = last.get(\"created_at\")\n        cursor_ca = int(last_ca) if isinstance(last_ca, (int, float)) else cursor_ca\n        cursor_id = str(last.get(\"id\") or \"\")\n    else:\n        # All pages exhausted without a short final page: save the keyset\n        # cursor so the next iteration resumes here instead of restarting\n        # from the lookback window (#3558 page-cap starvation fix).\n        hit_page_cap = True\n\n    if not saw_rows:\n        # Nothing to scan.  Clear any stale resume cursor so the next\n        # iteration doesn't try to pick up mid-way through an empty window.\n        if resume_cursor is not None:\n            with _state_lock:\n                _state[\"resume_cursor\"] = None\n        return 0\n\n    # Advance the watermark, prune the dedup map to the new lookback window\n    # (older rows can never be re-fetched), and persist. Cheap (single small\n    # JSON file); a daemon crash mid-poll loses at most this iteration's\n    # rows, which the persisted map + ``_in_flight`` absorb on replay.\n    cutoff = max_ingest - _INGEST_LOOKBACK_MS\n    seen = {i: c for i, c in seen.items() if c >= cutoff}\n    if len(seen) > _SEEN_IDS_MEM_CAP:\n        seen = dict(sorted(seen.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1],\n                           reverse=True)[:_SEEN_IDS_MEM_CAP])\n    with _state_lock:\n        _state[\"last_ingest_ms\"] = max_ingest\n        _state[\"seen_recent_ids\"] = seen\n        _state[\"resume_cursor\"] = (cursor_ca, cursor_id) if hit_page_cap else None\n        snapshot_ms = int(_state[\"last_ingest_ms\"])\n        snapshot_ids = dict(_state[\"seen_recent_ids\"])\n    _persist_watermark(snapshot_ms, snapshot_ids)\n\n    return processed\n\n\n# ── OpenClaw native exec-approval gate (2026-07-08) ─────────────────────────\n# ClawMetry's own watcher is REACTIVE: it sees a tool_call only after the\n# transcript records it, so a destructive `rm -rf` on an OpenClaw agent has\n# already run by the time a policy could match (confirmed live 2026-07-08:\n# rm -rf executed, dir gone, no approval fired — OpenClaw never emitted a\n# matchable tool_call event either). The real fix is OpenClaw's OWN\n# pre-execution gate: `openclaw exec-policy preset cautious` sets\n# security=allowlist / ask=on-miss / askFallback=deny, so a non-allowlisted\n# exec PAUSES before running and is denied if unanswered.\n#\n# We drive it from the daemon (not a cloud→host call): the daemon already\n# runs inside the OpenClaw box and already fetches the cloud policies every\n# 2s. When an enabled require-approval policy that covers exec is present we\n# apply `cautious`; when none are, we restore `yolo` — but only when WE were\n# the one who changed it (tracked in a small state file), so we never clobber\n# a posture the operator set by hand. Best-effort; never raises into the loop.\n_EXEC_POLICY_STATE = Path.home() / \".clawmetry\" / \"exec_policy_applied\"\n# Backoff between FAILED preset applies. Live-hit 2026-07-10 (agent-builder\n# shared-cpu-1x box): `openclaw` is a wrapper whose node child can outlive\n# the 60 s timeout on a busy 1-core host; subprocess.run's kill reaped only\n# the wrapper, the ~200 MB node grandchild survived as an orphan, and the\n# watcher retried every ~62 s forever (the state file is only written on\n# success) — one orphan per minute until the VM OOM/throttle-wedged. The\n# process-group kill in _apply_openclaw_exec_preset stops the leak; this\n# backoff stops the hot retry so a host that can't apply the preset degrades\n# to an occasional attempt instead of a permanent CPU tax.\n_EXEC_POLICY_APPLY_TIMEOUT_S = 60\n_EXEC_POLICY_BACKOFF_BASE_S = 300      # first retry 5 min after a failure\n_EXEC_POLICY_BACKOFF_MAX_S = 3600     # never back off longer than an hour\n_EXEC_POLICY_BACKOFF = {\"fails\": 0, \"until\": 0.0}\n# The state file only records what WE last applied. OpenClaw's posture can\n# be changed underneath it (CVE-2026-25253 / ATLAS AML.CS0050 S06 flips\n# `exec.approvals.set {\"ask\": \"off\"}` through the gateway API), so while a\n# policy wants the gate we re-read OpenClaw's EFFECTIVE posture on this\n# interval and put `cautious` back if it is no longer gated\n# (vivekchand/clawmetry-pro#259). One `openclaw exec-policy show` per\n# minute, and only on hosts where a require-approval exec policy is active.\n_EXEC_POSTURE_CHECK_INTERVAL_S = 60\n_EXEC_POSTURE_CHECK = {\"at\": 0.0}\n# State-file value for \"a policy wants the gate and OpenClaw was already at\n# least as strict when we looked\" (e.g. a hand-set deny-all). We leave that\n# posture alone and, unlike \"cautious\", never relax it to yolo later.\n_EXEC_POLICY_HELD = \"held\"\n\n# Native approvals are live Gateway state. Keep the CLI poll bounded and\n# cache the result so the kick-driven policy watcher does not create a\n# request storm on machines with a slow Node wrapper.\n#\n# The watcher thread starts on EVERY daemon, so whatever this interval is,\n# it is a permanent background cost on every user's machine: one `openclaw`\n# process (a node wrapper) per tick, forever, whether or not anyone ever\n# opens the Approvals tab. 10 s is the cheapest interval that costs a human\n# nothing — these prompts are read and decided by a person, so seconds of\n# discovery latency are imperceptible, while 3 s would spawn 20 node\n# processes a minute against a perfectly healthy gateway.\n_NATIVE_APPROVAL_POLL_INTERVAL_S = 10.0\n_NATIVE_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_S = 30\n# The watcher is kicked on every tool_call, so \"gateway down\" would otherwise\n# mean one `openclaw` (node) spawn every 3 s, forever. Same reasoning as\n# _EXEC_POLICY_BACKOFF above, shorter ceiling: an unreachable gateway has no\n# pending approvals to show, so waiting is free, but a transient blip should\n# recover in seconds rather than minutes.\n_NATIVE_APPROVAL_BACKOFF_BASE_S = 30\n_NATIVE_APPROVAL_BACKOFF_MAX_S = 300\n_NATIVE_APPROVAL_BACKOFF = {\"fails\": 0, \"until\": 0.0}\n_native_approval_poll_at = 0.0\n_native_approval_poll_lock = threading.Lock()\n_native_approval_poll_thread: Optional[threading.Thread] = None\n_native_approval_poll_result: Optional[tuple[bool, dict | list | None, str]] = None\n\n\ndef _openclaw_env_and_bin():\n    \"\"\"Resolve the `openclaw` binary with an augmented PATH (the daemon runs\n    under a minimal launchd/systemd PATH where node-shim CLIs aren't found —\n    same gotcha cli.py handles). Returns (bin_path, env) or (None, env).\"\"\"\n    import shutil\n    extra = [\"/usr/local/bin\", \"/opt/homebrew/bin\",\n             os.path.expanduser(\"~/.local/bin\"), \"/usr/bin\"]\n    env = os.environ.copy()\n    env[\"PATH\"] = \":\".join(extra) + \":\" + env.get(\"PATH\", \"\")\n    return shutil.which(\"openclaw\", path=env[\"PATH\"]), env\n\n\ndef _native_approvals_enabled() -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether to poll OpenClaw for native approvals on this node at all.\n\n    Off by env switch, and skipped outright when there is no `openclaw`\n    here — most nodes run some other runtime, and resolving the binary\n    costs a few stat calls where spawning the CLI to find out costs a node\n    process every tick.\"\"\"\n    if os.environ.get(\"CLAWMETRY_NATIVE_APPROVALS\", \"1\").strip().lower() in (\n            \"0\", \"false\", \"no\", \"off\"):\n        return False\n    ocbin, _ = _openclaw_env_and_bin()\n    return bool(ocbin)\n\n\ndef _run_openclaw_approval_command(args: list[str]) -> tuple[bool, dict | list | None, str]:\n    \"\"\"Run a native approval CLI command without letting it escape the watcher.\n\n    Runs in its own process group and kills the whole GROUP on timeout, for\n    the reason _apply_openclaw_exec_preset does: `openclaw` is a wrapper\n    whose node child survives the wrapper's death as a CPU/RAM-burning\n    orphan (live-hit 2026-07-10). This path polls every few seconds rather\n    than once a minute, so leaking one orphan per timeout is not survivable.\n    \"\"\"\n    import signal\n    import subprocess\n\n    ocbin, env = _openclaw_env_and_bin()\n    if not ocbin:\n        return False, None, \"openclaw binary not found\"\n    try:\n        p = subprocess.Popen([ocbin, *args],\n                             stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,\n                             text=True, env=env, start_new_session=True)\n        try:\n            out, err = p.communicate(timeout=_NATIVE_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_S)\n        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:\n            try:\n                os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL)  # pgid == pid (new session)\n            except Exception:\n                p.kill()\n            try:\n                p.wait(timeout=10)\n            except Exception:\n                pass\n            return False, None, \"openclaw command timed out\"\n    except Exception as exc:\n        return False, None, str(exc)\n    if p.returncode != 0:\n        return False, None, (err or out or \"command failed\")[-500:]\n    if \"--json\" not in args:\n        return True, None, \"\"\n    try:\n        return True, json.loads(out or \"{}\"), \"\"\n    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:\n        return False, None, f\"invalid JSON: {exc}\"\n\n\ndef _native_approval_cli_worker() -> None:\n    global _native_approval_poll_result\n    result = _run_openclaw_approval_command(\n        [\"approvals\", \"pending\", \"--json\"]\n    )\n    with _native_approval_poll_lock:\n        _native_approval_poll_result = result\n\n\ndef poll_openclaw_approvals() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Import OpenClaw's live pending approvals into the local queue.\n\n    Reads the contract `openclaw approvals pending --json` documents: a\n    top-level ``approvals`` list of normalized entries shaped\n    ``{id, kind, agentId, sessionKey, createdAtMs, expiresAtMs, summary}``\n    (docs/cli/approvals.md, `readPendingApprovalEntry` in the CLI bundle).\n\n    Native approvals are deliberately marked in ``args`` so the dashboard's\n    existing decision endpoint can route them back to OpenClaw. A CLI failure\n    is observational only and never blocks the watcher.\n    \"\"\"\n    global _native_approval_poll_at, _native_approval_poll_thread\n    global _native_approval_poll_result\n    now = time.time()\n    with _native_approval_poll_lock:\n        if (_native_approval_poll_thread is not None\n                and _native_approval_poll_thread.is_alive()):\n            return 0\n        result = _native_approval_poll_result\n        _native_approval_poll_result = None\n        if _native_approval_poll_thread is not None:\n            _native_approval_poll_thread = None\n        if result is None:\n            # Nothing to consume. Start the next poll if the interval has\n            # elapsed and we are not backing off a failing gateway; either\n            # way this iteration has no snapshot to reconcile against.\n            if (now - _native_approval_poll_at >= _NATIVE_APPROVAL_POLL_INTERVAL_S\n                    and now >= _NATIVE_APPROVAL_BACKOFF[\"until\"]\n                    and _native_approvals_enabled()):\n                _native_approval_poll_at = now\n                _native_approval_poll_thread = threading.Thread(\n                    target=_native_approval_cli_worker,\n                    name=\"clawmetry-openclaw-approvals\",\n                    daemon=True,\n                )\n                _native_approval_poll_thread.start()\n            # The watcher is kick-driven (every tool_call), so it re-enters\n            # well inside the poll interval — returning here instead of\n            # falling through is what keeps that from unpacking None.\n            return 0\n    ok, payload, error = result\n    if not ok:\n        _native_approval_backoff_note(error)\n        return 0\n    entries = payload.get(\"approvals\", []) if isinstance(payload, dict) else payload\n    if not isinstance(entries, list):\n        log.warning(\"openclaw approvals pending returned no approvals list\")\n        return 0\n    _NATIVE_APPROVAL_BACKOFF[\"fails\"] = 0\n    _NATIVE_APPROVAL_BACKOFF[\"until\"] = 0.0\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store\n        store = local_store.get_store()\n    except Exception as exc:\n        log.debug(\"openclaw native approval store unavailable: %s\", exc)\n        return 0\n\n    rows_by_id = {row.get(\"id\"): row\n                  for row in store.query_approvals(limit=1000)}\n    # The stale sweep asks for pending rows specifically rather than\n    # filtering the window above: only a pending row can go stale, and on a\n    # node with a long decision history the 1000 most recent rows can be\n    # entirely resolved ones.\n    pending_rows = store.query_approvals(status=\"pending\", limit=1000)\n    pending_ids = set()\n    imported = 0\n    for entry in entries:\n        if not isinstance(entry, dict):\n            continue\n        approval_id = str(entry.get(\"rawId\") or entry.get(\"id\") or \"\").strip()\n        if not approval_id:\n            continue\n        pending_ids.add(approval_id)\n        existing = rows_by_id.get(approval_id)\n        if existing is not None and existing.get(\"status\") != \"pending\":\n            # are accepted only as a forward-compatible fallback.\n        session_id = (entry.get(\"sessionKey\") or entry.get(\"sessionId\")\n                      or entry.get(\"session_id\"))\n        summary = str(entry.get(\"summary\") or entry.get(\"tool\")\n                      or \"OpenClaw approval\")\n        store.ingest_approval({\n            \"id\": approval_id,\n            \"requestor_session_id\": f\"openclaw:{session_id}\" if session_id else None,\n            \"action\": summary,\n            \"args\": {\n                \"source\": \"openclaw-native\",\n                \"runtime\": \"openclaw\",\n                # is deciding.\n                \"kind\": \"permission_prompt\",\n                \"tool_name\": str(entry.get(\"kind\") or \"exec\"),\n                \"command\": summary,\n                \"policy\": \"OpenClaw native approval\",\n                \"agent_id\": entry.get(\"agentId\"),\n                \"expires_at_ms\": entry.get(\"expiresAtMs\"),\n                \"native\": entry,\n            },\n            \"status\": \"pending\",\n            \"created_at\": _native_approval_created_at(entry.get(\"createdAtMs\")),\n        }, preserve_resolved=True)\n        imported += 1\n    for row in pending_rows:\n        args = row.get(\"args\") if isinstance(row.get(\"args\"), dict) else {}\n        if (args.get(\"source\") == \"openclaw-native\"\n                and row.get(\"id\") not in pending_ids):\n            store.update_approval_decision(\n                row[\"id\"], \"expired\", \"openclaw-sync\",\n                \"no longer pending in OpenClaw\",\n            )\n    return imported\n\n\ndef _native_approval_created_at(created_ms) -> str:\n    \"\"\"OpenClaw reports epoch milliseconds; the approvals table holds ISO-8601\n    everywhere else (and the UI renders the column verbatim). Convert, and\n    fall back to now for a value the CLI did not give us.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        if created_ms is not None:\n            return time.strftime(\"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\",\n                                 time.gmtime(float(created_ms) / 1000.0))\n    except (TypeError, ValueError, OSError, OverflowError):\n        pass\n    return time.strftime(\"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\", time.gmtime())\n\n\ndef _native_approval_backoff_note(error: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Record one failed poll and widen the retry window. Gateway-down is the\n    ordinary case on a box where OpenClaw is installed but not running.\"\"\"\n    _NATIVE_APPROVAL_BACKOFF[\"fails\"] += 1\n    delay = min(_NATIVE_APPROVAL_BACKOFF_MAX_S,\n                _NATIVE_APPROVAL_BACKOFF_BASE_S\n                * (2 ** (_NATIVE_APPROVAL_BACKOFF[\"fails\"] - 1)))\n    _NATIVE_APPROVAL_BACKOFF[\"until\"] = time.time() + delay\n    log.debug(\"openclaw native approval poll failed (%s); next attempt in %ss\",\n              error, delay)\n\n\ndef resolve_openclaw_approval(approval_id: str, decision: str,\n                              reason: str | None = None,\n                              remember: str | None = None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Resolve one native OpenClaw approval through its documented CLI.\n\n    ``remember=\"always\"`` maps an \"Approve & always allow\" click onto\n    OpenClaw's own ``allow-always``. Without it the decision goes back as\n    ``allow-once`` and OpenClaw asks again on the next identical command,\n    while ClawMetry's side shows a remembered rule — a control that looks\n    like it worked and did not. Tiny blobs (session titles) are never compressed:\n# gzip grows them.\n_SERVER_CAPS: dict = {}\nBLOB_GZIP_MIN_BYTES = 4096\n\n\ndef _record_server_caps(resp: dict) -> None:\n    caps = resp.get(\"caps\") if isinstance(resp, dict) else None\n    if isinstance(caps, dict):\n        _SERVER_CAPS.update(caps)\n\n\ndef blob_gzip_enabled() -> bool:\n    env = str(os.environ.get(\"CLAWMETRY_BLOB_GZIP\", \"\")).strip().lower()\n    if env in (\"1\", \"true\", \"yes\"):\n        return True\n    if env in (\"0\", \"false\", \"no\"):\n        return False\n    return _SERVER_CAPS.get(\"blob_gzip\") is True\n\n\ndef encrypt_payload(data: dict, key_b64: str, compress: bool | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"\n    Encrypt a dict as AES-256-GCM.\n    Returns base64url(nonce || ciphertext) — a single opaque string.\n    Cloud stores this blob and never sees plaintext.\n\n    ``compress`` forces gzip-before-encrypt on or off; ``None`` (the default)\n    follows ``blob_gzip_enabled()``, so every call site gains compression the\n    moment the server advertises it and none of them has to know.\n    \"\"\"\n    cipher = _get_aesgcm(key_b64)\n    nonce = secrets.token_bytes(12)  # 96-bit nonce (GCM standard)\n    plain = json.dumps(data).encode()\n    if compress is None:\n        compress = blob_gzip_enabled()\n    if compress and len(plain) >= BLOB_GZIP_MIN_BYTES:\n        import gzip as _gzip\n        plain = _gzip.compress(plain, compresslevel=6, mtime=0)\n    ct = cipher.encrypt(nonce, plain, None)\n    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(nonce + ct).decode()\n\n\n# ── The no-key rule ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n# Every content-bearing upload goes through this gate.
