Their subscription expiry comes from the\n            # plan, not from the trial they took before they bought.\n            if _trial_deadline_applies:\n                expiry = _trial_end_epoch\n            payload = {\"plan\": tier, \"node_limit\": 1, \"expiry\": expiry}\n            if _trial_used is not None:\n                payload[\"trial_used\"] = _trial_used\n            if _trial_end_epoch is not None:\n                payload[\"trial_end\"] = _trial_end_epoch\n            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_CLOUD_PLAN_CACHE_PATH), exist_ok=True)\n            tmp = _CLOUD_PLAN_CACHE_PATH + \".tmp\"\n            with open(tmp, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n                json.dump(payload, fh)\n            os.replace(tmp, _CLOUD_PLAN_CACHE_PATH)\n        try:\n            from clawmetry import entitlements as _ent\n            _ent.invalidate()\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n    except Exception as exc:\n        log.debug(\"cloud_plan: persist failed: %s\", exc)\n\n\ndef _update_trial_state(resp: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Mirror plan info from a cloud response into the local cache + log\n    a one-line \"upgrade to resume\" message once per UTC day on transition.\"\"\"\n    prev_allowed = _TRIAL_STATE[\"sync_allowed\"]\n    prev_plan = _TRIAL_STATE.get(\"plan\")\n    prev_days = _TRIAL_STATE.get(\"trial_days_left\")\n    new_allowed = bool(resp.get(\"sync_allowed\", True))\n    _TRIAL_STATE[\"sync_allowed\"] = new_allowed\n    if \"plan\" in resp:\n        _TRIAL_STATE[\"plan\"] = resp.get(\"plan\")\n    if \"trial_days_left\" in resp:\n        _TRIAL_STATE[\"trial_days_left\"] = resp.get(\"trial_days_left\")\n    # users.trial_end / users.trial_used, mirrored so the resolver can tell a\n    # burnt trial from a never-trialed install (see _persist_cloud_plan_to_disk).\n    if \"trial_end\" in resp:\n        _TRIAL_STATE[\"trial_end\"] = resp.get(\"trial_end\")\n    if \"trial_used\" in resp:\n        _TRIAL_STATE[\"trial_used\"] = resp.get(\"trial_used\")\n    if resp.get(\"upgrade_url\"):\n        _TRIAL_STATE[\"upgrade_url\"] = resp[\"upgrade_url\"]\n    if resp.get(\"checkout_url\"):\n        _TRIAL_STATE[\"checkout_url\"] = resp[\"checkout_url\"]\n    # Persist the URLs for the dashboard process (paywall \"Continue to\n    # payment\" button); idempotent, so cheap on every beat.\n    _persist_trial_state_to_disk()\n    # Reconcile the on-disk plan cache on EVERY heartbeat (the founder ask:\n    # \"check & start sync at every heartbeat, for which plan it is in\"). The\n    # call is idempotent (a no-op when the cache already matches the live tier),\n    # so this is cheap, but it self-heals a cache that drifted for any reason\n    # (deleted file, a daemon that started while free then the plan upgraded,\n    # etc.) and flips paid runtimes on the moment the plan becomes entitled.\n    if (\n        \"plan\" in resp\n        or \"trial_days_left\" in resp\n        or \"trial_end\" in resp\n        or \"trial_used\" in resp\n    ):\n        _persist_cloud_plan_to_disk(\n            _TRIAL_STATE.get(\"plan\"),\n            _TRIAL_STATE.get(\"trial_days_left\"),\n            trial_end=_TRIAL_STATE.get(\"trial_end\"),\n            trial_used=_TRIAL_STATE.get(\"trial_used\"),\n        )\n    reason = (resp.get(\"reason\") or \"\").strip()\n    today = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\")\n    if not new_allowed and _TRIAL_STATE[\"last_log_day\"] != today:\n        _TRIAL_STATE[\"last_log_day\"] = today\n        if reason == \"intent_pending\":\n            # KiloClaw / similar auto-provisioned flows. The user hasn't\n            # asked to view their dashboard yet, so we heartbeat (so the\n            # cloud knows we're alive) but upload nothing else. The moment\n            # they click \"View Observability\", the heartbeat response\n            # flips and uploads resume — no daemon restart needed.\n            log.info(\n                \"Cloud sync deferred — waiting for the user to open their \"\n                \"dashboard. Heartbeats continue; no sessions / events / \"\n                \"logs / memory will leave this machine until then.\"\n            )\n        else:\n            log.warning(\n                \"⚠ Trial expired (plan=%s). Cloud sync resumed.\",\n                _TRIAL_STATE[\"plan\"],\n            )\n\n    # Trial-end pipeline. Two concerns, both idempotent + best-effort:\n    #   1. We write it to ~/.clawmetry/license.key\n    #      and invalidate the entitlement cache so the dashboard picks it up\n    #      within one 60s cycle — no restart, no re-login.\n    #   2. Fire a \"trial ends in N days\" notification so the cloud can send\n    #      the customer an email + surface a soft banner in the dashboard,\n    #      once per UTC day, only within the operator-configured warning\n    #      window (default 2 days, ``CLAWMETRY_TRIAL_WARN_DAYS``).\n    try:\n        _maybe_install_license_from_heartbeat(resp)\n    except Exception as _le:\n        log.debug(\"license auto-install skipped: %s\", _le)\n    try:\n        _maybe_send_trial_warning(resp)\n    except Exception as _we:\n        log.debug(\"trial warning skipped: %s\", _we)\n\n\n_TRIAL_WARNING_STATE = {\n    \"last_warn_day\": \"\",   # YYYY-MM-DD of the last warning we sent\n}\n\n# Same file routes/trial.py's /api/trial/mark-warned writes ({\"YYYY-MM-DD\":\n# days_left}); sharing it means either writer suppresses the other's re-fire.\n# The in-memory guard alone resets on every daemon restart, and auto-update\n# restarts the daemon on every release (often several per day), so without the\n# disk check each restart re-fired /ingest/trial-warning (2026-08-10 trial-email\n# spam RCA).\n_TRIAL_WARNINGS_PATH = os.path.expanduser(\"~/.clawmetry/trial_warnings.json\")\n\n\ndef _trial_warning_sent_on(day: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when ``day`` (YYYY-MM-DD) is already recorded on disk. Never raises.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        if not os.path.isfile(_TRIAL_WARNINGS_PATH):\n            return False\n        with open(_TRIAL_WARNINGS_PATH, encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n            data = json.load(fh)\n        return isinstance(data, dict) and day in data\n    except Exception:\n        return False\n\n\ndef _record_trial_warning(day: str, days_left: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Persist ``{day: days_left}`` into the warnings file. Never raises.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_TRIAL_WARNINGS_PATH), exist_ok=True)\n        existing = {}\n        if os.path.isfile(_TRIAL_WARNINGS_PATH):\n            try:\n                with open(_TRIAL_WARNINGS_PATH, encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n                    existing = json.load(fh) or {}\n            except Exception:\n                existing = {}\n        if not isinstance(existing, dict):\n            existing = {}\n        existing[day] = days_left\n        tmp = _TRIAL_WARNINGS_PATH + \".tmp\"\n        with open(tmp, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n            json.dump(existing, fh)\n        os.replace(tmp, _TRIAL_WARNINGS_PATH)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        log.debug(\"trial-warning persist failed: %s\", exc)\n\n\ndef _maybe_install_license_from_heartbeat(resp: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Persist a signed license key the cloud attached to this heartbeat.\n\n    Contract with the cloud (documented in\n    ``docs/TRIAL_ENFORCEMENT.md``): a heartbeat response for an account that\n    completed checkout carries a ``license_key`` string holding the raw\n    ``header.payload.signature`` Ed25519 token. We treat it as\n    authoritative — write it atomically to ``~/.clawmetry/license.key``,\n    invalidate the entitlements cache, and log once.\n\n    Idempotent: skips writing when the file already matches. Never raises.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(resp, dict):\n        return\n    key = resp.get(\"license_key\")\n    if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():\n        return\n    key = key.strip()\n    lic_path = os.path.expanduser(\"~/.clawmetry/license.key\")\n    try:\n        existing = \"\"\n        if os.path.isfile(lic_path):\n            try:\n                with open(lic_path, encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n                    existing = fh.read().strip()\n            except Exception:\n                existing = \"\"\n        if existing == key:\n            return\n        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(lic_path), exist_ok=True)\n        tmp = lic_path + \".tmp\"\n        with open(tmp, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n            fh.write(key)\n        os.replace(tmp, lic_path)\n        try:\n            os.chmod(lic_path, 0o600)\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n        log.info(\n            \"✓ ClawMetry license installed from cloud — dashboard will unlock \"\n            \"on the next resolver refresh (up to 60s).\"\n        )\n        try:\n            from clawmetry import entitlements as _ent\n            _ent.invalidate()\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n    except Exception as exc:\n        log.warning(\"license auto-install failed: %s\", exc)\n\n\ndef _maybe_send_trial_warning(resp: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Ping the cloud once per day when the trial is inside its warning window.\n\n    The heartbeat response carries ``trial_days_left``; we compare it against\n    the operator-configured window (``CLAWMETRY_TRIAL_WARN_DAYS``, default 2\n    — see :mod:`clawmetry.trial_enforcement`) and, when we're inside it,\n    fire ``POST /ingest/trial-warning`` on the cloud so it can send the\n    customer a \"your trial ends in N days — click to upgrade\" email.\n\n    Rate-limited: at most one warning per UTC day, guarded both in memory\n    (fast path for a daemon that beats every 30s) and on disk\n    (``~/.clawmetry/trial_warnings.json``) so an auto-update restart — which\n    happens on every release, often several times a day — doesn't reset the\n    guard and re-fire the POST. The cloud is authoritative on email\n    throttling itself.\n\n    Never raises.\"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(resp, dict):\n        return\n    days = resp.get(\"trial_days_left\")\n    try:\n        days_i = int(days)\n    except Exception:\n        return\n    if days_i < 0:\n        return\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import trial_enforcement as _te\n        window = _te.warning_window_days()\n    except Exception:\n        window = 2\n    if days_i > window:\n        return\n    today = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\")\n    if _TRIAL_WARNING_STATE[\"last_warn_day\"] == today:\n        return\n    if _trial_warning_sent_on(today):\n        # A previous daemon process (pre-restart) already warned today.\n        _TRIAL_WARNING_STATE[\"last_warn_day\"] = today\n        return\n    _TRIAL_WARNING_STATE[\"last_warn_day\"] = today\n    _record_trial_warning(today, days_i)\n    try:\n        cfg = load_config() or {}\n        api_key = cfg.get(\"api_key\")\n        if not api_key:\n            log.debug(\"trial-warning skipped: no cloud api_key on this node\")\n            return\n        _post(\"/ingest/trial-warning\", {\n            \"days_left\": days_i,\n            \"plan\": _TRIAL_STATE.get(\"plan\"),\n        }, api_key, timeout=6)\n        log.info(\n            \"trial-ending notice queued (days_left=%d) — cloud will email \"\n            \"the account owner.\", days_i,\n        )\n    except Exception as exc:\n        # Keep the last_warn_day set even on failure so we don't retry every\n        # 30s; the next daily beat will try again.\n        log.debug(\"trial-warning POST failed (will retry tomorrow): %s\", exc)\n\n\ndef _sync_allowed() -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Gate for large blob uploads. The\n    cloud's ``sync_allowed=False`` reflects the CLOUD ACCOUNT's plan, but\n    this flag also gates LOCAL DuckDB ingest (sync_family_runtimes and\n    every other sync_* function), so a node whose old cloud account said\n    ``trial_expired`` refused to ingest Claude Code into its OWN local\n    store even while holding a freshly activated local trial key — the\n    entitlement resolver said Trial, the daemon said paused, and the\n    Activity tab stayed empty (founder live-hit 2026-07-28). The signed\n    key IS the entitlement (Ed25519, verified offline, license-first in\n    the resolution order); the cloud remains free to refuse uploads\n    server-side for its own capacity reasons.\n    \"\"\"\n    if _TRIAL_STATE.get(\"sync_allowed\", True):\n        return True\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import entitlements as _ent\n\n        ent = _ent.get_entitlement()\n        # is_paid / expired are PROPERTIES, not methods. Calling them raised\n        # TypeError, the except swallowed it, and the override silently never\n        # fired — the exact bug class the tests missed because their doubles\n        # used callables (fixed: tests now build REAL Entitlement objects).\n        if ent.source == \"license\" and ent.is_paid and not ent.expired:\n            return True\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    return False\n\n\ndef get_machine_id() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Generate a stable hardware fingerprint for this machine.\"\"\"\n    import hashlib, platform\n\n    mid = \"\"\n    # macOS: IOPlatformUUID (stable across reboots/reinstalls)\n    if platform.system() == \"Darwin\":\n        try:\n            import subprocess\n\n            out = subprocess.check_output(\n                [\"ioreg\", \"-rd1\", \"-c\", \"IOPlatformExpertDevice\"],\n                timeout=5,\n                stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n            ).decode()\n            for line in out.splitlines():\n                if \"IOPlatformUUID\" in line:\n                    mid = line.split('\"')[-2]\n                    break\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n    # Fallback: MAC address (less stable but better than nothing)\n    if not mid:\n        import uuid as _uuid_mod\n\n        mid = str(_uuid_mod.getnode())\n    return hashlib.sha256(mid.encode()).hexdigest()[:32]\n\n\ndef validate_key(\n    api_key: str, hostname: str = \"\", existing_node_id: str = \"\", **kwargs\n) -> dict:\n    payload = {\"api_key\": api_key}\n    if hostname:\n        payload[\"hostname\"] = hostname\n    if existing_node_id:\n        payload[\"existing_node_id\"] = existing_node_id\n    payload[\"machine_id\"] = get_machine_id()\n    return _post(\"/auth\", payload, api_key)\n\n\n# ── Path detection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n\ndef _find_openclaw_dirs(root, max_depth=4):\n    \"\"\"Search a directory tree for OpenClaw sessions and workspace dirs.\"\"\"\n    sessions_dir = None\n    workspace_dir = None\n    try:\n        for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):\n            depth = dirpath.replace(root, \"\").count(os.sep)\n            if depth > max_depth:\n                dirnames.clear()\n                continue\n            # Skip noisy dirs\n            base = os.path.basename(dirpath)\n            if base in (\"node_modules\", \".git\", \"__pycache__\", \"venv\", \".venv\"):\n                dirnames.clear()\n                continue\n            if dirpath.endswith(\n                os.sep + \"agents\" + os.sep + \"main\" + os.sep + \"sessions\"\n            ) or dirpath.endswith(\"/agents/main/sessions\"):\n                if not sessions_dir:\n                    sessions_dir = dirpath\n                    log.info(f\"  Found sessions: {dirpath}\")\n            if os.path.basename(dirpath) == \"workspace\" and os.path.isfile(\n                os.path.join(dirpath, \"AGENTS.md\")\n            ):\n                if not workspace_dir:\n                    workspace_dir = dirpath\n                    log.info(f\"  Found workspace: {dirpath}\")\n            if sessions_dir and workspace_dir:\n                break\n    except PermissionError:\n        pass\n    return sessions_dir, workspace_dir\n\n\ndef _is_running_in_container() -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Detect whether ClawMetry itself is running inside a Docker/OpenShell container.\"\"\"\n    # Check for /.dockerenv (present in Docker containers)\n    if os.path.exists(\"/.dockerenv\"):\n        return True\n    # Check cgroup for container indicators\n    try:\n        with open(\"/proc/1/cgroup\", \"r\") as f:\n            cgroup = f.read()\n        if any(\n            k in cgroup\n            for k in (\"docker\", \"kubepods\", \"containerd\", \"lxc\", \"opencontainer\")\n        ):\n            return True\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    return False\n\n\ndef _read_nemoclaw_sandbox_routing() -> list:\n    \"\"\"Read ``~/.nemoclaw/sandboxes.json`` and derive per-sandbox model routing.\n\n    Gap #2684. The NemoClaw registry persists ``{sandboxes: {<name>: entry},\n    defaultSandbox}`` (harness/nemoclaw/src/lib/state/registry.ts); each entry\n    carries the raw ``provider`` + ``model``. Never raises — returns [] on missing/old/malformed registry files\n    so the daemon never crashes.\n    \"\"\"\n    import json as _j\n\n    home = os.environ.get(\"HOME\") or os.path.expanduser(\"~\")\n    reg = os.path.join(home, \".nemoclaw\", \"sandboxes.json\")\n    out: list = []\n    try:\n        with open(reg, \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n            data = _j.load(fh)\n    except Exception:\n        return out\n    if not isinstance(data, dict):\n        return out\n    default_sb = data.get(\"defaultSandbox\")\n    sandboxes = data.get(\"sandboxes\")\n    if not isinstance(sandboxes, dict):\n        return out\n    MANAGED = \"inference\"\n    INFERENCE_ROUTE_URL = \"https://inference.local/v1\"\n    for name, entry in sandboxes.items():\n        try:\n            if not isinstance(entry, dict):\n                continue\n            provider = entry.get(\"provider\") or \"\"\n            model = entry.get(\"model\") or \"\"\n            # inferenceApi defaults to \"openai-completions\" unless the sandbox\n            # pins preferredInferenceApi (harness config.ts:188).\n            api = entry.get(\"preferredInferenceApi\") or \"openai-completions\"\n            base_url = INFERENCE_ROUTE_URL\n            # Derive providerKey/primaryModelRef per the harness switch\n            # (getSandboxInferenceConfig, nemoclaw/src/lib/inference/config.ts).\n            # Default = managed \"inference\" provider for any unknown/cloud route.\n            if provider == \"openai-api\":\n                provider_key = \"openai\"\n                primary = f\"openai/{model}\" if model else \"\"\n            elif provider == \"anthropic-prod\" or (\n                provider == \"compatible-anthropic-endpoint\"\n                and api != \"openai-completions\"\n            ):\n                # Real anthropic route only when NOT the openai-completions\n                # default; a compatible-anthropic-endpoint with the default api\n                # is served by the MANAGED provider (config.ts:196-203).\n                provider_key = \"anthropic\"\n                primary = f\"anthropic/{model}\" if model else \"\"\n                base_url = \"https://inference.local\"\n                api = \"anthropic-messages\"\n            elif provider in (\"minimax\", \"minimax-api\"):\n                provider_key = \"minimax\"\n                primary = f\"minimax/{model}\" if model else \"\"\n                base_url = os.environ.get(\"MINIMAX_BASE_URL\", \"\").strip() or \"https://api.minimax.chat/v1\"\n            else:\n                # Includes compatible-anthropic-endpoint + openai-completions\n                # (the common default) → managed \"inference\" provider.\n                provider_key = MANAGED\n                primary = f\"{MANAGED}/{model}\" if model else \"\"\n            out.append({\n                \"sandbox\": name,\n                \"isDefault\": bool(default_sb and name == default_sb),\n                \"provider\": provider,\n                \"model\": model,\n                \"providerKey\": provider_key,\n                \"primaryModelRef\": primary,\n                \"inferenceBaseUrl\": base_url,\n                \"inferenceApi\": api,\n            })\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n    return out\n\n\ndef _detect_nemoclaw() -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Detect NemoClaw (NVIDIA's OpenClaw wrapper) presence on the host.\n\n    Returns a dict with fields:\n      detected (bool), binary (str), version (str),\n      sandbox_name (str), sandbox_status (str), sandbox_type (str),\n      inference_provider (str), inference_model (str),\n      security_sandbox_enabled (bool), security_network_policy (bool)\n    \"\"\"\n    import subprocess, shutil\n\n    result: dict = {\"detected\": False}\n\n    # 1. Check for the nemoclaw binary\n    nemo_bin = shutil.which(\"nemoclaw\")\n    if not nemo_bin:\n        for candidate in [\n            \"/usr/local/bin/nemoclaw\",\n            \"/opt/nemoclaw/bin/nemoclaw\",\n            \"/usr/bin/nemoclaw\",\n        ]:\n            if os.path.isfile(candidate):\n                nemo_bin = candidate\n                break\n\n    if not nemo_bin:\n        # Also accept NEMOCLAW_SANDBOX env as a hint even without binary\n        if not os.environ.get(\"NEMOCLAW_SANDBOX\"):\n            return result\n\n    result[\"detected\"] = True\n    result[\"binary\"] = nemo_bin or \"(env-only)\"\n\n    # 2. Get version\n    if nemo_bin:\n        try:\n            ver = (\n                subprocess.check_output(\n                    [nemo_bin, \"--version\"], stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=5\n                )\n                .decode()\n                .strip()\n            )\n            result[\"version\"] = ver\n        except Exception:\n            result[\"version\"] = \"unknown\"\n\n    # 3. corrupt key?): %s\",\n                    fname, _enc_e,\n                )\n            return\n    if blob is None and not content_egress_permitted(enc_key, \"/ingest/events\"):\n        return\n    try:\n        if blob is not None:\n            _post(\n                \"/ingest/events\",\n                {\"node_id\": node_id, \"encrypted\": True, \"blob\": blob},\n                api_key,\n            )\n    except Exception as _cloud_e:\n        try:\n            _dlq_enqueue_encryption_failure(\n                kind=\"post_failure\",\n                endpoint=\"/ingest/events\",\n                payload=payload,\n                fname=fname,\n                node_id=node_id,\n                subagent_id=subagent_id,\n                error=str(_cloud_e),\n            )\n        except Exception as _dlq_e:\n            log.warning(\n                \"cloud /ingest/events POST failed AND DLQ park failed for %s \"\n                \"(events permanently dropped from cloud): post=%s dlq=%s\",\n                fname, _cloud_e, _dlq_e,\n            )\n        else:\n            log.warning(\n                \"cloud /ingest/events POST failed for %s — parked in sync_dlq \"\n                \"for retry on next tick: %s\",\n                fname, _cloud_e,\n            )\n\n\ndef _extract_cost_tokens_model(obj: dict) -> tuple:\n    \"\"\"Pull (cost_usd, token_count, model) out of a raw OpenClaw transcript event.\n\n    Real OpenClaw events nest these under ``obj[\"message\"][\"usage\"]``:\n\n        {\n          \"type\": \"message\",\n          \"message\": {\n            \"model\": \"claude-opus-4-7\",\n            \"usage\": {\n              \"totalTokens\": 162,\n              \"cost\": {\"total\": 0.00495, ...}\n            }\n          }\n        }\n\n    Older / synthesised events sometimes carry top-level ``cost_usd`` /\n    ``tokens`` / ``model``. We accept either shape so tests, sub-agent\n    adapters, and the real OpenClaw harness all populate the columns\n    (previously the nested shape silently became NULL — see MOAT_E2E_REPORT\n    2026-05-13 root-cause #4).\"\"\"\n    cost_usd = obj.get(\"cost_usd\")\n    if cost_usd is None:\n        cost_usd = obj.get(\"costUsd\")\n    token_count = obj.get(\"token_count\")\n    if token_count is None:\n        token_count = obj.get(\"tokens\")\n    model = obj.get(\"model\")\n\n    msg = obj.get(\"message\")\n    if isinstance(msg, dict):\n        if model is None:\n            model = msg.get(\"model\")\n        usage = msg.get(\"usage\")\n        if isinstance(usage, dict):\n            if token_count is None:\n                tt = usage.get(\"totalTokens\")\n                if tt is None:\n                    tt = usage.get(\"total_tokens\")\n                if tt is not None:\n                    try:\n                        token_count = int(tt)\n                    except (TypeError, ValueError):\n                        token_count = None\n            if cost_usd is None:\n                cost = usage.get(\"cost\")\n                if isinstance(cost, dict):\n                    cv = cost.get(\"total\")\n                    if cv is None:\n                        cv = cost.get(\"total_usd\")\n                else:\n                    cv = cost  # rare: cost itself is a number\n                if cv is not None:\n                    try:\n                        cost_usd = float(cv)\n                    except (TypeError, ValueError):\n                        cost_usd = None\n    else:\n        # Best-effort, never raises.\n    if cost_usd is None and model:\n        u = usage if (isinstance(msg, dict) and isinstance(usage, dict)) else {}\n        if not u and isinstance(obj.get(\"usage\"), dict):\n            u = obj[\"usage\"]\n\n        def _utok(*keys):\n            for _k in keys:\n                _v = u.get(_k)\n                if _v is not None:\n                    try:\n                        return int(_v)\n                    except (TypeError, ValueError):\n                        pass\n            return 0\n\n        _in = _utok(\"input_tokens\", \"inputTokens\", \"prompt_tokens\", \"promptTokens\", \"input\")\n        _out = _utok(\"output_tokens\", \"outputTokens\", \"completion_tokens\", \"completionTokens\", \"output\")\n        _cr = _utok(\"cache_read_input_tokens\", \"cacheReadInputTokens\", \"cache_read_tokens\", \"cacheRead\")\n        _cw = _utok(\"cache_creation_input_tokens\", \"cacheCreationInputTokens\", \"cache_write_tokens\", \"cacheWrite\")\n        if _in or _out or _cr or _cw:\n            try:\n                from clawmetry.providers_pricing import estimate_event_cost_usd\n                _derived = estimate_event_cost_usd(model, _in, _out, _cr, _cw)\n                if _derived and _derived > 0:\n                    cost_usd = _derived\n            except Exception:\n                pass\n\n    return cost_usd, token_count, model\n\n\ndef _extract_channel_message(\n    obj: dict,\n    *,\n    session_id: str,\n) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"Best-effort projection of a transcript event into a\n    ``channel_messages`` row.\n\n    Issue #1088 Phase 4. Returns ``None`` when the event is not a chat\n    message OR carries no recoverable channel signal — the daemon then\n    just records the event in ``events`` and moves on.\n\n    Two recognition paths:\n\n    1. **Inbound** — a ``user``-role message whose text starts with one of\n       the known adapter wrappers (e.g. ``[Telegram Alice id:123]…``,\n       ``[iMessage +14155551234]…``). Per-provider extras\n    (attachments, reactions, message_id) ride along in ``raw_blob`` so\n    we don't widen the schema for adapter-specific fields.\n    \"\"\"\n    import re as _re\n    if not isinstance(obj, dict):\n        return None\n    if obj.get(\"type\") != \"message\":\n        return None\n    msg = obj.get(\"message\")\n    if not isinstance(msg, dict):\n        return None\n    role = msg.get(\"role\")\n    if role not in (\"user\", \"assistant\"):\n        return None\n    content = msg.get(\"content\")\n    text = \"\"\n    if isinstance(content, str):\n        text = content\n    elif isinstance(content, list):\n        for c in content:\n            if isinstance(c, dict) and c.get(\"type\") == \"text\":\n                text = c.get(\"text\", \"\") or \"\"\n                if text:\n                    break\n    if not text:\n        return None\n    # Skip system/heartbeat noise — these aren't user-facing channel msgs.\n    stripped = text.strip()\n    if stripped.startswith(\"System:\") or \"HEARTBEAT\" in stripped:\n        return None\n    ts = obj.get(\"timestamp\") or obj.get(\"ts\") or \"\"\n    if not ts:\n        return None\n    eid = (\n        obj.get(\"id\")\n        or obj.get(\"eventId\")\n        or obj.get(\"messageId\")\n        or f\"{session_id}:{ts}:{role}\"\n    )\n    if role == \"user\":\n        # Recognised inbound formats — the Connector layer tags every\n        # inbound message with one of these prefixes. We try Telegram /\n        # iMessage / WhatsApp / Signal / Discord / Slack first because\n        # those cover ~95% of installed adapters; the rest fall through\n        # to the generic ``[Provider …]`` matcher.\n        m = _re.match(\n            r\"\\[(?P<prov>Telegram|iMessage|WhatsApp|Signal|Discord|Slack|\"\n            r\"IRC|WebChat|GoogleChat|MSTeams|BlueBubbles|Matrix|Mattermost|\"\n            r\"LINE|Nostr|Twitch|Feishu|Zalo|Tlon|SynologyChat|NextcloudTalk)\"\n            r\"\\s+(?P<sender>.+?)\\s+id:(?P<sid>[^\\]]+?)\\]\\s*(?P<body>.*)\",\n            stripped,\n            flags=_re.IGNORECASE | _re.DOTALL,\n        )\n        if not m:\n            return None\n        provider = m.group(\"prov\").lower()\n        sender_name = m.group(\"sender\").strip()\n        chan_id = m.group(\"sid\").strip()\n        body = m.group(\"body\").strip() or stripped\n        return {\n            \"id\":          str(eid),\n            \"agent_id\":    \"main\",\n            \"provider\":    provider,\n            \"channel_id\":  chan_id,\n            \"sender_id\":   chan_id,\n            \"sender_name\": sender_name,\n            \"body\":        body[:4000],\n            \"ts\":          str(ts),\n            \"direction\":   \"in\",\n            \"session_key\": session_id,\n            \"raw_blob\":    None,\n        }\n    # Assistant turn — outbound. Returning None here\n    # keeps this PR's footprint minimal and avoids stamping the wrong\n    # provider on assistant turns from sessions we haven't classified.\n    return None\n\n\n# ── v3 underscore-schema parser (#1135) ───────────────────────────────────────\n#\n# OpenClaw writes TWO different jsonl shapes per session:\n#\n#   1. ``<sid>.trajectory.jsonl`` — runtime debug trace sidecar.\n#      Dot.separated event types (``trace.artifacts``, ``model.completed``,\n#      ``prompt.submitted``, ``session.ended``…) with content under\n#      ``data.*``. Keep this set narrow to\n# avoid mis-routing trajectory events that happen to have a synonym name.\n_V3_KNOWN_TYPES = frozenset({\n    \"session\",\n    \"model_change\",\n    \"thinking_level_change\",\n    \"cwd_change\",\n    \"message\",\n    \"tool_use\",\n    \"tool_use_result\",\n    # cloud workspace conflict — all plausible casing variants (#4148)\n    \"cloud_workspace_conflict\",\n    \"cloudWorkspaceConflict\",\n    \"workspace_conflict\",\n    \"workspaceConflict\",\n})\n\n# Plumbing event types that carry no transcript-visible content. Returning\n# None here is intentional — the dashboard's brain feed and transcript view\n# are noisier, not richer, when these are surfaced.\n_V3_SKIP_TYPES = frozenset({\n    \"thinking_level_change\",\n    \"cwd_change\",\n})\n\n\ndef _is_v3_event(obj: dict) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Sniff a single parsed JSONL event for the v3 underscore schema.\n\n    The first line of a v3 file is always ``{\"type\": \"session\", \"version\": N,\n    ...}`` — that's the strongest signal. For subsequent lines we look for\n    type-name + structural cues that only the v3 shape carries:\n\n    * ``model_change``, ``thinking_level_change``, ``cwd_change``,\n      ``tool_use``, ``tool_use_result`` — these names are NEW in v3 and\n      never appear in trajectory or legacy synthesised events.\n    * ``message`` is overloaded: legacy synthesised events use\n      ``{\"type\":\"message\",\"role\":\"user\",\"text\":\"…\"}`` (top-level fields)\n      while v3 nests under ``{\"type\":\"message\",\"message\":{role,content,…}}``.\n      We require the nested ``message`` dict to disambiguate; without it\n      the line is treated as legacy and falls through to the trajectory\n      parser (which preserves the existing event_type and data).\n    \"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(obj, dict):\n        return False\n    t = obj.get(\"type\")\n    if not isinstance(t, str):\n        return False\n    if t == \"session\" and obj.get(\"version\") is not None:\n        return True\n    if t == \"message\":\n        # Disambiguate v3 (nested message dict) from legacy synthesised\n        # events that ALSO use type=message but with top-level role/text.\n        return isinstance(obj.get(\"message\"), dict)\n    return t in _V3_KNOWN_TYPES\n\n\ndef _v3_content_to_text(content) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Flatten a v3 ``message.content`` (string OR list of typed blocks)\n    into a single plain-text string. Returns [] when there are no tool calls.\"\"\"\n    out: list[dict] = []\n    if not isinstance(content, list):\n        return out\n    for block in content:\n        if not isinstance(block, dict):\n            continue\n        if block.get(\"type\") != \"tool_use\":\n            continue\n        out.append({\n            \"id\": block.get(\"id\"),\n            \"name\": block.get(\"name\") or \"tool\",\n            \"input\": block.get(\"input\") or {},\n        })\n    return out\n\n\ndef _parse_v3_event(\n    obj: dict,\n    session_id: str,\n    node_id: str,\n    agent_type: str = \"openclaw\",\n) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"Map ONE v3 underscore-schema event to a normalised local-store row.\n\n    Returns ``None`` for plumbing events we deliberately skip\n    (``thinking_level_change``, ``cwd_change``) and for anything unrecognised\n    inside the v3 namespace — the caller treats ``None`` as \"drop this row\"\n    rather than re-routing through the trajectory path (the v3 sniff already\n    classified it).\n\n    The output row carries the dot.separated ``event_type`` values and the\n    nested ``data.*`` key paths the trajectory parser produces, so the read\n    side (``_try_local_store_transcript`` / ``_try_local_store_transcript_events``\n    in routes/sessions.py) works unchanged on both shapes.\n    \"\"\"\n    t = obj.get(\"type\")\n    if not isinstance(t, str):\n        return None\n    if t in _V3_SKIP_TYPES:\n        return None\n\n    ts = obj.get(\"timestamp\") or obj.get(\"ts\") or \"\"\n    if not ts:\n        # The local store indexes on ts; without it we cannot place the\n        # event on the timeline. Non-fatal and\n    # non-blocking: a session with no location is a cosmetic gap, never a\n    # reason to lose the batch's events.\n    if seen_cwd or seen_branch:\n        try:\n            store.update_session_location(\n                session_id, agent_type=agent_type,\n                cwd=seen_cwd, git_branch=seen_branch,\n            )\n        except Exception as _e:\n            log.debug(\"session location update skipped (non-fatal): %s\", _e)\n    # Reconstruct OTel-compatible spans from this batch (issue #1010 / Trace 4).\n    # ``agent_type`` rides through so a non-OpenClaw batch on this transcript\n    # shape (NemoClaw sandbox sessions, agent_type='nemoclaw') stamps its REAL\n    # runtime on the spans instead of mislabeling the Agent Graph 'openclaw'.\n    # Non-fatal: span failures never block event ingest.\n    try:\n        from clawmetry.adapters.openclaw import OpenClawAdapter\n        _spans = list(OpenClawAdapter._build_spans_from_events(\n            batch, session_id, agent_type=agent_type\n        ))\n        if _spans:\n            store.ingest_spans_batch(_spans)\n    except Exception as _e:\n        log.debug(\"span reconstruction skipped (non-fatal): %s\", _e)\n    # Replay stream (#4816): the canonical replay_events rows for this\n    # session, re-read from the transcript the batch came from plus the\n    # read-only OpenClaw state database. Order is priority: the first\n# non-empty alias wins.\n_CWD_ALIASES = (\n    \"cwd\", \"workingDir\", \"workingDirectory\", \"working_directory\",\n    \"working_dir\", \"workspace\", \"workspace_path\", \"workspaceRoot\",\n    \"project_path\", \"project_dir\", \"projectRoot\", \"directory\", \"folder\",\n)\n_GIT_BRANCH_ALIASES = (\n    \"git_branch\", \"gitBranch\", \"branch\", \"vcs_branch\", \"scm_branch\",\n)\n\n\ndef _first_alias(row: dict, aliases: tuple) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"First non-empty value among ``aliases`` in ``row``, else None.\n\n    Also looks one level into a ``metadata`` / ``extra`` sub-dict, because\n    several adapters tuck environment details there rather than at the top\n    level. A detached HEAD legitimately\n    reports no branch, so None here is not necessarily a parse failure.\"\"\"\n    return _first_alias(row, _GIT_BRANCH_ALIASES)\n\n\ndef _session_agent_type(row: dict, session_id: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Which runtime a session belongs to, for the ``sessions.agent_type``\n    column.\n\n    This used to be ``row.get(\"agent_type\") or \"openclaw\"``. The family\n    adapters (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) don't set ``agent_type`` — they\n    carry the runtime in ``runtime`` and, authoritatively, in the\n    ``<runtime>:<uuid>`` ``session_id`` prefix that ``local_store`` already\n    keys its event-side runtime split on. The prefix is checked against\n    ``local_store._NON_OPENCLAW_RUNTIME_PREFIXES`` so a genuine OpenClaw\n    session id containing a colon can never be mistaken for a runtime.\n    \"\"\"\n    for key in (\"agent_type\", \"runtime\"):\n        val = row.get(key)\n        if isinstance(val, str) and val.strip():\n            return val.strip()\n    prefix = str(session_id or \"\").split(\":\", 1)[0].strip().lower()\n    if prefix:\n        try:\n            from clawmetry.local_store import _NON_OPENCLAW_RUNTIME_PREFIXES\n            if prefix in _NON_OPENCLAW_RUNTIME_PREFIXES:\n                return prefix\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n    return \"openclaw\"\n\n\ndef _annotate_public_share(rows: list) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Stamp ``shared`` / ``share_created_at`` onto OpenClaw session rows.\n\n    Probes the gateway once per session key (see\n    :mod:`clawmetry.adapters.openclaw_share` for why a list call cannot\n    answer this, and why the share token is never carried). Never raises.\n    \"\"\"\n    if os.environ.get(\"CLAWMETRY_OPENCLAW_SHARE\", \"1\").strip() == \"0\":\n        return\n    if not rows:\n        return\n    keys = [r.get(\"session_key\") for r in rows if r.get(\"session_key\")]\n    if not keys:\n        return\n    from clawmetry.adapters.openclaw_share import fetch_share_state\n\n    state = fetch_share_state(keys)\n    if not state:\n        return\n    for r in rows:\n        fields = state.get(r.get(\"session_key\") or \"\")\n        if fields:\n            r.update(fields)\n\n\ndef _local_ingest_sessions_batch(rows: list, node_id: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Mirror a batch of session rows (the same dicts we push to /ingest/sessions)\n    into the local DuckDB ``sessions`` table. Take the first non-None.\n        cost = s.get(\"cost_usd\")\n        if cost is None:\n            cost = s.get(\"total_cost\") or s.get(\"totalCostUsd\") or 0\n        # Channel/chat_type/subject move into a separate metadata blob —\n        # they're OpenClaw-specific and (per the multi-agent design) will get\n        # promoted into the openclaw_channels extension table later.\n        meta_extras = {\n            k: v for k, v in s.items()\n            if k in (\"channel\", \"chat_type\", \"subject\", \"recent_model\",\n                     \"session_key\", \"end_reason\", \"runtime\", \"thinking_level\",\n                     # #5746 public-share verdict. ``shared`` is a bool, so\n                     # the ``and v`` filter below would drop a stored False —\n                     # which is a real answer (\"we asked; it is not\n                     # published\"), not a missing one. Handled explicitly\n                     # after this comprehension.\n                     \"share_created_at\")\n            and v\n        }\n        # ``shared`` carries meaning when False, so it bypasses the\n        # truthiness filter above. Absent stays absent: a session the daemon\n        # could not probe must not be recorded as \"not shared\" (#5746).\n        if isinstance(s.get(\"shared\"), bool):\n            meta_extras[\"shared\"] = s[\"shared\"]\n        session_rows.append({\n            \"agent_type\": _session_agent_type(s, sid),\n            \"session_id\": sid,\n            \"node_id\": node_id,\n            \"agent_id\": s.get(\"agent_id\") or \"main\",\n            \"title\": s.get(\"subject\") or s.get(\"title\"),\n            \"started_at\": s.get(\"started_at\"),\n            \"last_active_at\": s.get(\"updated_at\") or s.get(\"last_active_at\"),\n            \"ended_at\": s.get(\"ended_at\"),\n            \"status\": s.get(\"status\"),\n            \"total_tokens\": s.get(\"total_tokens\") or 0,\n            \"cost_usd\": cost,\n            \"message_count\": s.get(\"message_count\") or 0,\n            \"metadata\": meta_extras or None,\n            \"cwd\":        _session_cwd(s),\n            \"git_branch\": _session_git_branch(s),\n        })\n    for row in session_rows:\n        q = _openclaw_session_quality(store, row)\n        if q is not None:\n            row[\"metadata\"] = dict(row[\"metadata\"] or {}, quality=q)\n    if session_rows:\n        store.ingest_sessions_batch(session_rows)\n\n\n# sid -> (last_active_at it was graded at, stored quality block). The metadata\n# upsert replaces the whole blob, so a row re-sent without its grade would ERASE\n# the stored one; the cache lets an unchanged session carry its grade forward\n# without re-reading its events every cycle.\n_OPENCLAW_QUALITY_CACHE: dict = {}\n_OPENCLAW_QUALITY_CACHE_MAX = 5000\n\n\ndef _openclaw_session_quality(store, row: dict):\n    \"\"\"Quality verdicts for one OpenClaw session row, for ``metadata.quality``.\n\n    Family runtimes are graded at ingest (``_session_quality`` in\n    ``sync_family_runtimes``); OpenClaw sessions never were, so every OpenClaw\n    session had no grade and the Harness Engineering bench stamped OpenClaw\n    \"Can't see\" (2026-09-11). The cycle ingests events before session\n    metadata, so the session's events are already in the store here. A\n    session still being written is re-graded on its next change. Never\n    raises; None means \"leave metadata as is\".\n    \"\"\"\n    sid = row.get(\"session_id\") or \"\"\n    if not sid or \":\" in sid:\n        return None  # runtime-prefixed ids belong to the family path\n    stamp = str(row.get(\"last_active_at\") or \"\")\n    hit = _OPENCLAW_QUALITY_CACHE.get(sid)\n    if hit and hit[0] == stamp:\n        return hit[1]\n    try:\n        events = store.query_events(session_id=sid, limit=4000) or []\n        q = _session_quality_from_rows(\n            events, runtime=\"openclaw\", session_id=sid,\n            thresholds=_quality_thresholds_for(\"openclaw\", store))\n    except Exception:\n        log.debug(\"openclaw quality assessment failed (%s)\", sid, exc_info=True)\n        return hit[1] if hit else None\n    if len(_OPENCLAW_QUALITY_CACHE) >= _OPENCLAW_QUALITY_CACHE_MAX:\n        _OPENCLAW_QUALITY_CACHE.clear()\n    _OPENCLAW_QUALITY_CACHE[sid] = (stamp, q)\n    return q\n\n\ndef _local_ingest_memory_files(all_files: list, changed_paths: list) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Persist plaintext memory blobs to local DuckDB. ``all_files`` is the\n    full list of (name, content) tuples; ``changed_paths`` is the subset\n    that changed since last sync. We only write the changed ones — the\n    store's sha256 dedup means it's a no-op anyway, but skipping the\n    encode round-trip is cheaper.\"\"\"\n    if not changed_paths:\n        return\n    from clawmetry import local_store\n\n    store = local_store.get_store()\n    changed_set = set(changed_paths)\n    now_iso = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()\n    for name, content in all_files:\n        if name not in changed_set:\n            continue\n        store.ingest_memory_blob({\n            \"agent_type\": \"openclaw\",  # OpenClaw harness writes these files\n            \"agent_id\": \"main\",\n            \"path\": name,\n            \"ts\": now_iso,\n            \"blob\": content,\n        })\n\n\n_sessions_json_cache: dict = {\"ts\": 0.0, \"data\": None, \"mtime\": 0.0}\n\n\ndef sync_sessions_recent(\n    config: dict, state: dict, paths: dict, minutes: int = 60\n) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Sync only events from the last N minutes, reading files from the tail.\n\n    This gives the dashboard immediate visibility into *current* activity.\n    The normal ``sync_sessions`` loop then backfills older events in the\n    background without blocking the Brain feed.\n\n    Strategy:\n      1. For each session file (newest-modified first), binary-search for the\n         first line whose timestamp falls within the window.\n      2. Sync from that line to EOF.\n      3. Advance ``last_event_ids`` so the normal loop skips already-synced\n         recent lines and continues backfilling from where it left off.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not _sync_allowed():\n        return 0\n    _record_sync_progress(\"sessions_recent\", 0)\n    from datetime import timedelta\n\n    sessions_dir = _openclaw_sessions_dir(paths, state)\n    api_key = config[\"api_key\"]\n    enc_key = config.get(\"encryption_key\")\n    node_id = config[\"node_id\"]\n    last_ids: dict = state.setdefault(\"last_event_ids\", {})\n    total = 0\n\n    cutoff = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=minutes)\n    cutoff_iso = cutoff.isoformat()\n\n    # Build subagent map (same logic as sync_sessions)\n    # Cache sessions.json for 60 seconds to avoid re-parsing every call\n    global _sessions_json_cache\n    file_to_subagent_id: dict[str, str] = {}\n    index_path = os.path.join(sessions_dir, \"sessions.json\")\n    if os.path.isfile(index_path):\n        try:\n            current_mtime = os.path.getmtime(index_path)\n            if _sessions_json_cache[\"data\"] is not None and _sessions_json_cache[\"mtime\"] == current_mtime:\n                file_to_subagent_id = _sessions_json_cache[\"data\"]\n            else:\n                with open(index_path) as _fi:\n                    _idx = json.load(_fi)\n                for _k, _meta in _idx.items():\n                    if \":subagent:\" in _k and isinstance(_meta, dict):\n                        _sf = _meta.get(\"sessionFile\", \"\")\n                        if _sf:\n                            file_to_subagent_id[os.path.basename(_sf)] = _k.split(\":\")[-1]\n                _sessions_json_cache = {\"ts\": time.time(), \"data\": file_to_subagent_id.copy(), \"mtime\": current_mtime}\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n\n    jsonl_files = _list_session_jsonls(sessions_dir)\n    jsonl_files.sort(key=lambda p: os.path.getmtime(p), reverse=True)\n\n    for fpath in jsonl_files:\n        if total >= MAX_EVENTS_PER_CYCLE:\n            break\n\n        fname = os.path.basename(fpath)\n        cloud_fname = _canonical_session_file(fname)\n        subagent_id = file_to_subagent_id.get(cloud_fname) or file_to_subagent_id.get(fname)\n\n        try:\n            with open(fpath, \"r\", errors=\"replace\") as f:\n                all_lines = list(islice(f, None))  # read all for backwards scan\n\n            n = len(all_lines)\n            if n == 0:\n                continue\n\n            # Find the first line >= cutoff by scanning backwards.\n            # Most lines have a \"timestamp\" field we can compare lexicographically.\n            start_idx = n  # default: nothing recent\n            for idx in range(n - 1, -1, -1):\n                raw = all_lines[idx].strip()\n                if not raw:\n                    continue\n                try:\n                    obj = json.loads(raw)\n                    ts = obj.get(\"timestamp\", \"\")\n                    if ts and ts < cutoff_iso:\n                        start_idx = idx + 1\n                        break\n                except Exception:\n                    continue\n            else:\n                # All lines are within the window (or no timestamps found)\n                start_idx = 0\n\n            if start_idx >= n:\n                continue  # nothing recent in this file\n\n            # Only sync lines that haven't been synced yet\n            already_synced = last_ids.get(fname, 0)\n            effective_start = max(start_idx, already_synced)\n            if effective_start >= n:\n                continue\n\n            batch: list[dict] = []\n            for i in range(effective_start, n):\n                raw = all_lines[i].strip()\n                if not raw:\n                    continue\n                try:\n                    obj = json.loads(raw)\n                except Exception:\n                    continue\n                batch.append(obj)\n                if len(batch) >= BATCH_SIZE:\n                    _flush_session_batch(\n                        batch, cloud_fname, api_key, enc_key, node_id, subagent_id\n                    )\n                    total += len(batch)\n                    batch = []\n                    if total >= MAX_EVENTS_PER_CYCLE:\n                        break\n\n            if batch:\n                _flush_session_batch(\n                    batch, cloud_fname, api_key, enc_key, node_id, subagent_id\n                )\n                total += len(batch)\n\n            # Advance cursor to EOF so backfill loop doesn't re-send these.\n            # But DON'T advance past what the normal loop would have started at\n            # — keep the old cursor so it backfills the gap between old cursor\n            # and start_idx.\n            last_ids[fname] = max(last_ids.get(fname, 0), n)\n\n        except Exception as e:\n            log.warning(f\"Recent sync error ({fname}): {e}\")\n\n    _record_sync_progress(\"sessions_recent\", total, total)\n    return total\n\n\n# ── Sync: claude-cli backend transcripts ──────────────────────────────────────\n# OpenClaw routes most chat (TUI, Telegram, etc.) through the agent/cli-backend\n# plugin, which delegates to the Claude Code CLI. Claude CLI writes the actual\n# transcript to ~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/<cli-session-id>.jsonl -- keyed on\n# the agent process CWD, which is usually *not* the OpenClaw workspace. Without\n# this adapter the cloud Brain feed stays frozen at the last bootstrap event\n# and misses every real message.\n\n\ndef _claude_projects_root() -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Return Claude Code's projects directory.\"\"\"\n    custom = os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR\")\n    if custom:\n        return Path(os.path.expanduser(custom)) / \"projects\"\n    return Path(os.path.expanduser(\"~/.claude/projects\"))\n\n\n# ── Canonical Claude Code event id derivation (#1232) ────────────────────────\n#\n# Background: three independent ingest paths converge on the same logical\n# Claude Code message but used to compute three different ``events.id`` values,\n# defeating the ``INSERT OR IGNORE`` dedup at the local store boundary:\n#\n#   path #1  sync_claude_cli_sessions        →  bare uuid              (legacy)\n#   path #2  sync_openclaw_claude_sessions   →  openclaw-cc:<cc>:top:<uuid>\n#   path #3  sync_openclaw_claude_sessions_via_index\n#                                            →  openclaw-cc:<oc>:top:<uuid> | line:N\n#\n# The user observed 2x and 3x duplicate rows in Brain. PR #1227's\n# ``skip_claude_ids`` short-circuit only suppresses path #2 vs #3 collisions —\n# path #1 (legacy) was always free to re-write the same logical event under a\n# different id, and historical data already carries the dupes regardless.\n#\n# Fix: every Claude Code-derived event flows through ``_canonical_event_id`` so\n# all three paths produce IDENTICAL ids for identical source lines. The store's\n# existing PRIMARY KEY then dedups for free on subsequent re-reads. Subagent /\n# tool-result rows keep their path-scoped id schemes — those aren't dupes\n# (each file/uuid pair is genuinely unique).\ndef _canonical_event_id(\n    obj: dict,\n    *,\n    session_id: str,\n    line_no: int | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Stable, path-independent id for a Claude Code event.\n\n    Deterministic — three different ingest paths reading the same source jsonl\n    line MUST return the same id. The local store keys ``events`` by id, so\n    matching ids → ``INSERT OR IGNORE`` collapses re-writes silently.\n\n    Strategy:\n      1. If the source line carries a ``uuid`` (or pre-translated ``id``) that\n         looks like a UUID, use ``cc-msg:<uuid>``. Top-level Claude Code\n         messages always have this; assistant / user / attachment / system\n         events all qualify.\n      2. Otherwise (queue-operation, summary, and other synthesised types\n         that carry no per-event uuid), compose a content-stable hash from\n         the few fields that survive across all three paths: session, ts,\n         type, and an MD5 of the canonical body. ``line_no`` is intentionally\n         NOT part of this — the same line read twice from two byte offsets\n         (path #2 vs #3) would otherwise produce different ids.\n\n    Returns a string suitable for use as ``events.id``. Never raises.\n    \"\"\"\n    raw_uuid = obj.get(\"uuid\") or obj.get(\"id\")\n    if isinstance(raw_uuid, str):\n        s = raw_uuid.strip().lower()\n        # 36-char canonical UUID form: 8-4-4-4-12 hex with dashes.\n        if (\n            len(s) == 36\n            and s[8] == \"-\" and s[13] == \"-\" and s[18] == \"-\" and s[23] == \"-\"\n            and all(c in \"0123456789abcdef-\" for c in s)\n        ):\n            return f\"cc-msg:{s}\"\n    # Fallback: synthesise a deterministic id from the body. We compute the\n    # hash over a normalised projection of the event so injected metadata\n    # (added by _translate_claude_session_line: _claude_session_id,\n    # _openclaw_session_id, _oc_cc_kind, _subagent_file, parentUuid renamed\n    # to parentId, etc.) doesn't change the digest. The keys we keep are\n    # everything except the small set of wrapper/cross-ref fields that\n    # differ per-path.\n    skip_keys = {\n        \"_claude_session_id\",\n        \"_openclaw_session_id\",\n        \"_oc_cc_kind\",\n        \"_subagent_file\",\n        \"parentUuid\",\n        \"parentId\",\n        \"uuid\",\n        \"id\",\n    }\n    canonical = {\n        k: v for k, v in obj.items()\n        if k not in skip_keys\n    }\n    try:\n        body = json.dumps(canonical, sort_keys=True, separators=(\",\", \":\"), default=str)\n    except Exception:\n        body = repr(sorted(canonical.items()))\n    digest = _nsh.md5(body.encode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")).hexdigest()[:16]\n    ts = obj.get(\"timestamp\") or obj.get(\"ts\") or \"?\"\n    evt_type = obj.get(\"type\") or \"unknown\"\n    return f\"cc-derived:{session_id}:{ts}:{evt_type}:{digest}\"\n\n\ndef _translate_claude_cli_event(obj: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Map claude-cli jsonl event keys onto OpenClaw event keys.\n\n    The cloud Brain parser keys off 'id', 'parentId', 'type', 'timestamp',\n    and 'message'. We rename in-place and pass the rest through\n    so cost/usage/tool fields survive without per-version translation.\n\n    Tags the result with ``_cc_source: True`` so the downstream local-ingest\n    helper knows to compute a canonical Claude Code event id (#1232) instead\n    of falling back to its legacy session+ts+type composition.\n    \"\"\"\n    out = dict(obj)\n    if \"uuid\" in out and \"id\" not in out:\n        out[\"id\"] = out.pop(\"uuid\")\n    if \"parentUuid\" in out and \"parentId\" not in out:\n        out[\"parentId\"] = out.pop(\"parentUuid\")\n    out[\"_cc_source\"] = True\n    return out\n\n\ndef sync_claude_cli_sessions(config: dict, state: dict, paths: dict) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Tail claude-cli transcripts and push them under the OpenClaw session_file.\n\n    For each entry in `agents/main/sessions/sessions.json` that carries a\n    `claudeCliSessionId`, locate the matching jsonl under\n    `~/.claude/projects/*/` (scanning all project dirs, since Claude Code\n    derives the slug from the agent's CWD rather than the OpenClaw workspace),\n    tail new lines, translate them, and push via `_flush_session_batch` using\n    the OpenClaw session_file basename. The cloud correlates events to the\n    existing session row by that basename, so no cloud-side change is required.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not _sync_allowed():\n        return 0\n    sessions_dir = paths.get(\"sessions_dir\") or \"\"\n    if not sessions_dir:\n        return 0\n\n    api_key = config[\"api_key\"]\n    enc_key = config.get(\"encryption_key\")\n    node_id = config[\"node_id\"]\n\n    index_path = os.path.join(sessions_dir, \"sessions.json\")\n    if not os.path.isfile(index_path):\n        return 0\n    try:\n        with open(index_path) as fi:\n            idx = json.load(fi)\n    except Exception:\n        return 0\n\n    # Claude Code derives the project slug from the *agent process CWD*, not the\n    # OpenClaw workspace — a Telegram session spawned from ~/clawd writes to\n    # `-home-vivek-clawd/`, even though OpenClaw's workspace is\n    # ~/.openclaw/workspace. Scan every project dir and index transcripts by\n    # their session-id filename so we find the right file regardless of CWD.\n    projects_root = _claude_projects_root()\n    if not projects_root.is_dir():\n        return 0\n    cli_id_to_path: dict[str, Path] = {}\n    try:\n        for proj_dir in projects_root.iterdir():\n            if not proj_dir.is_dir():\n                continue\n            for jp in proj_dir.glob(\"*.jsonl\"):\n                cli_id_to_path[jp.stem] = jp\n    except OSError:\n        return 0\n\n    targets: list[tuple[str, str]] = []  # (claude_jsonl_path, openclaw_basename)\n    for sess_key, meta in idx.items():\n        if not isinstance(meta, dict):\n            continue\n        cli_id = meta.get(\"claudeCliSessionId\") or (\n            meta.get(\"cliSessionIds\", {}) or {}\n        ).get(\"claude-cli\")\n        if not cli_id:\n            continue\n        cli_path = cli_id_to_path.get(cli_id)\n        if cli_path is None:\n            continue\n        oc_sf = meta.get(\"sessionFile\", \"\")\n        # Fall back to <openclaw_session_id>.jsonl when sessionFile is absent\n        # (e.g. Telegram session metadata exists but the OpenClaw jsonl was\n        # never written). Cloud will create the session row from these events.\n        oc_basename = (\n            os.path.basename(oc_sf)\n            if oc_sf\n            else f\"{meta.get('sessionId', cli_id)}.jsonl\"\n        )\n        targets.append((str(cli_path), oc_basename))\n\n    if not targets:\n        return 0\n\n    # Separate offset namespace so it can't collide with OpenClaw jsonl offsets.\n    cli_offsets: dict = state.setdefault(\"last_event_ids_cli\", {})\n    total = 0\n\n    for cli_path, oc_basename in targets:\n        if total >= MAX_EVENTS_PER_CYCLE:\n            break\n\n        offset_key = os.path.basename(cli_path)\n        last_line = cli_offsets.get(offset_key, 0)\n        batch: list[dict] = []\n\n        try:\n            with open(cli_path, \"r\", errors=\"replace\") as f:\n                new_lines = list(islice(f, last_line, None))\n\n            line_cursor = last_line\n            for i, raw in enumerate(new_lines, start=last_line):\n                raw = raw.strip()\n                if not raw:\n                    line_cursor = i + 1\n                    continue\n                try:\n                    obj = json.loads(raw)\n                except Exception:\n                    line_cursor = i + 1\n                    continue\n                batch.append(_translate_claude_cli_event(obj))\n                line_cursor = i + 1\n                if len(batch) >= BATCH_SIZE:\n                    _flush_session_batch(\n                        batch, oc_basename, api_key, enc_key, node_id\n                    )\n                    total += len(batch)\n                    batch = []\n                    cli_offsets[offset_key] = line_cursor\n                    if total >= MAX_EVENTS_PER_CYCLE:\n                        break\n\n            if batch:\n                _flush_session_batch(batch, oc_basename, api_key, enc_key, node_id)\n                total += len(batch)\n\n            cli_offsets[offset_key] = line_cursor\n\n        except Exception as e:\n            log.warning(f\"claude-cli sync error ({offset_key}): {e}\")\n\n    return total\n\n\n# ── Sync: OpenClaw → Claude Code session JSONL (process-discovered) ──────────\n#\n# OpenClaw delegates execution to a ``claude`` CLI subprocess. Claude Code\n# writes its session transcript to:\n#\n#     ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<session-id>.jsonl\n#\n# where ``<encoded-cwd>`` is the agent's working directory with ``/`` and ``.``\n# both replaced by ``-``. The user observed that Telegram conversations\n# weren't appearing in Brain even though the file\n# (``-Users-vivek--openclaw-workspace/49f1d9fc-….jsonl``) was being actively\n# written. The legacy ``sync_claude_cli_sessions`` path covers most cases, but\n# only when ``~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json`` carries the\n# ``claudeCliSessionId`` binding for that session — which is missing for any\n# session that was started before OpenClaw wrote its binding, or where the\n# binding was lost on a crash. This complementary, defense-in-depth path\n# discovers the live session file by inspecting the running ``claude``\n# subprocess directly, so capture is independent of OpenClaw's index file.\n#\n# Discovery works on macOS, Linux, and Windows because Claude Code uses the\n# same ``~/.claude/projects/`` layout everywhere; the encoding is uniform.\n#\n# Default: ON. Escape hatch: ``CLAWMETRY_DISABLE_CLAUDE_SESSION_INGEST=1``.\n# Per the DuckDB-first / never-default-off-a-MOAT-capability rule\n# (feedback_local_store_default_off_killed_moat 2026-05-13).\n\n\ndef _encode_cwd_for_claude_projects(cwd: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Reproduce Claude Code's project-dir naming convention.\n\n    Claude Code derives the ``~/.claude/projects/<dir>`` slug by replacing\n    every path-structural character in the agent's CWD with ``-``. So\n    ``/Users/vivek/.openclaw/workspace`` → ``-Users-vivek--openclaw-workspace``\n    (the leading ``-`` comes from the absolute path's leading ``/``; the\n    consecutive ``--`` comes from ``/.`` collapsing).\n\n    Windows paths use ``\\\\`` as the separator and carry a drive-letter\n    ``:``; both collapse to ``-`` the same way, so ``C:\\\\Users\\\\Vivek`` →\n    ``C--Users-Vivek``. We\n# don't want a 1 MB grep dump occupying a single row.\n_OC_CC_TOOL_RESULT_MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024\n\n# Cap on number of tool-result files ingested per session per cycle, so a\n# fresh discovery of a 100-file dir doesn't stall the cycle.\n_OC_CC_MAX_TOOL_RESULTS_PER_CYCLE = 200\n\n# Cap on number of subagent files inspected per session per cycle.\n_OC_CC_MAX_SUBAGENT_FILES_PER_CYCLE = 50\n\n\ndef _walk_openclaw_session_bindings(sessions_dir: str) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Read ``~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json`` and return one\n    binding dict per session that has a Claude CLI binding. Skip them so we don't crash on JSON-object-per-file\n# layouts and don't pollute ``events`` with daemon plumbing.\n_CHANNEL_NON_TRANSCRIPT_BASENAMES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({\n    \"update-offset-default.json\",\n    \"schema.json\",\n    \"manifest.json\",\n})\n\n\ndef _list_channel_transcripts(channel_dir: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Return paths to all *transcript* files under a single channel dir.\n\n    A \"transcript\" is any ``*.jsonl`` (live or archived ``.jsonl.reset.<ts>``);\n    we explicitly skip the per-adapter bookkeeping files listed in\n    ``_CHANNEL_NON_TRANSCRIPT_BASENAMES``. has — single source of truth, no drift.\n        \"raw_blob\": obj,\n    }\n\n\ndef sync_channel_messages(config: dict, state: dict, paths: dict) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Tail each ``~/.openclaw/<channel>/*.jsonl`` and ingest both events\n    + channel_messages rows into local DuckDB.\n\n    Returns the number of NEW rows ingested this cycle. If running, definitely installed\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n\n    return result\n\n\n# ── Gateway process-metric capture (#852 follow-up) ──────────────────────────\n# PR #1146 added a *live* gateway-health snapshot (RSS/CPU/uptime). _LAST_GATEWAY_METRIC_TS\n        if elapsed < GATEWAY_METRIC_DEDUP_WINDOW_SEC and _should_dedupe_gateway_metric(\n            _LAST_GATEWAY_METRIC, curr\n        ):\n            return False\n\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store as _ls\n        store = _ls.get_store()\n        store.ingest({\n            \"id\":         uuid.uuid4().hex,\n            \"node_id\":    config.get(\"node_id\") or \"unknown\",\n            \"agent_id\":   \"openclaw-gateway\",\n            \"agent_type\": \"openclaw\",\n            \"event_type\": \"gateway.metric\",\n            \"ts\":         datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),\n            \"data\":       curr,\n        })\n    except Exception as _e:\n        log.debug(\"gateway.metric: ingest failed (%s)\", _e)\n        return False\n\n    _LAST_GATEWAY_METRIC_TS = now_mono\n    _LAST_GATEWAY_METRIC = curr\n    return True\n\n\n# ── Daemon-collected snapshots ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n# Cloud's tabs (Security, Models, Upgrades, Clusters, …) need data the OSS\n# routes/* endpoints derive from local state — host filesystem checks,\n# `openclaw --version` output, gateway WebSocket, etc. None of that exists\n# on Cloud Run. The daemon collects locally and pushes on the heartbeat;\n# cloud stores the latest blob per node and serves it via cloud-side\n# `/api/<feature>` handlers that mirror the OSS shape.\n#\n# Each collector caches its result in `_snapshot_cache` so we don't\n# recompute every heartbeat (most of these are ~100ms-1s and don't change\n# minute-to-minute). Re-collected at the interval below or when missing.\n\n_snapshot_cache: dict = {}            # name → (value, computed_at_unix_ts)\n_SNAPSHOT_TTL_SEC = 300               # 5 min — security posture etc.\n\n\ndef _collect_security_posture() -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"Run OSS `_scan_security_posture()` locally and return its result.\n\n    Imports OSS dashboard.py via importlib so we don't pull the whole Flask\n    app into the daemon process. Assistant opt-in only answers early\n    for eligible Assistant actions, then includes the same general hints.\n\n    Returns the parsed response dict, or None on any failure. The row's session_id is the same\n            # id the device-agent + sessions table use, so it's authoritative.\n            _sid = r.get(\"session_id\")\n            if _sid:\n                data = {**data, \"sessionId\": _sid.rsplit(\":\", 1)[-1]}\n            out.append(_cap_brain_event_size(data))\n        elif isinstance(data, str):\n            _sid = r.get(\"session_id\")\n            out.append({\n                **enrich,\n                \"type\":      r.get(\"event_type\") or \"raw\",\n                \"timestamp\": r.get(\"ts\", \"\"),\n                \"detail\":    data[:_BRAIN_FIELD_CAP],\n                **({\"sessionId\": _sid.rsplit(\":\", 1)[-1]} if _sid else {}),\n            })\n    return out\n\n\n# ── Phase 2: proactive brain cache_push (epic #1032) ─────────────────────────\n# The Brain page is the first thing most users hit on the cloud dashboard. In\n# Phase 1 the cloud only had data for it after a browser /api/cloud/subscribe\n# round-trip (one full heartbeat cycle, up to 60s). Phase 2 pushes the top-50\n# brain events on EVERY heartbeat so the page paints from cache in <100ms.\n#\n# Key shape: `brain:{owner_hash}:{node_id}:recent`. The cloud derives\n# owner_hash from the cm_ token (sha256 hex) — we compute the same value here\n# so both sides agree on the key without needing the daemon to know the\n# cloud's internal user id.\n#\n# TTL: 6h. Each heartbeat overwrites the entry, so TTL only matters when the\n# daemon goes offline — after 6h the cloud treats the cache as cold and\n# re-subscribes. Long enough to cover a typical work-day pause; short enough\n# that stale data doesn't linger after a node is decommissioned.\nBRAIN_CACHE_TTL_SEC = 21600\nBRAIN_CACHE_LIMIT = 50\n# Unchanged brain events are re-pushed at most this often (cloud TTL / 2, so\n# the cache never expires between pushes).\nBRAIN_PUSH_MIN_INTERVAL_SEC = BRAIN_CACHE_TTL_SEC // 2\n_brain_push_state: dict = {\"fingerprint\": None, \"ts\": 0.0}\n# Per-session fairness for the brain blob (the device \"no activity for this\n# session\" fix): guarantee each of the most-recently-active sessions at least\n# BRAIN_PER_SESSION renderable events, across up to BRAIN_SESSION_FANOUT\n# sessions, before filling the rest with the freshest node-wide events. Without\n# this a single very active session floods the newest-N window and crowds out a\n# session the user just messaged. 8×5=40 guaranteed + 10 fill = BRAIN_CACHE_LIMIT,\n# which (with the per-event size cap) keeps the blob inside the device buffer.\nBRAIN_PER_SESSION = 5\nBRAIN_SESSION_FANOUT = 8\n# How deep to scan per session to find BRAIN_PER_SESSION *renderable* events. Far\n# larger than BRAIN_PER_SESSION because a session can end with a long tail of\n# non-renderable plumbing; the scan must reach past it to the real messages.\nBRAIN_PER_SESSION_SCAN = 200\n# Opt-in fanout debug (CLAWMETRY_BRAIN_DEBUG=1) -- logs per-session pick counts so\n# a \"session shows no activity\" report can be diagnosed from the daemon log.\n_BRAIN_DEBUG = os.environ.get(\"CLAWMETRY_BRAIN_DEBUG\", \"\") not in (\"\", \"0\", \"false\")\n\n# Event types that are internal plumbing, NOT real activity -- the device parser\n# (summary_parse.c brain_event_to_row) drops them, so including them in the blob\n# just wastes its limited slots (a session whose only in-window events were\n# ``prompt.submitted`` showed \"no activity\" even though it had real messages).\n_BRAIN_SKIP_TYPES = {\n    \"prompt.submitted\", \"queue-operation\", \"queue_operation\", \"compaction\",\n    \"session.ended\", \"sessionended\", \"session_end\", \"permission-mode\",\n    \"file-history-snapshot\", \"ai-title\", \"last-prompt\",\n}\n\n\ndef _v3_chat_message(data) -> \"dict | None\":\n    \"\"\"Project a daemon-normalised v3 chat row onto the ``{role, content[]}``\n    shape the cloud's ``transformEvents`` and the device's\n    ``brain_event_to_row`` actually render.\n\n    ``_parse_v3_event`` stores OpenClaw v3 conversations as\n    ``prompt.submitted{finalPromptText}`` / ``model.completed{completionText,\n    assistantTexts, toolMetas}`` — there is NO other message-shaped event for\n    these turns, so a brain filter that only knows ``content``/``text``/\n    ``tool_calls`` drops the ENTIRE conversation and the cloud Activity tab\n    shows \"No brain activity events found\" for a node that is talking all\n    day (live-confirmed 2026-07-07 on a hosted openclaw node). Detectors,\n    the outcome classifier, and the eval runner all read these keys already;\n    the brain pipeline was the holdout.\n\n    Returns ``None`` when the row isn't a v3 chat event, already carries a\n    ``message`` block, or has nothing printable.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(data, dict) or isinstance(data.get(\"message\"), dict):\n        return None\n    text = data.get(\"completionText\")\n    if not (isinstance(text, str) and text.strip()):\n        at = data.get(\"assistantTexts\")\n        text = \"\\n\".join(t for t in at if isinstance(t, str) and t) \\\n            if isinstance(at, list) else \"\"\n    if (isinstance(text, str) and text.strip()) or data.get(\"toolMetas\"):\n        content = []\n        if isinstance(text, str) and text.strip():\n            content.append({\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": text})\n        for tm in data.get(\"toolMetas\") or []:\n            if isinstance(tm, dict):\n or {}})\n        if content:\n            return {\"role\": \"assistant\", \"content\": content}\n    fp = data.get(\"finalPromptText\")\n    if isinstance(fp, str) and fp.strip():\n        return {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": fp}]}\n    return None\n\n\ndef _brain_row_renderable(r: dict) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True if the event row would render as a real message / tool event on the\n    device + cloud Brain feed (mirrors ``summary_parse.c brain_event_to_row``).\n    Skips internal plumbing so the blob's limited slots hold real activity.\"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(r, dict):\n        return False\n    raw = r.get(\"data\")\n    data = raw\n    unparseable = False\n    if isinstance(raw, str):\n        try:\n            data = json.loads(raw)\n        except Exception:\n            data, unparseable = None, True\n    # v3 chat turns win over the skip list: for OpenClaw v3 the user prompt\n    # IS a prompt.submitted row (finalPromptText) — Rows without printable v3 text still\n    # fall through to the skip list below.\n    if _v3_chat_message(data) is not None:\n        return True\n    if (r.get(\"event_type\") or \"\").lower() in _BRAIN_SKIP_TYPES:\n        return False\n    if unparseable:\n        return bool(raw.strip())\n    if not isinstance(data, dict):\n        return False\n    if (data.get(\"type\") or \"\").lower() in _BRAIN_SKIP_TYPES:\n        return False\n    msg = data.get(\"message\") if isinstance(data.get(\"message\"), dict) else None\n    src = msg or data\n    content = src.get(\"content\")\n    if isinstance(content, str) and content.strip():\n        return True\n    if isinstance(content, list) and content:\n        return True\n    if data.get(\"text\"):\n        return True\n    if src.get(\"tool_calls\") or data.get(\"tool_calls\") or data.get(\"tool_name\"):\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _owner_hash_for_token(api_key: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Mirror of cloud's `_owner_hash_for(token)` — sha256 hex of the cm_\n    token. The daemon computes it locally so the cache key it sends matches\n    exactly what the cloud derives from the same token on read.\"\"\"\n    import hashlib\n    return hashlib.sha256((api_key or \"\").encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest()\n\n\ndef _build_brain_events() -> list:\n    \"\"\"Build the per-session-fair, renderable, sessionId-stamped brain event list\n    — the SINGLE source of truth for the brain blob. Used by BOTH the heartbeat\n    cache push (``_build_brain_cache_pushes``) AND the on-demand q_brain_refresh\n    path (``_dispatch_pending_queries``) so the two writers of the\n    ``brain:*:recent`` key can never diverge: the refresh path used to rebuild it\n    node-wide and overwrite the heartbeat's fair blob, hiding a just-messaged\n    session behind a flooding one. Returns ``[]`` on any failure.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store\n    except Exception:\n        return []\n    try:\n        store = local_store.get_store(read_only=True)\n        # Newest node-wide events (headroom: drops helper sessions + non-render\n        # plumbing below, so over-fetch to still land BRAIN_CACHE_LIMIT real ones).\n        nw_rows = store.query_events(limit=BRAIN_CACHE_LIMIT * 4)\n    except Exception:\n        return []\n    if not nw_rows:\n        return []\n\n    # Per-session fairness: guarantee each recently-active session its newest\n    # renderable events before filling with the freshest node-wide events, so a\n    # flooding session can't crowd out one the user just messaged. Dedup by id.\n    seen_ids: set = set()\n    picked: list = []\n    per_session: dict = {}\n\n    def _consider(r, cap=None):\n        rid = r.get(\"id\")\n        sid = r.get(\"session_id\") or \"\"\n        if not rid or rid in seen_ids:\n            return\n        if cap is not None and per_session.get(sid, 0) >= cap:\n            return\n        if not _brain_row_renderable(r):\n            return\n        seen_ids.add(rid)\n        per_session[sid] = per_session.get(sid, 0) + 1\n        picked.append(r)\n\n    # Most-recently-active sessions, from the typed sessions table (one row per\n    # session, ordered by last activity) -- NOT the event stream, which a\n    # flooding session dominates. Same source the device-agent session list uses,\n    # so every session the user can TAP on the device is covered.\n    recent_sids: list = []\n    try:\n        for s in store.query_sessions_table(limit=BRAIN_SESSION_FANOUT * 3):\n            sid = s.get(\"session_id\")\n            if sid and sid not in recent_sids:\n                recent_sids.append(sid)\n            if len(recent_sids) >= BRAIN_SESSION_FANOUT:\n                break\n    except Exception:\n        recent_sids = []\n    # Supplement with any session in the newest events not yet in the table.\n    for r in nw_rows:\n        if len(recent_sids) >= BRAIN_SESSION_FANOUT:\n            break\n        sid = r.get(\"session_id\")\n        if sid and sid not in recent_sids:\n            recent_sids.append(sid)\n    # (a) each recent session's newest renderable events (capped per session).\n    # Fetch GENEROUSLY (not just BRAIN_PER_SESSION) because a session can end with\n    # a burst of non-renderable plumbing (queue-operation/prompt.submitted) -- a\n    # tight limit returns only that tail and the renderable filter then picks\n    # nothing, so the session vanishes from its own feed. A wide window lets the\n    # filter always reach its quota of real messages.\n    for sid in recent_sids:\n        try:\n            srows = store.query_events(session_id=sid, limit=BRAIN_PER_SESSION_SCAN)\n        except Exception:\n            srows = []\n        before = len(picked)\n        for r in srows:\n            _consider(r, cap=BRAIN_PER_SESSION)\n        if _BRAIN_DEBUG:\n            log.info(\"brain fanout: %s -> %d picked (scanned %d)\",\n                     (sid or \"\")[:24], len(picked) - before, len(srows))\n    # (b) fill the rest with the freshest node-wide renderable events.\n    for r in nw_rows:\n        if len(picked) >= BRAIN_CACHE_LIMIT:\n            break\n        _consider(r)\n\n    picked.sort(key=lambda r: r.get(\"ts\") or \"\", reverse=True)\n    picked = picked[:BRAIN_CACHE_LIMIT]\n    # Collapse duplicate-content siblings (assistant + model.completed +\n    # delivery-mirror echo; gateway prompt.submitted + transcript user copy)\n    # with the SAME shared logic /api/brain-history uses. Without this the\n    # cloud feed showed each reply three times while the local API showed it\n    # once (founder screenshot, 2026-07-31).\n    try:\n        from clawmetry.brain_dedupe import collapse_duplicate_brain_rows\n        picked = collapse_duplicate_brain_rows(picked)\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    # Same translation as routes/brain.py:_try_local_store_brain (incl. the\n    # hide_clawmetry_session filter + sessionId stamp + size cap).\n    return _rows_to_brain_events(picked)[:BRAIN_CACHE_LIMIT]\n\n\n# Hard ceiling for one windowed brain relay answer. Bounds the encrypted\n# blob the daemon POSTs back to /ingest/cache (each event is size-capped by\n# _cap_brain_event_size, so 500 events stays low-single-digit MB).\nBRAIN_WINDOW_LIMIT = 500\n\n\ndef _build_brain_events_window(since=None, until=None, limit=BRAIN_WINDOW_LIMIT) -> list:\n    \"\"\"Windowed variant of ``_build_brain_events`` for the date-time range\n    investigation feature (\"what happened at 3AM\").
