Same renderable filter + translation as the\n    live blob so the cloud browser's ``transformEvents`` handles both\n    identically. Returns ``[]`` on any failure.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store\n    except Exception:\n        return []\n    try:\n        lim = max(1, min(int(limit or BRAIN_WINDOW_LIMIT), BRAIN_WINDOW_LIMIT))\n    except (TypeError, ValueError):\n        lim = BRAIN_WINDOW_LIMIT\n    qkwargs = {\"limit\": lim * 2, \"exclude_daemon\": True}\n    if since:\n        qkwargs[\"since\"] = str(since)\n    if until:\n        qkwargs[\"until\"] = str(until)\n    try:\n        store = local_store.get_store(read_only=True)\n        rows = store.query_events(**qkwargs)\n    except Exception:\n        return []\n    rows = [r for r in rows if _brain_row_renderable(r)][:lim]\n    # Same duplicate-sibling collapse as the live blob (_build_brain_events):\n    # a windowed investigation must not show one reply three times either.\n    try:\n        from clawmetry.brain_dedupe import collapse_duplicate_brain_rows\n        rows = collapse_duplicate_brain_rows(rows)\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    return _rows_to_brain_events(rows)[:lim]\n\n\ndef _build_brain_cache_pushes(config: dict) -> list:\n    \"\"\"Return the heartbeat `cache_pushes` array — currently a single entry\n    holding the encrypted top-50 brain events for this node.\n\n    Returns an empty list when:\n      - The local store has no events yet (fresh install) — nothing to push.\n      - Encryption key is unset — we never push plaintext.\n      - The local store import fails — degrade silently.\n\n    The blob shape mirrors `routes.brain._try_local_store_brain` so the cloud\n    read path can hand the decrypted dict straight to the existing dashboard\n    JS without translation.\n    \"\"\"\n    enc_key = config.get(\"encryption_key\")\n    if not enc_key:\n        return []\n    api_key = config.get(\"api_key\", \"\")\n    node_id = config.get(\"node_id\", \"\")\n    if not (api_key and node_id):\n        return []\n    events = _build_brain_events()\n    if not events:\n        return []\n    # Skip the encrypt + upload when the picked events are the ones already\n    # in the cloud cache (2026-09-02: the ~8.7 MB brain blob was rebuilt and\n    # re-sent on every heartbeat whether or not anything had happened).\n    try:\n        import hashlib as _hl\n        fp = _hl.sha256(\"|\".join(\n            str(e.get(\"id\") or e.get(\"ts\") or \"\") for e in events\n        ).encode()).hexdigest()\n    except Exception:\n        fp = None\n    _now = time.time()\n    if (fp is not None and fp == _brain_push_state.get(\"fingerprint\")\n            and (_now - float(_brain_push_state.get(\"ts\") or 0)) < BRAIN_PUSH_MIN_INTERVAL_SEC):\n        return []\n    payload = {\n        \"events\":  events,\n        \"count\":   len(events),\n        \"_source\": \"local_store\",\n        \"_shape\":  \"brain_history\",\n    }\n    try:\n        blob = encrypt_payload(payload, enc_key)\n    except Exception:\n        return []\n    # Pending until the heartbeat that carries it returns 2xx (see\n    # _commit_cache_push_gates): a build the cloud never received must not\n    # silence the next one.\n    _brain_push_state[\"pending\"] = (fp, _now)\n    owner_hash = _owner_hash_for_token(api_key)\n    return [{\n        \"key\":    f\"brain:{owner_hash}:{node_id}:recent\",\n        \"ttl_s\":  BRAIN_CACHE_TTL_SEC,\n        \"blob\":   blob,\n    }]\n\n\n# ── Memory files cache push (epic #1032 — Memory tab fix) ───────────────────\n# The cloud Memory tab in Node Detail reads from a cache key populated here.\n# Same heartbeat-piggyback envelope as the Brain cache push: encrypted blob\n# under ``memory:{owner_hash}:{node_id}:files`` with the user's E2E key.\n# Cloud read path: ``routes/cloud.py:cloud_memory_files``.\n\nMEMORY_CACHE_TTL_SEC = 21600       # 6h — matches Brain TTL; files change slowly\nMEMORY_CACHE_LIMIT = 600            # every runtime's memory + skills, not just OpenClaw's\nMEMORY_CONTENT_TRUNCATE = 120_000   # per file\n# Total plaintext budget for one push. MEMORY_CACHE_LIMIT × the per-file cap is\n# a 72MB worst case, which is not a heartbeat payload. Files past the budget\n# are still LISTED (so the tree is honest about what exists) with empty\n# content, and the viewer says to open them locally.\nMEMORY_CACHE_TOTAL_BUDGET = 6_000_000\n# Re-push floor. Push when the content actually changed, or when we're\n# halfway to the cache TTL and the cloud copy needs refreshing either way.\nMEMORY_PUSH_MIN_INTERVAL_SEC = MEMORY_CACHE_TTL_SEC // 2\n# A CHANGED snapshot is re-pushed at most this often. The cloud Memory tab is\n# not a live feed; a fresh file reaching it within ten minutes is plenty, and\n# the push is the whole 5.9 MB snapshot encrypted and uploaded, not a delta.\nMEMORY_PUSH_CHANGED_MIN_INTERVAL_SEC = 600\n# Catalog categories that are runtime CONFIG rather than memory: hook\n# settings (settings.json / settings.local.json), MCP server manifests and\n# openclaw.json. They stay in the local catalog but never ride the cloud push,\n# because they routinely carry gateway tokens, bot tokens and provider keys.\nMEMORY_PUSH_EXCLUDED_CATEGORIES = frozenset({\"hooks\", \"mcp\"})\n# A file whose hash has changed on this many consecutive builds is runtime\n# state, not memory (2026-09-02: Grok Bot's ``local-exec-supervisor.json`` and\n# ``local-exec-daemon-connection.json`` rewrote every cycle, so the fingerprint\n# never matched and the full snapshot went out every 95 s -- 5.2 GB a day of\n# upload for nothing). Such files still ship in the snapshot; they just stop\n# deciding when it ships.\nMEMORY_PUSH_VOLATILE_AFTER = 3\n_memory_push_state: dict = {\"fingerprint\": None, \"ts\": 0.0, \"seen\": {}, \"churn\": {}}\n\n\ndef _commit_cache_push_gates() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Arm the brain/memory skip gates for the pushes the cloud just accepted.\n\n    A builder records only a *pending* fingerprint; ``send_heartbeat`` calls\n    this once ``/ingest/heartbeat`` returned 2xx. So a build whose heartbeat\n    failed, or a build made outside the heartbeat (tests, a one-off tool),\n    never suppresses the next push: the gate only ever remembers a snapshot\n    the cloud actually holds.\"\"\"\n    for _st in (_brain_push_state, _memory_push_state):\n        _p = _st.pop(\"pending\", None)\n        if _p:\n            _st[\"fingerprint\"], _st[\"ts\"] = _p\n\n\ndef _memory_push_fingerprint(rows: list) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Fingerprint of the memory snapshot that ignores files which churn.\n\n    Tracks each file's hash across builds; a file that changed on\n    ``MEMORY_PUSH_VOLATILE_AFTER`` consecutive builds is left out of the\n    fingerprint until it holds still again. sent_at = body.get(\"sent_at\")\n            if isinstance(sent_at, bool) or not isinstance(sent_at, (float, int)) or not 0 <= time.time() - sent_at <= 300:\n                raise ValueError(\"expired _post_process_control_result(config, action, result)\n\n\ndef _action_process_control(config: dict, action: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Cloud/device-relayed kill / pause / resume of a runaway agent Never raises.\"\"\"\n    if not action.get(\"cache_key\"):\n        return  # no cache_key -> nowhere to report; drop (cloud always sets one)\n    threading.Thread(target=_run_process_control, args=(config, action),\n                     name=\"cm-proc-ctl\", daemon=True).start()\n\n\ndef _hitl_set_pause(session_id: str, paused: bool) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Belt-and-suspenders enforcement: create/remove the proxy HITL pause file\n    ``~/.clawmetry/hitl/pause_<session_id>``. Never raises.\"\"\"\n    if not session_id:\n        return\n    try:\n        d = Path.home() / \".clawmetry\" / \"hitl\"\n        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        f = d / (\"pause_%s\" % session_id)\n        if paused:\n            f.write_text(\"\")  # empty marker; existence is the signal\n        elif f.exists():\n            f.unlink()\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.debug(\"hitl pause file set failed for %s: %s\",\n                  str(session_id)[:128].replace(\"\\r\", \" \").replace(\"\\n\", \" \"), e)\n\n\ndef _openclaw_cancel_task(lookup, timeout: int = 30) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Cancel a running OpenClaw task/session via the CLI with OpenClaw's OWN\n    credentials. The gateway token ClawMetry holds is ``operator.read`` only, so\n    mutating a run goes through ``openclaw tasks cancel <lookup>`` (same escape\n    hatch as ``run_openclaw_cron``). Returns\n    ``{ok, scope_pending, error, raw}``; classifies a pairing/scope rejection as\n    ``scope_pending`` so the caller can show an actionable approval hint.\"\"\"\n    binp = _resolve_openclaw_bin()\n    if not binp:\n        return {\"ok\": False, \"scope_pending\": False,\n                \"error\": \"openclaw CLI not found on this machine\", \"raw\": \"\"}\n    env = dict(os.environ)\n    env[\"PATH\"] = os.pathsep.join([\n        os.path.dirname(binp), \"/opt/homebrew/bin\", \"/usr/local/bin\",\n        os.path.expanduser(\"~/.local/bin\"), env.get(\"PATH\", \"/usr/bin:/bin\")])\n    cmd = [binp, \"tasks\", \"cancel\", str(lookup)]\n    try:\n        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True,\n                              timeout=timeout, env=env)\n    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:\n        return {\"ok\": False, \"scope_pending\": False,\n                \"error\": \"openclaw tasks cancel timed out\", \"raw\": \"\"}\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        # The exception text stays in the log; the result dict can reach an\n        # HTTP response, so it carries a fixed token instead.\n        log.warning(\"openclaw tasks cancel could not run: %s\", e)\n        return {\"ok\": False, \"scope_pending\": False,\n                \"error\": \"openclaw_cli_error\", \"raw\": \"\"}\n    blob = (proc.stdout or \"\") + \"\\n\" + (proc.stderr or \"\")\n    low = blob.lower()\n    scope_pending = (\"pairing required\" in low or \"scope upgrade\" in low\n                     or \"more scopes than currently approved\" in low)\n    if proc.returncode != 0:\n        err = (proc.stderr or proc.stdout or \"exit %d\" % proc.returncode).strip()\n        if scope_pending:\n            err = (\"Stopping an OpenClaw run needs a one-time gateway approval. \"\n                   \"On the host run `openclaw devices list` then \"\n                   \"`openclaw devices approve <id>`, then retry.\")\n        return {\"ok\": False, \"scope_pending\": scope_pending,\n                \"error\": err[:500], \"raw\": blob[:1000]}\n    return {\"ok\": True, \"scope_pending\": False, \"error\": \"\", \"raw\": blob[:1000]}\n\n\ndef _proc_control_cwd_backfill(runtime: str, session_id: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Working directory for a session about to be signaled, read from the\n    local store. Deliberately NOT falling back to the bare\n        # id: an unscoped match can return a DIFFERENT runtime's directory,\n        # which would then be used to choose a process to signal.\n        row = store.get_session_location(ns_id, agent_type=\"openclaw\")\n        if row:\n            cwd = row.get(\"cwd\")\n            if isinstance(cwd, str) and cwd.strip():\n                return cwd.strip()\n            meta = row.get(\"metadata\")\n            if isinstance(meta, dict):\n                hit = _first_alias(meta, _CWD_ALIASES)\n                if hit:\n                    return hit\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - backfill is best-effort\n        log.debug(\"proc-control cwd backfill failed (%s): %s\", ns_id, e)\n    return \"\"\n\n\ndef _registered_kill(runtime: str, session_id: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"Try the pro-registered per-runtime kill handler\n    (``clawmetry.approvals.KILL_HANDLERS`` — nanoclaw docker-stop, n8n\n    execution-stop API, antigravity CancelCascadeInvocation, …). noqa: BLE001 - a bad plugin degrades, never crashes\n        log.warning(\"registered kill handler (%s) raised: %s\", runtime, e)\n        return {\"ok\": False, \"action\": \"kill\", \"runtime\": runtime,\n                \"session_id\": session_id,\n                \"detail\": \"kill_handler_error\"}\n    return {\"ok\": ok, \"action\": \"kill\", \"runtime\": runtime,\n            \"session_id\": session_id,\n            \"detail\": (\"stopped via %s kill handler\" % runtime) if ok\n            else \"kill handler could not stop this session\"}\n\n\ndef _run_process_control(config: dict, action: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Worker body for _action_process_control (runs in a daemon thread).\"\"\"\n    import clawmetry.process_control as _pc\n    atype = action.get(\"type\")\n    # Lowercased once: _registered_kill lowercases its lookup, and the\n    # SUPPORTED_RUNTIMES membership test below must agree with it.\n    runtime = str(action.get(\"runtime\") or \"\").strip().lower()\n    session_id = str(action.get(\"session_id\") or \"\").strip()\n    cwd = str(action.get(\"cwd\") or \"\").strip()\n    # The cloud relay does not send cwd; cwd-resolved runtimes need it.\n    if not cwd and runtime and runtime not in (\"openclaw\", \"claude_code\"):\n        cwd = _proc_control_cwd_backfill(runtime, session_id)\n    result = {\"ok\": False, \"error\": \"no-op\", \"runtime\": runtime, \"action\": atype}\n    try:\n        if atype == \"kill_session\":\n            _hitl_set_pause(session_id, True)\n            if runtime in (\"openclaw\", \"nemoclaw\"):\n                # the result is relayed onward.\n        log.exception(\"process control %s failed for %s\", atype,\n                      str(session_id)[:128].replace(\"\\r\", \" \").replace(\"\\n\", \" \"))\n        result = {\"ok\": False, \"error\": \"control_error\", \"runtime\": runtime,\n                  \"action\": atype, \"session_id\": session_id}\n    _post_process_control_result(config, action, result)\n\n\ndef _post_process_control_result(config: dict, action: dict, result: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"E2E-encrypt the kill/pause/resume outcome and POST it to /ingest/cache\n    under the action's cache_key so the web dashboard and device can poll it.\"\"\"\n    cache_key = action.get(\"cache_key\")\n    enc_key = config.get(\"encryption_key\")\n    api_key = config.get(\"api_key\", \"\")\n    node_id = config.get(\"node_id\", \"\")\n    if not (cache_key and enc_key and api_key):\n        return\n    try:\n        blob = encrypt_payload(\n            {\"result\": result, \"session_id\": action.get(\"session_id\"),\n             \"runtime\": action.get(\"runtime\"), \"type\": action.get(\"type\"),\n             \"_shape\": \"process_control\"},\n            enc_key,\n        )\n        _post(\n            \"/ingest/cache\",\n            {\"node_id\": node_id, \"id\": action.get(\"id\"), \"cache_key\": cache_key,\n             \"blob\": blob, \"shape\": \"process_control\", \"ttl\": 600},\n            api_key,\n        )\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.warning(\"process_control cache post failed: %s\", e)\n\n\ndef _action_runtime_backfill(config: dict, action: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"On-demand backfill: raise the ingest depth for ONE family runtime so the\n    next ``sync_family_runtimes`` pass pulls older sessions into DuckDB and\n    uploads them. Triggered by the cloud UI when the user digs into the past\n    (founder 2026-06-03: \"we should be able to go back as much as the user\n    prefers but default-sync 50 recent\"). Never raises.\n\n    Action shape: ``{\"type\": \"runtime_backfill\", \"runtime\": \"claude_code\",\n    \"limit\": 500}``. The limit is the TOTAL most-recent sessions to ingest for\n    that runtime (capped at _RUNTIME_BACKFILL_MAX); it only ever increases the\n    override, so repeated \"load more\" requests deepen monotonically.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        runtime = str(action.get(\"runtime\") or \"\").strip()\n        if not runtime:\n            return\n        try:\n            want = int(action.get(\"limit\") or 0)\n        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n            want = 0\n        if want <= 0:\n            # No explicit target -> step the current depth up by one page.\n            want = _effective_family_limit(runtime) + max(50, _family_session_limit())\n        want = min(want, _RUNTIME_BACKFILL_MAX)\n        prev = int(_RUNTIME_BACKFILL_OVERRIDES.get(runtime, 0) or 0)\n        if want <= prev:\n            return  # already at or beyond this depth\n        _RUNTIME_BACKFILL_OVERRIDES[runtime] = want\n        log.info(\"runtime_backfill: %s ingest depth raised to %d (was %d); Accept\n            # std base64 too; raw plaintext-only string falls back to utf-8.\n            import base64 as _b64\n            try:\n                blob_bytes = _b64.urlsafe_b64decode(blob_raw + \"==\")\n            except Exception:\n                try:\n                    blob_bytes = _b64.b64decode(blob_raw + \"==\")\n                except Exception:\n                    blob_bytes = blob_raw.encode(\"utf-8\")\n        else:\n            log.warning(\"channel_config_upsert: bad blob type %s\", type(blob_raw))\n            return\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.warning(\"channel_config_upsert: local_store import failed: %s\", e)\n        return\n    try:\n        local_store.get_store().ingest_channel_config(\n            provider=provider,\n            encrypted_blob=blob_bytes,\n            enabled=bool(enabled) if enabled is not None else None,\n            status_meta=None,\n        )\n        log.info(\"channel_config_upsert provider=%s enabled=%s blob_bytes=%s\",\n                 provider, enabled, len(blob_bytes) if blob_bytes else 0)\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.warning(\"channel_config_upsert ingest failed (provider=%s): %s\",\n                    provider, e)\n\n\ndef _action_channel_test(config: dict, action: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Run a local test of the channel adapter and stamp the result.\n\n    Wire shape: ``{type: \"channel_test\", provider}``.\n\n    The actual upstream ping (Telegram getMe, Slack auth.test, ...) is\n    delegated to ``_run_channel_test_local``. The adapter binary writes its own real\n    test results back via the gateway in a follow-up phase.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store\n    except Exception as e:\n        return False, f\"local_store unavailable: {e}\"\n    try:\n        # Daemon owns the writer; using the same RW handle for the read\n        # avoids the \"cannot open RO when file doesn't exist yet\" edge case\n        # on first-channel-test-before-any-config.\n        rows = local_store.get_store().query_channel_configs(\n            provider=provider, limit=1)\n    except Exception as e:\n        return False, f\"local-store read failed: {e}\"\n    if not rows:\n        return False, \"not configured\"\n    blob = rows[0].get(\"config_json_encrypted\")\n    if blob is None or (isinstance(blob, (bytes, bytearray)) and len(blob) == 0):\n        return False, \"config blob empty\"\n    return True, None\n\n\n# ── Phase 4: proactive approvals cache_push (epic #1032) ─────────────────────\n# Approvals are now authoritative in local DuckDB — the policy watcher writes\n# the row, the daemon pushes the pending-queue snapshot to the cloud cache on\n# every heartbeat under `approvals:{owner_hash}:queue`, and the cloud Approvals\n# inbox paints from cache (no Cloud SQL row).\n#\n# TTL is short (60s) so the inbox stays close to real time even between\n# heartbeats — acceptance criterion is \"appears in cloud inbox within 2s\",\n# which the cache_push interval (60s default) bounds at the upper end and the\n# next heartbeat overwrites at the lower end. The local store has no pending approvals (the cloud inbox correctly\n        renders empty in that case — no push needed).\n      - Encryption key is unset — we never push plaintext.\n      - The local store import fails — degrade silently.\n\n    The blob shape mirrors `/api/cloud/approvals` (cloud-side list endpoint)\n    so the cloud read path can return the decrypted dict straight to the\n    dashboard JS without translation.\"\"\"\n    enc_key = config.get(\"encryption_key\")\n    if not enc_key:\n        return []\n    api_key = config.get(\"api_key\", \"\")\n    if not api_key:\n        return []\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store\n    except Exception:\n        return []\n    owner_hash = _owner_hash_for_token(api_key)\n    try:\n        store = local_store.get_store(read_only=True)\n        rows = store.query_approvals(\n            owner_hash=owner_hash,\n            status=\"pending\",\n            limit=APPROVALS_CACHE_LIMIT,\n        )\n    except Exception:\n        return []\n    if not rows:\n        return []\n    payload = {\n        \"approvals\": rows,\n        \"count\":     len(rows),\n        \"_source\":   \"local_store\",\n        \"_shape\":    \"approvals_queue\",\n    }\n    try:\n        blob = encrypt_payload(payload, enc_key)\n    except Exception:\n        return []\n    return [{\n        \"key\":    f\"approvals:{owner_hash}:queue\",\n        \"ttl_s\":  APPROVALS_CACHE_TTL_SEC,\n        \"blob\":   blob,\n    }]\n\n\ndef _pending_approvals_count(config: dict) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return count of pending approvals for this node's owner token.\n\n    Added as a plaintext top-level heartbeat field (issue #3303) so the cloud\n    can decide whether to push an FCM/APNs notification without decrypting the\n    E2E-encrypted cache blob. Without this push the\n# cloud Cron modal shows perpetual ``cache_pending`` for every job's run\n# history.  One encrypted blob per distinct job_id; capped at\n# CRON_RUNS_JOB_LIMIT jobs so heartbeat payload size stays bounded.\nCRON_RUNS_CACHE_TTL_SEC = 300   # 5 min — runs change frequently\nCRON_RUNS_JOB_LIMIT = 20        # max distinct jobs per heartbeat\nCRON_RUNS_LIMIT_PER_JOB = 20    # most-recent runs included per job\n\n\ndef _build_cron_runs_cache_pushes(config: dict) -> list:\n    \"\"\"Return heartbeat ``cache_pushes`` entries for cron-run history.\n\n    One entry per distinct ``job_id`` found in the local store, keyed as\n    ``cron_runs:{owner_hash}:{node_id}:{job_id}``.  Returns an empty list\n    when encryption key is absent, the local store is unavailable, or no\n    cron runs have been ingested yet.\n    \"\"\"\n    enc_key = config.get(\"encryption_key\")\n    if not enc_key:\n        return []\n    api_key = config.get(\"api_key\", \"\")\n    if not api_key:\n        return []\n    node_id = config.get(\"node_id\", \"\")\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store\n    except Exception:\n        return []\n    owner_hash = _owner_hash_for_token(api_key)\n    try:\n        store = local_store.get_store(read_only=True)\n        all_runs = store.query_cron_runs(\n            limit=CRON_RUNS_JOB_LIMIT * CRON_RUNS_LIMIT_PER_JOB\n        )\n    except Exception:\n        return []\n    if not all_runs:\n        return []\n    # Group by job_id (query already returns rows ORDER BY started_at DESC).\n    by_job: dict[str, list] = {}\n    for run in all_runs:\n        jid = run.get(\"job_id\") or \"\"\n        if not jid:\n            continue\n        if jid not in by_job:\n            if len(by_job) >= CRON_RUNS_JOB_LIMIT:\n                continue\n            by_job[jid] = []\n        if len(by_job[jid]) < CRON_RUNS_LIMIT_PER_JOB:\n            by_job[jid].append(run)\n    pushes = []\n    for jid, runs in by_job.items():\n        payload = {\n            \"runs\":    runs,\n            \"count\":   len(runs),\n            \"_source\": \"local_store\",\n            \"_shape\":  \"cron_runs\",\n        }\n        try:\n            blob = encrypt_payload(payload, enc_key)\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n        pushes.append({\n            \"key\":   f\"cron_runs:{owner_hash}:{node_id}:{jid}\",\n            \"ttl_s\": CRON_RUNS_CACHE_TTL_SEC,\n            \"blob\":  blob,\n        })\n    return pushes\n\n\n# ── Query Spine P4 (#2990): per-method q/1 proactive cache push ───────────────\n# Pushes each no-required-arg live q/1 shape as its own keyed cache entry\n# alongside the monolith snapshot. {shape: float} last-push unix timestamp\n\n\ndef _build_q1_cache_pushes(config: dict) -> list:\n    \"\"\"Return cache_push entries for all no-required-arg live q/1 shapes.\n\n    Plaintext-classed methods (aggregates, health, runtimes, models) are stored\n    as base64url JSON — the cloud can read them without a decryption key.\n    E2e-classed methods (rollup_sessions) are AES-256-GCM encrypted and are\n    skipped when no encryption key is configured.\n\n    The CI guard in ``tests/test_sync_q1_cache_pushes.py`` asserts that no\n    e2e-classed method is ever pushed without an encryption key (enforcing the\n    trust-class contract declared in ``clawmetry/query_contract.py``).\n    \"\"\"\n    if not os.environ.get(\"CLAWMETRY_QUERY_CACHE_PUSH\", \"\").lower() in (\n        \"1\", \"true\", \"yes\"\n    ):\n        return []\n    api_key = config.get(\"api_key\", \"\")\n    node_id = config.get(\"node_id\", \"\")\n    if not (api_key and node_id):\n        return []\n    enc_key = config.get(\"encryption_key\")\n\n    try:\n        from routes.local_query import _dispatch as _local_dispatch  # They are served\n        # on-demand via _dispatch_pending_queries.\n        if any(v.get(\"required\") for v in spec.get(\"args\", {}).values()):\n            continue\n        # Per-method debounce: skip if we pushed this shape recently.\n        if now - _Q1_LAST_PUSH.get(shape, 0) < _Q1_PUSH_DEBOUNCE_SEC:\n            continue\n        is_e2e = spec[\"trust\"] == TRUST_E2E\n        if is_e2e and not enc_key:\n            continue  # hard guard: never push e2e content without encryption\n        try:\n            payload = _local_dispatch(shape, {})\n            if is_e2e:\n                blob = encrypt_payload(payload, enc_key)\n            else:\n                blob = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(\n                    json.dumps(payload, default=str).encode()\n                ).rstrip(b\"=\").decode()\n            pushes.append({\n                \"key\":   f\"q1:{shape}:{owner_hash}:{node_id}\",\n                \"ttl_s\": Q1_PUSH_CACHE_TTL_SEC,\n                \"blob\":  blob,\n            })\n            _Q1_LAST_PUSH[shape] = now\n        except Exception as _e:\n            log.debug(\"q1 cache push failed for shape=%s: %s\", shape, _e)\n\n    return pushes\n\n\ndef _seal_shared_traces(config: dict, session_ids: list) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Seal each requested session's trace with the ORGANISATION key and upload.\n\n    This is the only path by which one person's session becomes readable by\n    their colleagues, and the key choice is the whole design:\n\n    * With an organisation key, the trace is sealed so every member can open\n      it, and the cloud stores ciphertext it cannot read.\n    * WITHOUT one we upload NOTHING. See issue #599.\nCRON_STATE_HEARTBEAT_SEC = 300  # 5 minutes\n\n\ndef _openclaw_state_sqlite() -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Path to OpenClaw v2026.6.5+ consolidated state DB.\"\"\"\n    return Path(_get_openclaw_dir()) / \"state\" / \"openclaw.sqlite\"\n\n\n# Module-level latch so the migration warning fires at most once per daemon\n# restart — frequent enough to appear in sync.log, never often enough to spam.\n_SQLITE_MIGRATION_WARNED: bool = False\n\n\ndef _warn_sqlite_migration_once() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Emit a one-time WARNING when OpenClaw's state DB exists but there are\n    no transcripts to read from either store (.jsonl files, or the 2026.9.x+\n    SQLite store mirrored by ``clawmetry/openclaw_sqlite.py``). (#6173)\"\"\"\n    global _SQLITE_MIGRATION_WARNED\n    if _SQLITE_MIGRATION_WARNED:\n        return\n    _SQLITE_MIGRATION_WARNED = True\n    log.warning(\n        \"openclaw: no session transcripts found. state/openclaw.sqlite \"\n        \"exists but neither .jsonl files nor a readable \"\n        \"agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite transcript store were \"\n        \"found, so OpenClaw sessions will not appear until one is written.\"\n    )\n\n\ndef _load_jobs_from_state_sqlite() -> list | None:\n    \"\"\"Read cron job definitions from OpenClaw v2026.6.5+ state/openclaw.sqlite.\n\n    Returns a list of job dicts in the same shape as the legacy jobs.json\n    ``jobs`` array, or None when the DB is absent or unreadable.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = _openclaw_state_sqlite()\n    if not db.exists():\n        return None\n    try:\n        import sqlite3\n        conn = sqlite3.connect(f\"file:{db}?mode=ro\", uri=True, timeout=5)\n        try:\n            rows = conn.execute(\"SELECT job_json, state_json FROM cron_jobs\").fetchall()\n        finally:\n            conn.close()\n        jobs: list = []\n        for job_json_str, state_json_str in rows:\n            try:\n                j = json.loads(job_json_str) if job_json_str else {}\n            except Exception:\n                continue\n            if not isinstance(j, dict):\n                continue\n            try:\n                j_state = json.loads(state_json_str) if state_json_str else {}\n            except Exception:\n                j_state = {}\n            # A bare expr string here is what made the\n                    # schedule render as `{}`.\n                    \"schedule\":    json.dumps(sched) if sched else \"\",\n                    \"enabled\":     bool(j.get(\"enabled\", True)),\n                    \"last_run_at\": str(job_state.get(\"lastRunAtMs\") or \"\"),\n                    \"last_status\": str(job_state.get(\"lastStatus\") or \"\"),\n                    \"next_run_at\": str(job_state.get(\"nextRunAtMs\") or \"\"),\n                    # All other freeform fields go into the BLOB\n                    \"task\":        (j.get(\"task\") or \"\")[:500],\n                    \"model\":       (j.get(\"model\") or j.get(\"agentModel\")\n                                   or j.get(\"configuredModel\")),\n                    \"lastDurationMs\":      job_state.get(\"lastDurationMs\"),\n                    \"lastError\":           job_state.get(\"lastError\"),\n                    \"consecutiveFailures\": job_state.get(\"consecutiveFailures\"),\n                    # on-exit trigger / detached-run metadata (openclaw #92037 / #98755)\n                    \"watchedCommand\":      job_state.get(\"watchedCommand\"),\n                    \"lastExitCode\":        job_state.get(\"lastExitCode\") or job_state.get(\"exitCode\"),\n                    \"targetSessionId\":     job_state.get(\"targetSessionId\"),\n                    \"detachedAt\":          job_state.get(\"detachedAt\"),\n                })\n            except Exception as _e:\n                log.debug(\"local_store: ingest_cron failed for %s: %s\",\n                          job_id, _e)\n\n        if events:\n            _post(\"/api/ingest\", {\"events\": events, \"node_id\": node_id}, api_key)\n            # Only record new hashes/timestamps after the POST succeeds so a\n            # transient ingest failure re-emits next cycle.\n            for job_id, job_hash in emitted_job_ids:\n                job_dedup[job_id] = [job_hash, now_ts]\n            state[\"cron_hash\"] = h\n            _record_sync_progress(\"crons\", len(events), len(events))\n            return len(events)\n        elif not file_unchanged:\n            # File mtime/content changed but every job was deduped — still\n            # record the new file hash so we don't re-parse it next tick.\n            state[\"cron_hash\"] = h\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.warning(f\"Cron sync error: {e}\")\n    _record_sync_progress(\"crons\", 0, 0)\n    return 0\n\n\n# ── Cron-run JSONL → DuckDB ingest (issue #605 DuckDB follow-up) ─────────\n#\n# OpenClaw's cron writer appends one JSON record per run to\n# ``~/.openclaw/cron/runs/<jobId>.jsonl``. PR #1147 had the dashboard route\n# parse those files on every request; this helper moves the parse into the\n# sync daemon so the API can read from columnar DuckDB instead.\n#\n# Per-file offset tracking lives under ``state[\"cron_run_offsets\"]`` so the\n# daemon only re-reads new bytes each cycle. Offsets that point past the\n# current file size (post-rotation, truncation) reset to 0 — the\n# ``INSERT OR IGNORE`` on the cron_runs table makes the catch-up scan a\n# no-op for already-stored rows.\n#\n# The function is deliberately resilient: any per-file or per-line failure\n# is logged at debug level and skipped, never raised. ClawMetry is\n# read-only-by-default; a malformed cron jsonl line must not break the\n# rest of the sync cycle.\n\n\ndef _cron_run_dirs() -> list[Path]:\n    \"\"\"Candidate ``cron/runs`` directories, in resolution order. Mirrors\n    ``routes/crons.py:_resolve_cron_runs_jsonl`` so the daemon picks up the\n    same files the API would have read.\n    \"\"\"\n    roots: list[str] = []\n    data_dir = os.environ.get(\"OPENCLAW_DATA_DIR\", \"\").strip()\n    if data_dir:\n        roots.append(os.path.expanduser(data_dir))\n    home = os.environ.get(\"OPENCLAW_HOME\", \"\").strip()\n    if home:\n        roots.append(os.path.expanduser(home))\n    roots.append(_get_openclaw_dir())\n    roots.append(os.path.expanduser(\"~/.clawdbot\"))\n    out: list[Path] = []\n    seen: set[str] = set()\n    for r in roots:\n        p = Path(r) / \"cron\" / \"runs\"\n        rp = str(p)\n        if rp in seen:\n            continue\n        seen.add(rp)\n        if p.exists() and p.is_dir():\n            out.append(p)\n    return out\n\n\ndef _parse_cron_run_line(line: str, job_id: str, node_id: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"Parse one JSONL line into the ``LocalStore.ingest_cron_run`` shape.\n\n    Returns ``None`` on malformed JSON or non-dict payloads. The local\n    store dedups by ``id``; when the writer didn't supply one we\n    synthesise it from ``job_id`` + ``started_at`` so re-reads remain\n    idempotent.\n    \"\"\"\n    line = line.strip()\n    if not line:\n        return None\n    try:\n        obj = json.loads(line)\n    except Exception:\n        return None\n    if not isinstance(obj, dict):\n        return None\n    # Field-name normalisation matches the older\n    # ``routes/crons.py:_read_cron_run_lines`` so OpenClaw writers shipped\n    # by every gateway version round-trip cleanly.\n    started_at = (\n        obj.get(\"started_at\")\n        or obj.get(\"startedAt\")\n        or obj.get(\"ts\")\n        or obj.get(\"timestamp\")\n    )\n    ended_at = obj.get(\"ended_at\") or obj.get(\"endedAt\")\n    duration_ms = obj.get(\"duration_ms\") or obj.get(\"durationMs\") or obj.get(\"duration\")\n    status = obj.get(\"status\") or obj.get(\"result\") or \"unknown\"\n    err = obj.get(\"error\") or obj.get(\"err\") or obj.get(\"error_message\") or \"\"\n    if err and not isinstance(err, str):\n        err = str(err)\n    usage = obj.get(\"usage\") if isinstance(obj.get(\"usage\"), dict) else {}\n    token_count = (\n        obj.get(\"token_count\")\n        or obj.get(\"tokens\")\n        or (usage.get(\"total_tokens\") if isinstance(usage, dict) else None)\n        or (usage.get(\"totalTokens\") if isinstance(usage, dict) else None)\n    )\n    cost_usd = obj.get(\"cost_usd\") or obj.get(\"costUsd\")\n    delivered_at = obj.get(\"delivered_at\") or obj.get(\"deliveredAt\")\n    if not delivered_at and isinstance(obj.get(\"deliveryStatus\"), dict):\n        delivered_at = obj[\"deliveryStatus\"].get(\"deliveredAt\")\n    next_run_at = (\n        obj.get(\"next_run_at\")\n        or obj.get(\"nextRunAt\")\n        or obj.get(\"nextRunAtMs\")\n    )\n    # Coerce timestamps to ISO strings — the DuckDB column is VARCHAR\n    # because the gateway writer hasn't been consistent about epoch-ms\n    # vs ISO-8601 (issue #605 has examples of both). Keeping the column\n    # opaque lets us re-parse on read without a schema change.\n    def _norm_ts(v: Any) -> str | None:\n        if v is None:\n            return None\n        if isinstance(v, (int, float)):\n            return str(int(v))\n        return str(v)\n    rid = obj.get(\"id\") or obj.get(\"run_id\") or obj.get(\"runId\")\n    if not rid:\n        rid = f\"{job_id}:{_norm_ts(started_at) or ''}\"\n    run = {\n        \"id\": str(rid),\n        \"node_id\": node_id,\n        \"job_id\": job_id,\n        \"agent_type\": \"openclaw\",\n        \"started_at\": _norm_ts(started_at),\n        \"ended_at\": _norm_ts(ended_at),\n        \"duration_ms\": duration_ms,\n        \"status\": str(status) if status is not None else None,\n        \"error_message\": err,\n        \"token_count\": token_count,\n        \"cost_usd\": cost_usd,\n        \"delivered_at\": _norm_ts(delivered_at),\n        \"next_run_at\": _norm_ts(next_run_at),\n        \"raw_jsonl_line\": line[:8000],\n        # Preserve the freeform payload (usage dict, gateway extras) so\n        # ``query_cron_runs`` callers can introspect input/output token\n        # splits without losing fidelity.\n        \"usage\": usage,\n    }\n    return run\n\n\ndef sync_cron_runs(config: dict, state: dict, paths: dict) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Ingest new lines from ``~/.openclaw/cron/runs/*.jsonl`` into\n    ``cron_runs`` in the local DuckDB store.\n\n    Returns the number of rows newly ingested. Idempotent: lines already\n    in the table (matched on the synthesised ``id``) are skipped by the\n    ``ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`` clause in ``LocalStore.ingest_cron_run``.\n    Per-file byte offsets are persisted in ``state[\"cron_run_offsets\"]``\n    so subsequent cycles only read appended bytes.\n\n    Failure modes (all degrade silently):\n      * ``local_store`` not importable → return 0, no state mutation.\n      * ``~/.openclaw/cron/runs`` missing → return 0.\n      * Single file unreadable / line malformed → skip that file/line,\n        keep going.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store as _ls\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.debug(\"sync_cron_runs: local_store unavailable: %s\", e)\n        return 0\n\n    try:\n        store = _ls.get_store()\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.debug(\"sync_cron_runs: get_store failed: %s\", e)\n        return 0\n\n    node_id = config.get(\"node_id\", \"\") if isinstance(config, dict) else \"\"\n    offsets: dict = state.setdefault(\"cron_run_offsets\", {})\n    runs_dirs = _cron_run_dirs()\n    if not runs_dirs:\n        # OpenClaw v2026.6.5+ stores run logs in state/openclaw.sqlite\n        return _sync_cron_runs_from_state_sqlite(config, state, store)\n\n    n_ingested = 0\n    for runs_dir in runs_dirs:\n        try:\n            jsonl_files = sorted(runs_dir.glob(\"*.jsonl\"))\n        except OSError:\n            continue\n        for fpath in jsonl_files:\n            try:\n                job_id = fpath.stem  # filename without ``.jsonl``\n                if not job_id:\n                    continue\n                # Per-file offset key includes the parent dir so two\n                # candidate roots don't collide on the same jobId.\n                key = f\"{runs_dir}/{fpath.name}\"\n                last_offset = int(offsets.get(key, 0))\n                try:\n                    size = fpath.stat().st_size\n                except OSError:\n                    continue\n                # Truncation / rotation guard: an offset past EOF means\n                # the file was rewritten — reset to 0 and rely on\n                # INSERT OR IGNORE for dedup.\n                if last_offset > size:\n                    last_offset = 0\n                if last_offset == size:\n                    continue\n                with open(fpath, \"r\", errors=\"replace\") as fh:\n                    fh.seek(last_offset)\n                    for line in fh:\n                        run = _parse_cron_run_line(line, job_id, node_id)\n                        if run is None:\n                            continue\n                        try:\n                            store.ingest_cron_run(run)\n                            n_ingested += 1\n                        except Exception as e_in:\n                            log.debug(\n                                \"sync_cron_runs: ingest failed for %s: %s\",\n                                job_id, e_in,\n                            )\n                    new_offset = fh.tell()\n                offsets[key] = new_offset\n            except Exception as e_f:\n                log.debug(\"sync_cron_runs: file %s failed: %s\", fpath, e_f)\n                continue\n    if n_ingested:\n        log.debug(\"sync_cron_runs: ingested %d new rows\", n_ingested)\n    return n_ingested\n\n\n_RUN_LEDGER_SRC_COLS = (\n    \"task_id\", \"runtime\", \"task_kind\", \"source_id\", \"requester_session_key\",\n    \"owner_key\", \"scope_kind\", \"child_session_key\", \"parent_flow_id\",\n    \"parent_task_id\", \"agent_id\", \"run_id\", \"label\", \"task\", \"status\",\n    \"delivery_status\", \"notify_policy\", \"created_at\", \"started_at\", \"ended_at\",\n    \"last_event_at\", \"cleanup_after\", \"error\", \"progress_summary\",\n    \"terminal_summary\", \"terminal_outcome\",\n)\n\n\ndef _openclaw_task_ledger_paths() -> list[Path]:\n    \"\"\"Candidate locations of OpenClaw's run ledger SQLite, newest layout\n    first. OpenClaw 2026.6.5+/2026.7.x keeps ``task_runs`` (plus\n    ``subagent_runs`` and ``flow_runs``) in the unified\n    ``~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite``; 2026.5.x wrote a standalone\n    ``~/.openclaw/tasks/runs.sqlite``. Both are candidates — the reader\n    ingests from EVERY existing candidate (per-path watermarks, PK upsert)\n    so an install that migrated mid-history loses neither side.\n    \"\"\"\n    oc = Path(_get_openclaw_dir())\n    return [\n        oc / \"state\" / \"openclaw.sqlite\",\n        oc / \"tasks\" / \"runs.sqlite\",\n        Path(\"/root/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite\"),\n        Path(\"/root/.openclaw/tasks/runs.sqlite\"),\n        Path(\"/sandbox/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite\"),\n        Path(\"/sandbox/.openclaw/tasks/runs.sqlite\"),\n    ]\n\n\ndef sync_meeting_transcripts(config: dict, state: dict, paths: dict) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Mirror OpenClaw's meeting transcripts into DuckDB ``meeting_transcripts``.\n\n    OpenClaw 2026.9.3 ships a meeting library: capture a call, and the harness\n    writes ``meeting_transcript_sessions`` / ``_utterances`` / ``_summaries``\n    into the SAME ``~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite`` this module already\n    reads for the run ledger, so this needs no new path discovery and no new\n    permission. Schema read from the shipped harness and from a live store,\n    not from the changelog (#5747).\n\n    Content handling is the whole point of the design. ``transcript_text`` and\n    ``summary_markdown`` are human speech, including speakers who never\n    installed ClawMetry, so they are stored LOCALLY and reach the hosted\n    service only through :func:`seal_meeting_transcript`. Nothing here puts\n    them in a plaintext row.\n\n    Idempotent + incremental on an ``updated_at_ms`` watermark: a meeting\n    still being captured is re-read as its utterance count grows and the row\n    is overwritten, never duplicated.\n\n    Degrades silently: no DB, no meeting tables (a pre-2026.9.3 harness), a\n    locked file or a malformed row each return 0 rather than raising.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store as _ls\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.debug(\"sync_meeting_transcripts: local_store unavailable: %s\", e)\n        return 0\n\n    srcs = [p for p in _openclaw_task_ledger_paths() if p.exists()]\n    if not srcs:\n        return 0\n\n    node_id = config.get(\"node_id\", \"\") if isinstance(config, dict) else \"\"\n    marks = state.setdefault(\"meeting_transcript_watermarks\", {})\n\n    try:\n        store = _ls.get_store()\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.debug(\"sync_meeting_transcripts: get_store failed: %s\", e)\n        return 0\n\n    n = 0\n    for src in srcs:\n        key = str(src)\n        watermark = int(marks.get(key, 0) or 0)\n        try:\n            rows, new_watermark = _read_meeting_transcripts(src, watermark)\n        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n            log.debug(\"sync_meeting_transcripts: read failed for %s (%s)\", src, e)\n            continue\n        for r in rows:\n            try:\n                store.ingest_meeting_transcript(r, node_id=node_id)\n                n += 1\n            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n                log.debug(\"sync_meeting_transcripts: bad row skipped: %s\", e)\n        if new_watermark > watermark:\n            marks[key] = new_watermark\n    return n\n\n\ndef _read_meeting_transcripts(src, watermark: int) -> tuple:\n    \"\"\"Read meeting sessions past ``watermark``, joining their utterances and\n    summary. Returns ``(rows, new_watermark)``.\n\n    Read-only URI open so we never contend with OpenClaw's own writer, and a\n    missing ``meeting_transcript_sessions`` table (any harness before\n    2026.9.3) is a skip rather than an error.\n    \"\"\"\n    import sqlite3\n\n    out: list = []\n    new_watermark = watermark\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(f\"file:{src}?mode=ro\", uri=True, timeout=2.0)\n    try:\n        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n        has = conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' \"\n            \"AND name='meeting_transcript_sessions'\").fetchone()\n        if not has:\n            return [], watermark\n        sessions = conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT session_id, started_at, stopped_at, selector, provider_id, \"\n            \"       title, updated_at_ms \"\n            \"FROM meeting_transcript_sessions \"\n            \"WHERE COALESCE(updated_at_ms, 0) >= ? \"\n            \"ORDER BY COALESCE(updated_at_ms, 0) ASC LIMIT 500\",\n            [watermark],\n        ).fetchall()\n        for srow in sessions:\n            sid = srow[\"session_id\"]\n            if not sid:\n                continue\n            ums = int(srow[\"updated_at_ms\"] or 0)\n            new_watermark = max(new_watermark, ums)\n            speakers, lines, count = set(), [], 0\n            try:\n                for u in conn.execute(\n                    \"SELECT speaker_label, speaker_id, text, final \"\n                    \"FROM meeting_transcript_utterances WHERE session_id = ? \"\n                    \"ORDER BY sequence ASC LIMIT 20000\", [sid],\n                ):\n                    count += 1\n                    who = (u[\"speaker_label\"] or u[\"speaker_id\"] or \"\").strip()\n                    if who:\n                        speakers.add(who)\n                    txt = (u[\"text\"] or \"\").strip()\n                    if txt:\n                        lines.append(f\"{who}: {txt}\" if who else txt)\n            except sqlite3.Error:\n                pass\n            markdown = None\n            try:\n                srow2 = conn.execute(\n                    \"SELECT markdown, utterance_count FROM \"\n                    \"meeting_transcript_summaries WHERE session_id = ? LIMIT 1\",\n                    [sid],\n                ).fetchone()\n                if srow2:\n                    markdown = srow2[\"markdown\"]\n                    count = count or int(srow2[\"utterance_count\"] or 0)\n            except sqlite3.Error:\n                pass\n            out.append({\n                \"session_id\": sid,\n                \"title\": srow[\"title\"],\n                \"provider_id\": srow[\"provider_id\"],\n                \"selector\": srow[\"selector\"],\n                \"started_at\": srow[\"started_at\"],\n                \"stopped_at\": srow[\"stopped_at\"],\n                \"utterance_count\": count,\n                \"speaker_count\": len(speakers),\n                \"duration_ms\": _meeting_duration_ms(srow[\"started_at\"],\n                                                    srow[\"stopped_at\"]),\n                \"summary_markdown\": markdown,\n                \"transcript_text\": \"\\n\".join(lines) or None,\n                \"updated_at_ms\": ums,\n            })\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n    return out, new_watermark\n\n\ndef _meeting_duration_ms(started, stopped) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Milliseconds between two harness timestamps, 0 when either is missing\n    or unparseable. Never raises.\"\"\"\n    if not started or not stopped:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        from datetime import datetime as _dt\n\n        def _p(v):\n            return _dt.fromisoformat(str(v).replace(\"Z\", \"+00:00\"))\n\n        return max(0, int((_p(stopped) - _p(started)).total_seconds() * 1000))\n    except Exception:\n        return 0\n\n\ndef sync_run_ledger(config: dict, state: dict, paths: dict) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Mirror OpenClaw's background-run ledger (``tasks/runs.sqlite``) into\n    the local DuckDB ``run_ledger`` table.\n\n    This is the authoritative record of every background run — sub-agents\n    (``runtime='subagent'``), cron jobs (``runtime='cron'``) and inline\n    CLI/agent turns (``runtime='cli'``) — and is the shared source for the\n    Scheduler lane monitor, the sub-agent fan-out tree and the cron run log.\n\n    Idempotent + incremental: we keep a ``last_event_at`` watermark in\n    ``state['run_ledger_watermark']`` and only re-read rows that advanced\n    since the last cycle (status moves ``running`` -> terminal, so the\n    watermark catches updates as well as inserts). Returns rows ingested.\n\n    Degrades silently: missing ledger, locked DB, or malformed row each\n    return 0 / skip rather than raising (read-only-by-default contract).\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store as _ls\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.debug(\"sync_run_ledger: local_store unavailable: %s\", e)\n        return 0\n\n    srcs = [p for p in _openclaw_task_ledger_paths() if p.exists()]\n    if not srcs:\n        return 0\n\n    node_id = config.get(\"node_id\", \"\") if isinstance(config, dict) else \"\"\n    # Per-path watermarks: the 2026.6.5+ migration moved task_runs from\n    # tasks/runs.sqlite into state/openclaw.sqlite. A single shared watermark\n    # advanced by one DB would skip the other's history, so each source keeps\n    # its own (legacy single watermark is adopted as the default for\n    # backwards compatibility with existing daemon state files).\n    legacy_wm = int(state.get(\"run_ledger_watermark\", 0) or 0)\n    marks = state.setdefault(\"run_ledger_watermarks\", {})\n\n    import sqlite3\n\n    try:\n        store = _ls.get_store()\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.debug(\"sync_run_ledger: get_store failed: %s\", e)\n        return 0\n\n    n = 0\n    for src in srcs:\n        key = str(src)\n        watermark = int(marks.get(key, legacy_wm) or 0)\n        rows: list[dict] = []\n        try:\n            # Read-only URI open so we never contend with OpenClaw's writer.\n            conn = sqlite3.connect(f\"file:{src}?mode=ro\", uri=True, timeout=2.0)\n            try:\n                conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n                # The unified state DB holds many tables; skip a candidate\n                # without task_runs instead of erroring the whole pass.\n                has = conn.execute(\n                    \"SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' \"\n                    \"AND name='task_runs'\").fetchone()\n                if not has:\n                    continue\n                cur = conn.execute(\n                    f\"SELECT {', '.join(_RUN_LEDGER_SRC_COLS)} FROM task_runs \"\n                    \"WHERE COALESCE(last_event_at, ended_at, created_at, 0) >= ? \"\n                    \"ORDER BY COALESCE(last_event_at, ended_at, created_at, 0) ASC \"\n                    \"LIMIT 5000\",  # nosec B608 - column list is the _RUN_LEDGER_SRC_COLS module constant; the watermark is bound\n                    [watermark],\n                )\n                rows = [dict(r) for r in cur.fetchall()]\n            finally:\n                conn.close()\n        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — locked / corrupt / schema drift\n            log.debug(\"sync_run_ledger: read failed for %s (%s)\", src, e)\n            continue\n\n        new_watermark = watermark\n        for r in rows:\n            try:\n                store.ingest_run_ledger_row(r, node_id=node_id)\n                n += 1\n                wm = r.get(\"last_event_at\") or r.get(\"ended_at\") or r.get(\"created_at\") or 0\n                try:\n                    new_watermark = max(new_watermark, int(wm))\n                except (TypeError, ValueError):\n                    pass\n            except Exception as e_in:  # noqa: BLE001\n                log.debug(\"sync_run_ledger: ingest skipped for %s: %s\",\n                          r.get(\"task_id\"), e_in)\n        marks[key] = new_watermark\n    if n:\n        log.debug(\"sync_run_ledger: ingested %d rows across %d source(s)\",\n                  n, len(srcs))\n    return n\n\n\ndef _openclaw_session_key_to_id(index: dict, key: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an OpenClaw session KEY (``agent:main:main``,\n    ``agent:main:subagent:<uuid>``) to the canonical session UUID the\n    sessions/events tables are keyed on. sessions.json maps key -> meta with\n    ``sessionId`` (preferred) or a ``sessionFile`` whose basename is the id.\n    Falls back to the key's uuid tail, then the key itself. Never raises.\"\"\"\n    if not key:\n        return \"\"\n    try:\n        meta = index.get(key) if isinstance(index, dict) else None\n        if isinstance(meta, dict):\n            sid = meta.get(\"sessionId\") or \"\"\n            if sid:\n                return str(sid)\n            sf = os.path.basename(meta.get(\"sessionFile\") or \"\")\n            if sf.endswith(\".jsonl\"):\n                return sf[:-6]\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    tail = key.split(\":\")[-1]\n    return tail or key\n\n\ndef sync_openclaw_subagent_runs(config: dict, state: dict, paths: dict) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Mirror OpenClaw's sub-agent + flow registries into the ``subagents``\n    table with the orchestration facts (prompt / reply / status / parent).\n\n    OpenClaw 2026.6.5+/2026.7.x persists the authoritative record of every\n    delegation in ``~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite``:\n\n      * ``subagent_runs`` — one row per spawned sub-agent, carrying exactly\n        the operator-facing facts the orchestration surfaces render:\n        ``task`` (the context the child was handed → ``prompt``),\n        ``frozen_result_text`` (its final reply → ``reply``), ``label`` /\n        ``task_name``, ``model``, ``spawn_mode``, ``requester_session_key``\n        (the parent), ``created_at``/``started_at``/``ended_at`` and\n        ``ended_reason`` (status). Read-only (SQLite ro URI); every failure degrades to 0.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not _sync_allowed():\n        return 0\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store as _ls\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.debug(\"sync_openclaw_subagent_runs: local_store unavailable: %s\", e)\n        return 0\n\n    db = _openclaw_state_sqlite()\n    if not db.exists():\n        return 0\n\n    # sessions.json index for key -> canonical session id resolution.\n    index: dict = {}\n    try:\n        sessions_dir = paths.get(\"sessions_dir\", \"\") if isinstance(paths, dict) else \"\"\n        index_path = os.path.join(sessions_dir, \"sessions.json\") if sessions_dir else \"\"\n        if index_path and os.path.isfile(index_path):\n            with open(index_path) as _f:\n                index = json.load(_f)\n    except Exception:\n        index = {}\n\n    import sqlite3\n    marks = state.setdefault(\"openclaw_subagent_run_watermarks\", {})\n    now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)\n    rows_sub: list[dict] = []\n    rows_flow: list[dict] = []\n    try:\n        conn = sqlite3.connect(f\"file:{db}?mode=ro\", uri=True, timeout=2.0)\n        try:\n            conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n            names = {r[0] for r in conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'\").fetchall()}\n            if \"subagent_runs\" in names:\n                wm = int(marks.get(\"subagent_runs\", 0) or 0)\n                rows_sub = [dict(r) for r in conn.execute(\n                    \"SELECT run_id, child_session_key, requester_session_key, \"\n                    \"controller_session_key, task, task_name, label, model, \"\n                    \"spawn_mode, created_at, started_at, ended_at, ended_reason, \"\n                    \"outcome_json, frozen_result_text, fallback_frozen_result_text \"\n                    \"FROM subagent_runs \"\n                    \"WHERE COALESCE(ended_at, started_at, created_at, 0) >= ?
