Say so\n        # once rather than escalating on a latch that cannot track rungs.\n        if step > 0:\n            log.warning(\"guard: store predates escalation ladders; step %d of \"\n                        \"policy %s will not fire until the daemon is upgraded\",\n                        step + 1, policy_id)\n            return True\n        return bool(store.policy_already_fired(session_id, policy_id))\n    except Exception:\n        return True\n\n\ndef _ladder_suffix(decision: dict) -> str:\n    \"\"\"`` [step 1/3, then kill in 300s]`` — appended to the guard log line.\n\n    An escalation ladder is the one case where the log needs to say what\n    happens NEXT: reading \"guard: sess-1 pause ok\" gives no hint that a kill\n    is queued behind it.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        count = int(decision.get(\"step_count\") or 1)\n        if count <= 1:\n            return \"\"\n        idx = int(decision.get(\"step_index\") or 0)\n        nxt = str(decision.get(\"next_action\") or \"\")\n        tail = (f\", then {nxt} in {int(decision.get('next_after_secs') or 0)}s\"\n                if nxt else \", final step\")\n        return f\" [step {idx + 1}/{count}{tail}]\"\n    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — a log decoration must never raise\n        return \"\"\n\n\ndef _emit_detector_incidents(store, state: dict) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Run ``clawmetry.detectors`` over each active session, emit each incident\n    as a ``loop_signals`` row (reusing the stuck detector's device-alert path)\n    and fold the highest-severity incident per session into ``_LATEST_STUCK``\n    so the plaintext heartbeat carries it to cloud/device. Deduped per\n    (session, kind) within a re-emit window. Trajectory findings with stable\n    evidence have durable episodes; silence is stale, never recovery.\n    Never raises into the daemon loop. Returns the number of incidents emitted.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import detectors as _det\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.warning(\"detectors: import failed: %s\", e)\n        return 0\n\n    from clawmetry import guard_checks as _checks\n    settings_available = True\n    try:\n        _check_settings = store.list_node_settings()\n        disabled = _checks.disabled_kinds(_check_settings)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        log.warning(\"Guard check settings unavailable: %s\", exc)\n        disabled = set()\n        settings_available = False\n\n    candidates = _candidate_active_sessions(store)\n    # Lifecycle maintenance is independent of alert re-emission and continues\n    # when a session completes. Never make a failed read look like recovery.\n    try:\n        if hasattr(store, \"age_incidents\"):\n            from clawmetry.incident_evidence import reconcile_ended_sessions\n            store.age_incidents()\n            if settings_available:\n                reconcile_ended_sessions(store, {s.get(\"session_id\") for s in candidates},\n                                         disabled=disabled)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        log.warning(\"Incident lifecycle maintenance unavailable: %s\", exc, exc_info=True)\n    if not candidates:\n        return 0\n\n    memo = state.setdefault(\"detector_emit_memo\", {})\n    if not isinstance(memo, dict):\n        memo = {}\n        state[\"detector_emit_memo\"] = memo\n    now = time.time()\n    reemit = max(30, STUCK_MIN_SECONDS // 2)\n\n    heartbeat_items: list[dict] = []\n    # Facts (spend, how long it has been bad, workspace root) are built BEFORE\n    # the loop so a detector can price an incident and judge a path escape on\n    # the same tick it finds it.\n    facts_by_session = _detector_session_facts(candidates, state, now, store=store)\n    # What each runtime loads, and what changed recently (#5947). Once per\n    # tick, not per session: the scopes are shared.\n    inventory_recent = _agent_inventory_pass(store, state, facts_by_session, now)\n    first_seen_memo = state.setdefault(\"detector_first_seen\", {})\n    if not isinstance(first_seen_memo, dict):\n        first_seen_memo = {}\n        state[\"detector_first_seen\"] = first_seen_memo\n    baseline_cache: dict = {}\n    bad_sessions: set = set()\n    emitted = 0\n    all_incidents: list = []\n    # Each session's write actions, for the fleet pass after the loop\n    # (clawmetry/detector_swarm.py). Collected here so the steps are parsed once.\n    fleet_fps: dict = {}\n    # Opt-in capability-gap export (#5412, clawmetry/capability_gaps.py).\n    # None unless CLAWMETRY_CAPGAP_EXPORT_DIR is set, so the default tick\n    # pays one env read. Reads the SAME events this loop already fetched.\n    capgap = None\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import capability_gaps as _capgap\n        capgap = _capgap.Exporter.from_env()\n    except Exception as _ce:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.debug(\"capability gaps: exporter unavailable: %s\", _ce)\n    for s in candidates:\n        sid = s.get(\"session_id\") or \"\"\n        facts = facts_by_session.get(sid) or {}\n        # Derived from the session id, not from agent_type: see\n        # _detector_runtime. Getting this wrong silently merges every runtime\n        # into one cohort.\n        runtime = None\n        try:\n            # A session materialised from received spans names its own\n            # runtime; the id-prefix guess reads ``openclaw`` for it on a Free\n            # install and would file its incident there (AC-OBS-OTG-001.7).\n            from clawmetry.otlp_guard import observe_only_runtime as _oor\n            runtime = _oor(s)\n        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n            runtime = None\n        runtime = runtime or _detector_runtime(sid, s.get(\"agent_type\") or \"\") or None\n        try:\n            if hasattr(store, \"query_incident_window\") and s.get(\"node_id\") and runtime:\n                events = store.query_incident_window(\n                    session_id=sid, node_id=s[\"node_id\"], runtime=runtime,\n                    limit=_det.DETECT_EVENT_WINDOW) or []\n            else:\n                events = store.query_events(session_id=sid, limit=_det.DETECT_EVENT_WINDOW) or []\n        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n            log.warning(\"detectors: query_events failed for %s: %s\", sid, e)\n            continue\n        baseline = _guard_baseline_for(store, baseline_cache, runtime or \"\",\n                                       facts.get(\"agent_id\") or \"\")\n        try:\n            thresholds = _det.resolve_thresholds(runtime or \"\", baseline)\n            steps = _det.normalize_events(events)\n        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n                log.debug(\"capability gaps: observe skipped for %s: %s\", sid, _ce)\n        try:\n            from clawmetry import detector_swarm as _swarm\n            _fps = _swarm.write_fingerprints(steps)\n            if _fps:\n                fleet_fps[sid] = _fps\n        except Exception as _fe:  # noqa: BLE001\n            log.debug(\"detectors: fingerprinting skipped for %s: %s\", sid, _fe)\n\n        inspection_complete = settings_available\n        inspection = {}\n        try:\n            incidents = _det.run_all(events, sid, runtime, facts=facts,\n                                     thresholds=thresholds, steps=steps, inspection=inspection,\n                                     **({\"disabled\": disabled} if disabled else {})) or []\n        except Exception as e:  # seen after each action ran; nothing held it. Say so on the\n            # incident rather than let a Guard row read as prevention\n            # (REQ-OBS-OTG-001).\n            try:\n                from clawmetry import otlp_guard as _og\n                _obs = _og.observation_label(events)\n                if _obs:\n                    for _inc in incidents:\n                        _og.label_incident(_inc, _obs)\n            except Exception as _oe:  # noqa: BLE001\n                log.debug(\"detectors: observation label skipped: %s\", _oe)\n        # Resolve stable evidence while its exact window still exists, and\n        # persist before the notification cooldown can skip a re-emission.\n        episodes = {}\n        try:\n            if hasattr(store, \"record_incident_observation\"):\n                from clawmetry.incident_evidence import reconcile_session\n                nodes = {e.get(\"node_id\") for e in events if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get(\"node_id\")}\n                node_id = s.get(\"node_id\") or (next(iter(nodes)) if len(nodes) == 1 else \"\")\n                if len(nodes) > 1 or (nodes and node_id not in nodes):\n                    log.warning(\"Incident evidence spans multiple nodes; reconciliation withheld\")\n                else:\n                    episodes = reconcile_session(\n                        store, incidents, events, steps, session_id=sid, runtime=runtime or \"\",\n                        node_id=node_id, completed=inspection_complete, disabled=set(disabled) | {k for k, ok in inspection.items() if not ok},\n                        observed_at=int(now * 1000))\n        except Exception as exc:\n            log.warning(\"Incident reconciliation unavailable for %s: %s\", sid, exc, exc_info=True)\n        if incidents:\n            all_incidents.extend(incidents)\n            # Remember when this session FIRST looked wrong, so the next tick\n            # can say how long it has been that way (and price the stretch).\n            # Behavioural incidents only: a poisoned repo is a property of the\n            # FOLDER, not a stretch of the session going off track, and letting\n            # it start the clock would inflate the spend at risk of a real\n            # trajectory incident found later.\n            bad_sessions.add(sid)\n            first_seen_memo.setdefault(sid, now)\n\n        # The workspace surface: what the tool stream cannot see (a poisoned\n        # .git/config, an autorun task, a tampered agent hook). Same shape, same row,\n        # same rule: a policy acts on it only when it names the kind.\n        supply = _agent_inventory_incidents(\n            inventory_recent, sid, runtime or \"unknown\", facts.get(\"cwd\") or \"\", now)\n        if supply and disabled:\n            supply = [i for i in supply if i.get(\"kind\") not in disabled]\n        if supply:\n            all_incidents.extend(supply)\n        incidents = list(incidents) + workspace + supply\n        if not incidents:\n            continue\n\n        # An edited CLAUDE.md is worth a row in Guard, not a line on the desk\n        # device: an info-level inventory finding never rides the heartbeat.\n        if (top in supply and str(top.get(\"severity\") or \"\") == \"info\"):\n            top = None\n        if top is not None:\n            heartbeat_items.append({\n            \"runtime\": str(top.get(\"runtime\") or \"openclaw\"),\n            \"kind\": top.get(\"kind\"),\n            \"tool_calls\": int((top.get(\"evidence\") or {}).get(\"total_tool_calls\")\n                              or (top.get(\"evidence\") or {}).get(\"tool_calls\") or 0),\n            \"since_seconds\": 0,\n            # One\n        # bounded read per tick; the exporter dedups by approval id.\n        try:\n            capgap.observe_approvals(store.query_approvals(status=\"denied\", limit=200) or [])\n        except Exception as _ce:  # noqa: BLE001\n            log.debug(\"capability gaps: approvals skipped: %s\", _ce)\n        try:\n            n_gap = capgap.flush()\n            if n_gap:\n                log.info(\"capability gaps: %d record(s) exported\", n_gap)\n        except Exception as _ce:  # noqa: BLE001\n            log.debug(\"capability gaps: flush skipped: %s\", _ce)\n\n    # A session that recovered drops out of the memo so its \"bad for\" clock\n    # restarts if it goes wrong again later. This also bounds the memo: it can\n    # never grow past the set of currently-bad sessions.\n    for stale_sid in [k for k in first_seen_memo if k not in bad_sessions]:\n        first_seen_memo.pop(stale_sid, None)\n\n    # The baseline is a rolling memory, not an archive. Pruned on a slow clock\n    # (every 6h) rather than per tick: it is a DELETE over a small table and\n    # nothing downstream needs it to be prompt.\n    try:\n        last_prune = float(state.get(\"guard_baseline_pruned_at\") or 0)\n        if (now - last_prune) > _BASELINE_PRUNE_INTERVAL_SEC:\n            state[\"guard_baseline_pruned_at\"] = now\n            dropped = store.prune_guard_baseline()\n            if dropped:\n                log.info(\"guard: pruned %d stale baseline row(s)\", dropped)\n    except Exception as _pe:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.debug(\"guard: baseline prune skipped: %s\", _pe)\n\n    # Fold detector incidents into the heartbeat slice WITHOUT clobbering a\n    # fresh stuck-detector result: only append (the stuck detector owns the\n    # self-clear refresh). When the stuck cache is stale, replace it.\n    try:\n        if heartbeat_items:\n            if (now - float(_LATEST_STUCK.get(\"ts\") or 0)) < _STUCK_HEARTBEAT_FRESH_SECONDS:\n                existing = list(_LATEST_STUCK.get(\"items\") or [])\n                existing.extend(heartbeat_items)\n                _LATEST_STUCK[\"items\"] = existing[:_STUCK_HEARTBEAT_MAX_ITEMS]\n            else:\n                _LATEST_STUCK[\"items\"] = heartbeat_items[:_STUCK_HEARTBEAT_MAX_ITEMS]\n            _LATEST_STUCK[\"ts\"] = now\n    except Exception as _ce:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.debug(\"detectors: heartbeat fold failed (continuing): %s\", _ce)\n\n    # Bound memo growth: drop entries not touched in an hour.\n    try:\n        for k in [k for k, v in memo.items()\n                  if not (isinstance(v, (int, float)) and (now - v) < 3600)]:\n            memo.pop(k, None)\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    # The fleet question: are sessions that should be independent acting in\n    # step? One pass per tick over every session's write actions, after the\n    # per-session pass, so its incidents reach the same policy pass below.\n    try:\n        if \"coordinated_action\" not in disabled:\n            all_incidents.extend(_emit_fleet_incidents(store, state, fleet_fps, now))\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.warning(\"detectors: fleet pass failed: %s\", e)\n\n    # Guard policies: turn this tick's incidents into at most one enforcement\n    # decision per session. Isolated from the emit path above — a policy\n    # failure must never stop telemetry ingest.\n    try:\n        if all_incidents:\n            _apply_guard_policies(store, state, all_incidents, facts_by_session)\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.warning(\"guard: policy pass failed: %s\", e)\n\n    try:\n        store.set_node_setting(_checks.LAST_PASS_KEY, int(time.time() * 1000))\n    except Exception as exc:\n        log.debug(\"Guard check pass timestamp unavailable: %s\", exc)\n    return emitted\n\n\ndef _emit_fleet_incidents(store, state: dict, fleet_fps: dict, now: float) -> list:\n    \"\"\"Run ``coordinated_action`` over this tick's write actions.\n\n    One human message per fingerprint, however many sessions share it: forty\n    pages about one swarm get muted, one page with a count gets read. Each\n    participating session still gets its own ``loop_signals`` row, so the\n    Guard tab shows the finding on every row it concerns and a policy that\n    names ``coordinated_action`` can act per session.\n\n    Returns the per-session copies for the policy pass. Never raises.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not fleet_fps:\n        return []\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import detector_swarm as _swarm\n        keys = sorted({_swarm.fingerprint_key(fp)\n                       for fps in fleet_fps.values() for fp in fps})\n        hist = store.query_action_fingerprints(keys=keys) or {}\n        parents = store.query_subagent_parents(session_ids=sorted(fleet_fps)) or {}\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.debug(\"detectors: fleet pass inputs unavailable: %s\", e)\n        return []\n\n    incidents = _swarm.coordinated_action(\n        fleet_fps, parents=parents, history=hist.get(\"first_seen\") or {},\n        history_since_ms=hist.get(\"since\"), now=now)\n\n    # Remember what was seen, AFTER judging it, so this tick's burst is judged\n    # against the memory from before it.\n    try:\n        seen: dict = {}\n        for sid, fps in fleet_fps.items():\n            for fp in fps:\n                seen.setdefault(_swarm.fingerprint_key(fp), [tuple(fp), set()])[1].add(sid)\n        store.record_action_fingerprints(fingerprints=[\n            (k, fp[0], fp[1], fp[2], len(sids)) for k, (fp, sids) in sorted(seen.items())])\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.debug(\"detectors: fingerprint memory write failed: %s\", e)\n\n    memo = state.setdefault(\"detector_emit_memo\", {})\n    if not isinstance(memo, dict):\n        memo = {}\n        state[\"detector_emit_memo\"] = memo\n    reemit = max(30, STUCK_MIN_SECONDS // 2)\n    out: list = []\n    for inc in incidents:\n        base = {k: v for k, v in inc.items() if k != \"participants\"}\n        key = str((inc.get(\"evidence\") or {}).get(\"fingerprint_key\") or \"\")\n        delivered_via: list = []\n        try:\n            from clawmetry import incident_alerts as _ia\n            res = _ia.deliver_incident(\n                store, dict(base, session_id=\"fleet:\" + key[:100]), source=\"fleet_detector\")\n            delivered_via = list(res.get(\"delivered_via\") or [])\n        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n            log.debug(\"detectors: fleet alert delivery skipped: %s\", e)\n        for sid in list(inc.get(\"participants\") or [])[:200]:\n            per = dict(base, session_id=sid,\n                       runtime=_detector_runtime(sid, \"\") or \"unknown\")\n            out.append(per)\n            memo_key = f\"{sid}::coordinated_action\"\n            last = memo.get(memo_key)\n            if isinstance(last, (int, float)) and (now - last) < reemit:\n                continue\n            try:\n                store.ingest_loop_signal(\n                    session_id=sid,\n                    signature=\"daemon_detect_coordinated_action\",\n                    repeat_count=_DETECT_SEVERITY_COUNT.get(\"warning\", 5),\n                    severity=\"warning\",\n                    agent_type=str(per[\"runtime\"]),\n                    details={\n                        \"source\": \"daemon_fleet_detector\",\n                        \"kind\": \"coordinated_action\",\n                        \"message\": per.get(\"title\"),\n                        \"detail\": per.get(\"detail\"),\n                        \"evidence\": per.get(\"evidence\"),\n                        \"first_bad_step\": None,\n                        \"spend_at_risk_usd\": None,\n                        \"spend_basis\": \"unknown\",\n                        \"delivered_via\": delivered_via,\n                        \"frameworks\": per.get(\"frameworks\"),\n                    },\n                )\n                memo[memo_key] = now\n                log.info(\"detectors: %s\", per.get(\"title\"))\n            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n                log.warning(\"detectors: fleet loop_signal failed for %s: %s\", sid, e)\n    return out\n\n\n# ── Per-session loops slice (Command River Phase-2) ─────────────────────────\n# The desk device's deviceSummary.alert (and the heartbeat `stuck` payload)\n# carries the loudest single incident's *banner text* but STRIPS the\n# session_id, so the cloud Command River cannot bind a red \"whirlpool\" + the\n# Kill/Pause alarm to the EXACT looping sub-agent lane. This slice fixes that:\n# a small, bounded, plaintext `loops[]` array where every entry CARRIES the\n# canonical session_id the river keys lanes on. It is sourced for free from\n# the loop_signals rows the detector/stuck pass already wrote (no recompute,\n# no extra DuckDB scan beyond one indexed read) and is self-clearing: a\n# session that stops looping simply ages out of the 30-min loop_signals window\n# and drops from the slice (mirrors the device alert's self-clear).\n#\n# Trust class: this is the SAME exposure as the already-shipped\n# deviceSummary.alert — aggregate metadata (session id + a short plain-words\n# title + counts). Titles are the detector's plain-words summary (e.g.\n# \"codex looping: 6x identical Bash calls\"); the per-session encrypted brain\n# feed carries the real content. Honesty: only rows a detector GENUINELY\n# wrote appear here — never synthesized.\n_LOOPS_SLICE_MAX = int(os.environ.get(\"CLAWMETRY_LOOPS_SLICE_MAX\", \"12\"))\n# loop_signals signatures whose details.kind we trust as a real loop/stuck\n# incident. Detector rows are \"daemon_detect_<kind>\"; the no-progress stuck\n# detector writes \"daemon_stuck\"; the proxy LoopDetector writes a request-hash\n# signature (a genuine loop too). We surface all of them.\n_LOOPS_KIND_BY_SIGNATURE = {\n    \"daemon_stuck\": \"stuck_loop\",\n    \"daemon_detect_stuck_loop\": \"stuck_loop\",\n    \"daemon_detect_no_progress\": \"no_progress\",\n    \"daemon_detect_repeated_tool_failure\": \"repeated_tool_failure\",\n    \"daemon_detect_action_discrepancy\": \"action_discrepancy\",\n    # The silent-failure kinds (rate_limited / blocked_on_user / crashed) are\n    # deliberately NOT here: this slice is the device's LOOP river. They reach\n    # people through incident_alerts and the Guard tab (which reads\n    # details.kind directly), not through a whirlpool glyph.\n}\n_LOOPS_VALID_KINDS = frozenset(_LOOPS_KIND_BY_SIGNATURE.values())\n\n\n#: Repo AI-readiness snapshot slice (WO-5). The hosted dashboard has no\n#: filesystem to scan -- the cloud container never sees the user's repos -- so\n#: the DAEMON scores them here and ships the finished report. Capped hard:\n#: five reports at roughly 3 kB each is a rounding error next to the snapshot,\n#: and a 200-repo machine must not be able to inflate it.\n_READINESS_SLICE_MAX = int(os.environ.get(\"CLAWMETRY_READINESS_SLICE_MAX\", \"5\"))\n_READINESS_WINDOW_DAYS = int(os.environ.get(\"CLAWMETRY_READINESS_DAYS\", \"30\"))\n\n\ndef _build_repo_readiness_slice(store):\n    \"\"\"Score the repos this node's agents actually work in.\n\n    Returns ``{\"windowDays\": n, \"scope\": \"all_runtimes\", \"repos\": [...]}``\n    where each repo carries its readiness report AND the stuck-signal\n    pairing. ``scope`` is load-bearing: the daemon scores against EVERY\n    runtime's declared instruction files because it cannot know which\n    runtime the viewer has selected, so a hosted renderer must label this\n    \"all runtimes\" rather than presenting it as runtime-scoped.\n\n    Repos that no longer exist on disk are listed (their history is real)\n    but carry ``report: None`` -- there is nothing left to read, and an\n    invented grade for a deleted checkout is worse than an honest gap.\n\n    Never raises: an empty slice paints the honest \"nothing scored yet\"\n    state rather than breaking the snapshot.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import repo_readiness\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.debug(\"readiness-slice: module unavailable: %s\", e)\n        return {}\n    try:\n        rows = store.query_repo_activity(\n            since_days=_READINESS_WINDOW_DAYS, limit=5000) or []\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.debug(\"readiness-slice: query_repo_activity failed: %s\", e)\n        return {}\n\n    ranked = repo_readiness.rank_repos(\n        rows, window_days=_READINESS_WINDOW_DAYS, limit=_READINESS_SLICE_MAX)\n    out = []\n    for repo in ranked:\n        entry = {\n            \"path\": repo[\"path\"],\n            \"name\": repo[\"name\"],\n            \"exists\": repo[\"exists\"],\n            \"lastActiveAt\": repo[\"last_active_at\"],\n            \"signals\": repo[\"signals\"],\n            \"report\": None,\n        }\n        if repo[\"exists\"]:\n            try:\n                entry[\"report\"] = repo_readiness.score_repo(\n                    repo[\"path\"], signals=repo[\"signals\"])\n            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n                log.debug(\"readiness-slice: score failed for %s: %s\",\n                          repo[\"path\"], e)\n        out.append(entry)\n    if not out:\n        return {}\n    return {\n        \"windowDays\": _READINESS_WINDOW_DAYS,\n        \"scope\": \"all_runtimes\",\n        \"repos\": out,\n    }\n\n\ndef _build_loops_slice(store):\n    \"\"\"Build the bounded, plaintext ``loops[]`` snapshot slice from the loop\n    signals the detector/stuck pass already wrote.\n\n    Each entry carries the CANONICAL ``session_id`` (exactly the id the\n    detector ran on, which is the id ``query_sessions_table`` reports and the\n    same form the river's ``subagents[].parent`` ids take) so the cloud\n    Command River can bind a whirlpool + Kill/Pause alarm to the exact lane.\n\n    Shape per entry::\n\n        {\n          \"session_id\":       str,   # canonical bare-or-prefixed id\n          \"kind\":             \"stuck_loop\"|\"no_progress\"|\n                              \"repeated_tool_failure\"|\"action_discrepancy\",\n          \"title\":            str,   # plain-words incident text (device-equiv)\n          \"count\":            int,   # loop repeat / tool-call / failure count\n          \"first_bad_step_ts\": str|None,  # ISO ts the loop began (first_seen)\n          \"since\":            str|None,    # alias of first_bad_step_ts\n          \"severity\":         \"warning\"|\"info\",\n          \"runtime\":          str,\n        }\n\n    Sourced from ``query_recent_loop_signals`` (one indexed read, 30-min\n    self-clearing window) — NO recompute. Returns a list capped at\n    ``_LOOPS_SLICE_MAX``, newest-loop first, deduped per session (highest\n    repeat_count wins). Never raises — returns ``[]`` on any error so the\n    river falls back to its honest no-whirlpool default.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        sigs = store.query_recent_loop_signals(limit=50, since_minutes=30) or []\n    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n        log.debug(\"loops-slice: query_recent_loop_signals failed: %s\", e)\n        return []\n\n    out: list[dict] = []\n    seen: dict[str, int] = {}  # session_id -> index in `out` (dedupe)\n    for s in sigs:\n        if not isinstance(s, dict):\n            continue\n        sid = str(s.get(\"session_id\") or \"\").strip()\n        if not sid:\n            continue  # CRITICAL: a loop with no session id cannot bind a lane.\n        signature = str(s.get(\"signature\") or \"\")\n        det = s.get(\"details\")\n        if isinstance(det, str):\n            try:\n                det = json.loads(det)\n            except Exception:\n                det = None\n        det = det if isinstance(det, dict) else {}\n\n        # Resolve the kind: trust details.kind when it names a known detector\n        # class, else map by signature, else (proxy request-hash signature)\n        # fall back to the generic loop class. Skip anything we can't classify\n        # as a real loop/stuck incident — never synthesize.\n        kind = str(det.get(\"kind\") or \"\").strip()\n        if kind not in _LOOPS_VALID_KINDS:\n            kind = _LOOPS_KIND_BY_SIGNATURE.get(signature, \"\")\n        if not kind:\n            # Proxy LoopDetector rows carry a request-hash signature (not in the\n            # map) but are a genuine loop — classify as stuck_loop.\n            kind = \"stuck_loop\" if signature else \"\"\n        if kind not in _LOOPS_VALID_KINDS:\n            continue\n\n        try:\n            count = int(s.get(\"repeat_count\") or 0)\n        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n            count = 0\n\n        # Title: prefer the detector's plain-words message (device-equivalent\n        # exposure); else a generic kind+count line (keeps content out when we\n        # are unsure — honesty invariant #3).\n        title = str(det.get(\"message\") or \"\").strip()\n        runtime = str(s.get(\"agent_type\") or det.get(\"runtime\") or \"\").strip()\n        if not title:\n            rt = runtime or \"an agent\"\n            if kind == \"no_progress\":\n                title = f\"{rt}: {count} tool calls, not advancing\"\n            elif kind == \"repeated_tool_failure\":\n                title = f\"{rt}: a tool failed {count} times\"\n            elif kind == \"action_discrepancy\":\n                title = f\"{rt} continued after a failed command\"\n            else:\n                title = f\"{rt} looping, {count} repeats, no progress\"\n        title = title[:160]\n\n        first_seen = s.get(\"first_seen\")\n        first_bad = first_seen if isinstance(first_seen, str) and first_seen else None\n\n        entry = {\n            \"session_id\": sid,\n            \"kind\": kind,\n            \"title\": title,\n            \"count\": count,\n            \"first_bad_step_ts\": first_bad,\n            \"since\": first_bad,\n            \"severity\": str(s.get(\"severity\") or \"warning\"),\n            \"runtime\": runtime or \"openclaw\",\n        }\n\n        prev = seen.get(sid)\n        if prev is not None:\n            # One whirlpool per session: keep the loudest (highest count).\n            if count > int(out[prev].get(\"count\") or 0):\n                out[prev] = entry\n            continue\n        seen[sid] = len(out)\n        out.append(entry)\n        if len(out) >= _LOOPS_SLICE_MAX:\n            break\n    return out\n\n\ndef _device_question_set(row: dict) -> list:\n    \"\"\"The approval's question set (``args._cm_questions``, stored by the\n    hook receiver from Claude Code's AskUserQuestion), trimmed for the\n    snapshot: what a surface needs to render the options and nothing else.\n    Empty when the approval is an ordinary yes/no request.\"\"\"\n    args = row.get(\"args\") if isinstance(row.get(\"args\"), dict) else {}\n    out = []\n    for q in (args.get(\"_cm_questions\") or [])[:4]:\n        if not isinstance(q, dict) or not q.get(\"question\"):\n            continue\n        options = [\n            {\"label\": str(o.get(\"label\"))[:120],\n             \"description\": str(o.get(\"description\") or \"\")[:240]}\n            for o in (q.get(\"options\") or [])[:4]\n            if isinstance(o, dict) and o.get(\"label\")\n        ]\n        if not options:\n            continue\n        out.append({\n            \"question\": str(q.get(\"question\"))[:400],\n            \"header\": str(q.get(\"header\") or \"\")[:40],\n            \"multiSelect\": bool(q.get(\"multiSelect\")),\n            \"allow_free_text\": bool(q.get(\"allow_free_text\")),\n            \"options\": options,\n        })\n    return out\n\n\ndef _build_device_summary(spending, daily_usage, efficiency=None):\n    \"\"\"Compact, all-runtime payload for a WiFi hardware companion.\n\n    Mirrors ``routes/device.py``'s ``/api/device/snapshot`` but built on the\n    daemon's OWN store handle (never a ``read_only`` re-open — FLYWHEEL §1) so\n    it rides the E2E-encrypted snapshot to cloud. The device GETs the snapshot,\n    decrypts with the user's key, and reads this one small slice — the cloud\n    never sees plaintext (E2E invariant preserved). Approve/Deny is wired (the\n    daemon owns the approvals queue), ``alert`` is sourced from the daemon's\n    loop-detection signals, and ``approval.waiting_seconds`` from the approval's\n    ``created_at`` -- the device reads all three, so they must be populated here.\n\n    Schema 2 adds a per-runtime ``runtimes`` array (cost / tokens / session\n    count per active runtime, costliest first) alongside the names-only\n    ``runtimes_active``; every schema-1 field is preserved (additive only).\n\n    Never raises — every read degrades to a safe default so the device always\n    gets a valid shape.\n    \"\"\"\n    summary = {\n        # schema 2 adds the per-runtime ``runtimes`` array (cost/tokens/\n        # sessions per active runtime). Every schema-1 field is kept\n        # unchanged for back-compat -- the addition is purely additive and\n        # the firmware tolerates unknown fields, so an older device that\n        # only reads schema-1 keys keeps working.\n        \"schema\": 2,\n        \"cost_today_usd\": round(float((spending or {}).get(\"today\") or 0.0), 4),\n        \"tokens_today\": int((daily_usage or {}).get(\"today\") or 0),\n        \"active_sessions\": 0,\n        \"runtimes_active\": [],\n        \"runtimes\": [],\n        \"health\": \"green\",\n        \"alert\": None,\n        \"approval\": None,\n    }\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store as _ls\n        store = _ls.get_store()\n    except Exception:\n        return summary\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import waste_flags as _wf\n        rows = store.query_sessions_table(limit=300) or []\n        active = [s for s in rows\n                  if isinstance(s, dict) and s.get(\"status\") == \"active\"]\n        summary[\"active_sessions\"] = len(active)\n        summary[\"runtimes_active\"] = sorted({\n            (_wf.runtime_from_session_id(s.get(\"session_id\") or \"\") or \"openclaw\")\n            for s in active\n        })\n        # schema 2: per-runtime spend/tokens/session-count. Group the same\n        # active rows by runtime (session_id prefix) and sum the cost_usd +\n        # total_tokens that query_sessions_table already resolves (it\n        # GREATEST()s the stored column with the events SUM). Guarded\n        # separately so a grouping error degrades to the names-only\n        # ``runtimes_active`` above rather than dropping the whole slice.\n        try:\n            agg: dict = {}\n            for s in active:\n                name = (\n                    _wf.runtime_from_session_id(s.get(\"session_id\") or \"\")\n                    or \"openclaw\"\n                )\n                bucket = agg.setdefault(\n                    name, {\"cost\": 0.0, \"tokens\": 0, \"sessions\": 0}\n                )\n                try:\n                    bucket[\"cost\"] += float(s.get(\"cost_usd\") or 0.0)\n                except (TypeError, ValueError):\n                    pass\n                try:\n                    bucket[\"tokens\"] += int(s.get(\"total_tokens\") or 0)\n                except (TypeError, ValueError):\n                    pass\n                bucket[\"sessions\"] += 1\n            summary[\"runtimes\"] = [\n                {\n                    \"name\": name,\n                    \"cost_today_usd\": round(b[\"cost\"], 4),\n                    \"tokens_today\": b[\"tokens\"],\n                    \"sessions\": b[\"sessions\"],\n                    # An active runtime is healthy here; a stuck approval is\n                    # surfaced separately on the top-level ``health`` field.\n                    \"health\": \"green\",\n                }\n                # Highest spend first so the device shows the costliest\n                # runtime at the top.\n                for name, b in sorted(\n                    agg.items(),\n                    key=lambda kv: (-kv[1][\"cost\"], kv[0]),\n                )\n            ]\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n        # schema 2 (additive): per-runtime tools for the LEGACY encrypted\n        # slice path (the live device path is the heartbeat -> cloud\n        # device_summary; see _runtime_tools_payload).\n        try:\n            _rtt = _runtime_tools_payload(store)\n            if _rtt:\n                summary[\"runtime_tools\"] = _rtt\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n        # schema 2: per-session titles for the device's runtime-detail recent\n        # -sessions rows. The title is the session's FIRST USER MESSAGE (real\n        # content, e.g. \"read flywheel.md ...\"), so it rides the ENCRYPTED\n        # deviceSummary (decrypted on-device) and NEVER the plaintext\n        # device-agent endpoint -- raw content never leaves the daemon in the\n        # clear (the cloud only ever stores an empty display_name for these).\n        # The firmware looks each recent-session row up here by its BARE session\n        # id (post-':' so it matches the device-agent rows) and falls back to a\n        # short id when absent. Keyed by bare id, capped + truncated to keep the\n        # ~8s-polled summary small. ``rows`` is already last_active DESC.\n        try:\n            titles: dict = {}\n            for s in rows:\n                if not isinstance(s, dict):\n                    continue\n                t = (s.get(\"title\") or \"\").strip()\n                if not t:\n                    continue\n                bare = str(s.get(\"session_id\") or \"\").rsplit(\":\", 1)[-1]\n                if bare and bare not in titles:\n                    titles[bare] = t[:56]\n                if len(titles) >= 40:\n                    break\n            if titles:\n                summary[\"sessionTitles\"] = titles\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import waste_flags as _wf\n        now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)\n        # Only requests something is still waiting on. Read the body without assuming either.\n    body = \"\"\n    try:\n        raw_body = getattr(rec, \"body\", None)\n        has_field = getattr(rec, \"HasField\", None)\n        if callable(has_field):\n            raw_body = rec.body if has_field(\"body\") else None\n        if raw_body is not None:\n            try:\n                body = _otel_attr_value(raw_body)\n            except Exception:\n                body = str(raw_body)\n    except Exception:\n        body = \"\"\n    parts = [\n        str(service_name or \"\"), str(session_id or \"\"), str(event_name or \"\"),\n        str(getattr(rec, \"time_unix_nano\", 0) or 0),\n        str(getattr(rec, \"observed_time_unix_nano\", 0) or 0),\n        str(body),\n    ]\n    try:\n        for k in sorted(attrs):\n            parts.append(\"%s=%s\" % (k, attrs[k]))\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    joined = \"\\x1f\".join(parts).encode(\"utf-8\", \"replace\")\n    return hashlib.sha256(joined).hexdigest()[:32]\n\n\ndef _delegated_is_agent_id(value) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when an OTLP conversation id is a delegated vendor agent id.\n\n    Import is late and failure is False: the delegated-usage module is part of\n    the OSS package, but an ingest path must not start refusing records because\n    an optional import moved.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry.delegated_usage import is_delegated_agent_id\n        return is_delegated_agent_id(value)\n    except Exception:\n        return False\n\n\ndef _delegated_record_otel(agent_id, tin, tout, cache_read, cache_write,\n                           model=\"\", ts=0.0) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"File one Cursor cloud-agent OTel record against its agent id.\n\n    ``require_observed`` stays ON: a team's export carries every agent on the\n    Cursor team, and only the ones a transcript on THIS machine actually named\n    may be attributed here. Without that bound a colleague's agent would appear\n    on your session.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry.delegated_usage import (\n            SOURCE_OTEL, CURSOR, DelegatedUsage, get_store,\n        )\n\n        def _n(v):\n            try:\n                return int(v) if v is not None else 0\n            except (TypeError, ValueError):\n                return 0\n\n        usage = DelegatedUsage(\n            agent_id=str(agent_id),\n            vendor=CURSOR,\n            source=SOURCE_OTEL,\n            input_tokens=_n(tin),\n            output_tokens=_n(tout),\n            cache_read_tokens=_n(cache_read),\n            cache_write_tokens=_n(cache_write),\n            model=str(model or \"\"),\n            updated_at=float(ts or 0.0) or 0.0,\n        )\n        if usage.total_tokens <= 0:\n            return False\n        return get_store().record(usage)\n    except Exception:\n        return False\n\n\ndef _process_otlp_logs(pb_data, content_encoding=None, content_type=None, runtime=None, env=None):\n    \"\"\"Decode OTLP logs protobuf and ingest agent EVENT records (#2596, WO-7).\n\n    Claude Code and Codex export their per-turn event stream as OTel *logs* —\n    ``event_name`` like ``claude_code.api_request`` / ``tool_decision`` with\n    cost/token/model attributes. This handler is the daemon-free intake path:\n    an org points OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT here and gets observability with\n    nothing installed per machine.\n\n    Three destinations, in order of durability:\n\n    1. **DuckDB ``otlp_records``** — the durable ledger. One row per record\n       with the identity the runtime already sends (``user.id``,\n       ``user.email``, ``organization.id``, ``session.id``) plus the rollup\n       dimensions an org adds through ``OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES``\n       (``team.id``, repository). Without them a cloud agent\n                        # exporting standard semconv had its cached tokens\n                        # dropped here too (#5685).\n                        c_cr = _f(\n                            attrs, \"cursor.api.request.cache_read_tokens\",\n                            \"cursor.cache_read_tokens\", \"cache_read_tokens\",\n                            \"gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens\",\n                            \"gen_ai.usage.cache_read_input_tokens\",\n                        )\n                        c_cw = _f(\n                            attrs, \"cursor.api.request.cache_creation_tokens\",\n                            \"cursor.cache_write_tokens\", \"cache_creation_tokens\",\n                            \"gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens\",\n                            \"gen_ai.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens\",\n                        )\n                        if any(v is not None for v in (c_in, c_out, c_cr, c_cw)):\n                            _delegated_record_otel(\n                                session_id, c_in, c_out, c_cr, c_cw, model, ts,\n                            )\n                    except Exception:\n                        pass\n\n                dur = _f(attrs, \"duration_ms\", \"duration.ms\")\n                dur_val = None\n                if dur is not None:\n                    try:\n                        dur_val = float(dur)\n                    except (TypeError, ValueError):\n                        dur_val = None\n                if dur_val is not None and fresh and any(\n                    k in suffix for k in (\"request\", \"run\", \"completion\")\n                ):\n                    _add_metric(\"runs\", {\n                        \"timestamp\": ts, \"duration_ms\": dur_val,\n                        \"model\": model, \"channel\": channel,\n                    })\n\n                # ── Fix 3: persist, rather than only caching in memory ───\n                out_records.append({\n                    \"record_id\": record_id,\n                    \"ts\": ts,\n                    \"received_at\": received_at,\n                    \"event_name\": event_name or suffix or \"log\",\n                    \"session_id\": ledger_session_id,\n                    \"user_id\": user_id,\n                    \"user_email\": user_email,\n                    \"org_id\": org_id,\n                    \"team\": team,\n                    \"repo\": repo,\n                    \"node_id\": node_id,\n                    \"agent_type\": agent_type,\n                    \"service_name\": service_name,\n                    \"model\": model or None,\n                    \"provider\": provider or None,\n                    \"cost_usd\": cost_val,\n                    \"tokens_input\": tin,\n                    \"tokens_output\": tout,\n                    \"token_count\": (\n                        (tin or 0) + (tout or 0) if has_tokens else None\n                    ),\n                    \"duration_ms\": dur_val,\n                    \"tool_name\": tool_name,\n                    \"decision\": decision,\n                    \"success\": success,\n                    \"attributes\": {\n                        \"resource\": resource_attrs,\n                        \"record\": attrs,\n                        \"repo_raw\": repo_raw,\n                    },\n                })\n\n                if not session_id:\n                    # Last resort: try docker exec\n    try:\n        result = _gw_invoke_docker(\"session_status\", {}, token)\n        if result:\n            return \"docker://localhost:18789\"  # sentinel value indicating docker mode\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    return None\n\n\n# (bp_auth handlers moved to routes/meta.py: /api/auth/check, /auth, /)\n\n\n@app.before_request\ndef _latency_probe_start():\n    \"\"\"Issue #1283: per-endpoint p50/p95 timing for /api/handler-latency.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        from flask import g\n        import time as _t\n        g._lat_start = _t.perf_counter()\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n\n\n@app.after_request\ndef _latency_probe_record(response):\n    try:\n        from flask import g, request\n        import time as _t\n        start = getattr(g, \"_lat_start\", None)\n        path = request.path or \"\"\n        if start is not None and path.startswith(\"/api/\"):\n            elapsed_ms = (_t.perf_counter() - start) * 1000.0\n            from clawmetry import latency_tracker as _lt\n            _lt.record(request.endpoint or path, elapsed_ms)\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    return response\n\n\n# Bodies bigger than this are left alone: the rewrite below exists for the\n# unreachable case, where a handler has almost nothing to say. A multi-MB\n# payload means the store answered.\n_STORE_FLAG_MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024\n\n\n@app.after_request\ndef _stamp_store_available(response):\n    \"\"\"Say so when a read in this request could not reach the local store.\n\n    Issue #5534: a daemon-proxy timeout ends as ``None`` in the handler and\n    renders as an EMPTY tab — \"no sessions have a transcript yet\" under a\n    header counting 61, ``{\"models\": []}`` over a store holding thousands.\n    An empty state is a positive claim about the user's own work; when the\n    truth is \"I could not read it\", that claim is false and reads exactly\n    like data loss.\n\n    The Cost and Efficiency Analytics blueprint already specifies the field\n    (``store_available``) and a handful of endpoints set it themselves. Silence stays silence: a handler that already\n    reports the fact keeps its own value, and a request where nothing failed\n    is untouched, so no existing response shape or snapshot test moves.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        from routes.local_query import store_available as _store_available\n        if _store_available():\n            return response\n        path = request.path or \"\"\n        if not (path.startswith(\"/api/\") or path.startswith(\"/v1/\")):\n            return response\n        # The header is the cheap universal signal: the frontend's banner\n        # reads it without paying to clone and parse every response body.\n        response.headers[\"X-CM-Store-Available\"] = \"false\"\n        if response.direct_passthrough or response.is_streamed:\n            return response\n        if (response.mimetype or \"\") != \"application/json\":\n            return response\n        raw = response.get_data()\n        if not raw or len(raw) > _STORE_FLAG_MAX_BYTES:\n            return response\n        body = json.loads(raw.decode(\"utf-8\"))\n        if not isinstance(body, dict) or \"store_available\" in body:\n            return response\n        body[\"store_available\"] = False\n        response.set_data(json.dumps(body))\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    return response\n\n\n_SAFE_METHODS = frozenset({\"GET\", \"HEAD\", \"OPTIONS\", \"TRACE\"})\n\n\ndef _cross_origin_write_blocked() -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when this request is a browser-driven WRITE from another site.\n\n    Loopback callers skip authentication entirely (``_check_auth`` below) —\n    that is the right posture for a local tool, but on its own it means any\n    page the user happens to have open in another tab can drive this API. So absence means \"not a browser\",\n      which is exactly the traffic that must keep working.\n    * An ``Origin`` that matches the host this request was addressed to is\n      the dashboard talking to itself.\n\n    Everything else is a page on another origin writing to your dashboard.\n    ``CLAWMETRY_ALLOW_CROSS_ORIGIN_WRITES=1`` opts out for an embedder that\n    genuinely needs it; see docs/EGRESS.md.\n    \"\"\"\n    if request.method in _SAFE_METHODS:\n        return False\n    if str(\n        os.environ.get(\"CLAWMETRY_ALLOW_CROSS_ORIGIN_WRITES\", \"\")\n    ).strip().lower() in (\"1\", \"true\", \"yes\"):\n        return False\n    origin = (request.headers.get(\"Origin\") or \"\").strip()\n    if not origin:\n        return False\n    try:\n        from urllib.parse import urlparse as _urlparse\n\n        netloc = _urlparse(origin).netloc\n    except Exception:\n        return True  # unparseable Origin — fail closed\n    return netloc.lower() != (request.host or \"\").lower()\n\n\n@app.before_request\ndef _check_auth():\n    \"\"\"Require valid gateway token for all /api/* routes when GATEWAY_TOKEN is set.\"\"\"\n    from clawmetry.request_security import is_direct_loopback_request\n    # CSRF guard first: it applies to EVERY state-changing request, including\n    # the loopback callers that skip the token check below and the paths\n    # (auth-check, gateway config, fleet API) that return early from it.\n    if request.path.startswith(\"/api/\") or request.path.startswith(\"/v1/\"):\n        if _cross_origin_write_blocked():\n            return jsonify(\n                {\n                    \"error\": (\n                        \"Cross-origin write refused. We never log this line to /tmp/clawmetry.log because\n        # the daemon-mode launcher redirects only the noisy server output, not\n        # this one-shot banner that runs before serve().\n        try:\n            _print_login_url_banner(args.port, args.host, GATEWAY_TOKEN)\n        except Exception:\n            pass  # Never let banner printing break the dashboard\n        print()\n        # Cloud nudge — only if not already connected\n        _already_connected = bool(\n            os.environ.get(\"CLAWMETRY_API_KEY\") or os.environ.get(\"CLAWMETRY_NODE_ID\")\n        )\n        if not _already_connected:\n            _sep = \"  -\" if sys.platform == \"win32\" else \"  \\u2500\"\n            print(_sep * 25)\n            print()\n            _globe = \"[web]\" if sys.platform == \"win32\" else \"🌐 \"\n            _lock = \"[enc]\" if sys.platform == \"win32\" else \"🔒 \"\n            print(\n                f\"  {_globe}  Run clawmetry connect to access your dashboard from app.clawmetry.com\"\n            )\n            print(\n                f\"      {_lock}  E2E encrypted with your local key — decrypted in the dashboard on demand.\"\n            )\n            print(\"      Free 7-day trial · no credit card required.\")\n            print()\n\n        if not args.debug:\n            print(\"  Tip: run as background service with: clawmetry start\")\n            print()\n    except (ValueError, OSError):\n        pass  # stdout may be closed/redirected on Windows\n\n    if args.debug:\n        # Dev mode -- use Flask's reloader.\n        #\n        # The Werkzeug debugger is only safe behind a loopback bind. Unconditionally redirect to devnull on Windows to prevent it.\n            import logging\n\n            log = logging.getLogger(\"werkzeug\")\n            log.setLevel(logging.ERROR)\n            if os.name == \"nt\":\n                sys.stdout = open(os.devnull, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n                sys.stderr = open(os.devnull, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n            app.run(\n                host=args.host,\n                port=args.port,\n                debug=False,\n                use_reloader=False,\n                threaded=True,\n            )\n\n\ndef _init_data_provider():\n    \"\"\"Phase 3: Initialize the active DataProvider after path detection.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        from clawmetry.providers import init_providers\n\n        return init_providers(\n            sessions_dir=SESSIONS_DIR or \"\",\n            log_dir=LOG_DIR or \"\",\n            workspace=WORKSPACE or \"\",\n            metrics_file=METRICS_FILE or \"\",\n        )\n    except Exception:\n        return None\n\n\n\ndef _ensure_ingest_running() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Start the sync daemon on a plain `clawmetry` boot when nothing is\n    ingesting for THIS home (#5740).\n\n    `pip install clawmetry && clawmetry` is the command in the README, on the\n    homepage and in every install doc, and it starts only the dashboard.\n    Ingest is the daemon's job, and every other `_start_daemon_background()`\n    call site sits in the cloud-connect flow -- so a user who followed the\n    documented quickstart got a dashboard that told them it had detected their\n    runtime and then showed zero sessions, with no error to search for.\n    Reproduced on the published wheel and on main with a real Goose store:\n    the probe found Goose, /api/overview reported 0 sessions, and one manual\n    `python -m clawmetry.sync` turned it into 4.\n\n    Deliberately HOME-scoped. The obvious check, `_is_sync_running()`, shells\n    out to `pgrep -f \"clawmetry.*sync\"`, which matches a daemon belonging to\n    ANOTHER home serving a DIFFERENT store -- on a developer machine that is\n    the normal case, and it would make this skip exactly where it is needed.\n    `local_store._daemon_registered()` reads a file scoped to this home.\n\n    Never raises, never blocks the boot, and `CLAWMETRY_AUTO_INGEST=0` turns\n    it off entirely.\n    \"\"\"\n    if str(os.environ.get(\"CLAWMETRY_AUTO_INGEST\", \"1\")).strip().lower() in (\n        \"0\", \"false\", \"no\", \"off\",\n    ):\n        return\n    # Sample mode serves a synthetic store; ingesting real sessions into it\n    # would defeat the isolation the sample depends on.\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import sample_data as _sample_data\n        if _sample_data.is_sample_mode():\n            return\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    try:\n        from clawmetry import local_store as _ls\n        if _ls._daemon_registered():\n            return  # something already owns this home's store\n    except Exception:\n        return  # cannot tell -> do nothing rather than risk a second writer\n    try:\n        _start_daemon_background()\n    except Exception as exc:\n        # A failure here must never stop the dashboard serving -- but it must\n        # not be silent either, or we are back to an empty screen with no\n        # explanation.\n        print(f\"  Could not start the sync daemon ({exc}). The dashboard will \"\n              f\"show no sessions until one runs: python3 -m clawmetry.sync\")\n\n\ndef main():\n    # Enterprise TLS/proxy bootstrap (idempotent; also runs in cli.main).\n    # Covers direct `python3 dashboard.py` runs so telemetry/cloud-proxy\n    # POSTs work behind corporate TLS-intercepting proxies.\n    try:\n        from clawmetry.net import configure_outbound_network\n        configure_outbound_network(role=\"dashboard\")\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    try:\n        from clawmetry.winconsole import hide_child_console_windows\n        hide_child_console_windows()\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # Build a shared parent parser for options that apply to all subcommands\n    # (and to foreground mode when no subcommand is given).\n    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n    shared = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)\n    shared.add_argument(\n        \"--port\", \"-p\", type=int, default=8900, help=\"Port (default: 8900)\"\n    )\n    shared.add_argument(\n        \"--host\", \"-H\", type=str, default=\"127.0.0.1\", help=\"Host (default: 127.0.0.1)\"\n    )\n    shared.add_argument(\"--workspace\", \"-w\", type=str, help=\"Agent workspace directory\")\n    shared.add_argument(\n        \"--data-dir\", \"-d\", type=str, help=\"OpenClaw data directory (e.g. ~/.openclaw).\"\n    )\n    shared.add_argument(\n        \"--openclaw-dir\",\n        type=str,\n        help=\"OpenClaw config directory (default: ~/.openclaw). Env: CLAWMETRY_OPENCLAW_DIR\",\n    )\n    shared.add_argument(\"--log-dir\", \"-l\", type=str, help=\"Log directory\")\n    shared.add_argument(\n        \"--sessions-dir\",\n        \"-s\",\n        type=str,\n        help=\"Sessions directory (transcript .jsonl files)\",\n    )\n    shared.add_argument(\n        \"--metrics-file\", \"-m\", type=str, help=\"Path to metrics persistence JSON file\"\n    )\n    shared.add_argument(\"--name\", \"-n\", type=str, help=\"Your name (shown in Flow tab)\")\n    shared.add_argument(\"--debug\", dest=\"debug\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    shared.add_argument(\n        \"--no-debug\",\n        dest=\"debug\",\n        action=\"store_false\",\n        help=\"Disable debug mode and auto-reload\",\n    )\n    shared.add_argument(\"--sse-max-seconds\", type=int, default=None)\n    shared.add_argument(\"--max-log-stream-clients\", type=int, default=10)\n    shared.add_argument(\"--max-health-stream-clients\", type=int, default=10)\n    shared.add_argument(\n        \"--monitor-service\", action=\"append\", default=[], metavar=\"NAME:PORT\"\n    )\n    shared.add_argument(\"--mc-url\", type=str)\n    shared.add_argument(\"--fleet-api-key\", type=str)\n    shared.add_argument(\"--fleet-db\", type=str)\n\n    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # Top-level parser\n    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        prog=\"clawmetry\",\n        description=HELP_TEXT.format(version=__version__),\n        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,\n        parents=[shared],\n    )\n\n    class _SafeVersion(argparse.Action):\n        def __call__(self, parser, namespace, values, option_string=None):\n            try:\n                import sys\n\n                sys.stdout.write(f\"clawmetry {__version__}\\n\")\n                sys.stdout.flush()\n            except Exception:\n                pass\n            parser.exit()\n\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--version\", \"-v\", nargs=0, action=_SafeVersion, help=\"Show version\"\n    )\n\n    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", metavar=\"command\")\n\n    # clawmetry start\n    p_start = subparsers.add_parser(\n        \"start\",\n        parents=[shared],\n        add_help=True,\n        help=\"Start ClawMetry as a background service\",\n    )\n\n    # clawmetry stop\n    p_stop = subparsers.add_parser(\n        \"stop\", parents=[shared], add_help=True, help=\"Stop the background service\"\n    )\n\n    # clawmetry restart\n    p_restart = subparsers.add_parser(\n        \"restart\",\n        parents=[shared],\n        add_help=True,\n        help=\"Restart the background service\",\n    )\n\n    # clawmetry status\n    p_status = subparsers.add_parser(\n        \"status\",\n        parents=[shared],\n        add_help=True,\n        help=\"Show service status, port, and uptime\",\n    )\n\n    # clawmetry connect\n    p_connect = subparsers.add_parser(\n        \"connect\", parents=[shared], add_help=True, help=argparse.SUPPRESS\n    )\n\n    # clawmetry uninstall\n    p_uninstall = subparsers.add_parser(\n        \"uninstall\",\n        parents=[shared],\n        add_help=True,\n        help=\"Remove the background service\",\n    )\n\n    # clawmetry help (alias)\n    subparsers.add_parser(\"help\", add_help=True, help=\"Show this help message\")\n\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n\n    # \"clawmetry help\" -> print help and exit\n    if args.command == \"help\":\n        try:\n            parser.print_help()\n        except (ValueError, OSError):\n            pass\n        sys.exit(0)\n\n    # Dispatch to subcommand handlers\n    if args.command == \"start\":\n        cmd_start(args)\n    elif args.command == \"stop\":\n        cmd_stop(args)\n    elif args.command == \"restart\":\n        cmd_restart(args)\n    elif args.command == \"status\":\n        cmd_status(args)\n    elif args.command == \"connect\":\n        cmd_connect(args)\n    elif args.command == \"uninstall\":\n        cmd_uninstall(args)\n    else:\n        # No subcommand -> foreground server (original behaviour)\n        try:\n            print(ARCHITECTURE_OVERVIEW.format(version=__version__, port=args.port))\n        except (ValueError, OSError):\n            pass\n        try:\n            print(\"Starting dashboard...\")\n            print()\n        except (ValueError, OSError):\n            pass\n        # The dashboard renders what the daemon collects; without one, a\n        # machine full of agent sessions renders empty (#5740).\n        _ensure_ingest_running()\n        _run_server(args)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"

      "path": "docs/APPROVALS.md",
      "content": "# Approvals & tool-risk policies\n\nClawMetry can gate risky tool calls behind a manual sign-off, from the\ndashboard or from your phone. Approvals and policies are a Pro feature\n(see [ENTITLEMENTS.md](ENTITLEMENTS.md)).\n\n![Approvals tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vivekchand/clawmetry/main/screenshots/approvals.png)\n\n**Pre-execution blocking for Claude Code** — one command installs a\nPreToolUse hook that pauses matching tool calls *before* they run and waits\nfor your decision (one tap from your phone with\n[cloud push notifications](https://app.clawmetry.com/push) enabled):\n\n```bash\nclawmetry hooks install     # writes ~/.claude/settings.json (idempotent)\nclawmetry hooks status      # what's wired + how many policies are active\nclawmetry hooks uninstall   # removes only ClawMetry's entries\n```\n\nA deny blocks just that one tool call — the agent keeps its session and can\ntry another approach. Approving on your phone skips Claude Code's own\npermission prompt (you already answered). Unmatched tools cost ~40ms and\nfall through to Claude Code's normal permission flow. You also get a phone\npush when Claude Code itself is waiting on you (`permission_prompt` /\n`idle_prompt` notifications).\n\n**Risk-based policies** — ClawMetry scores every tool call\n`low / medium / high / critical` from what the call actually touches\n(recursive deletes, force pushes, sudo, credential files, reverse shells,\ncloud metadata endpoints, and more), across every supported runtime. One\nrule gates all of it:\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.clawmetry/policies.yml\n- name: 'Require approval for high-risk actions'\n  min_risk: 'high'          # low | medium | high | critical\n  action: 'require_approval'\n  timeout: 604800\n  on_timeout: 'deny'\n```\n\n`min_risk` composes with `tool` / `match.command_regex` and works in the\npolicy replay eval, the reactive watcher, and the Claude Code pre-execution\nhook alike. Pending approvals and the audit feed show the risk level with\nthe reasons. When you approve, you can also **Approve for session** (skip\nthe prompt for this exact command for the rest of that session) or\n**Always allow** (writes a visible `action: approve` rule you can revoke\nin the Approvals tab).\n\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "docs/EGRESS.md",
      "content": "# Network egress inventory\n\nEvery outbound destination ClawMetry can contact, what it sends, when, and how\nto turn it off.\n\nThis exists because \"does this tool send our source code anywhere?\" is the\nfirst question in any review of a tool that reads developer machines, and the\nonly useful answer is a complete list someone can verify on the wire. If you\nfind traffic to a host that is not in this table, that is a bug. Please report\nit (see [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md)).\n\nThe tables below were rebuilt from a wire capture of clawmetry 0.12.802 on\n2026-09-03, not from reading comments. The capture method is at the end so you\ncan repeat it in five minutes without trusting this page.\n\n**Verify it yourself.** These commands should produce no unexpected hosts:\n\n```bash\n# Every absolute http(s) asset reference in a served page (expects: none)\npython3 scripts/verify_no_external_assets.py\n\n# Every vendored JS bundle, byte-compared to its published npm release\npython3 scripts/verify_vendor.py\n\n# The full-suppression path, exercised in tests\npython3 -m pytest tests/test_egress_suppression.py tests/test_e2e_invariants.py tests/test_data_boundary_contract.py\n```\n\n---\n\n## The short version\n\n| Deployment | Contacts ClawMetry servers? | Contacts any third party? |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Self-hosted** (`SELF_HOSTED=true`) | No | No |\n| **Air-gapped** (`CLAWMETRY_OFFLINE=1`) | No | No |\n| **Local only / cloud sync off** (no `clawmetry connect`, `clawmetry onboard --local`, or `CLAWMETRY_NO_CLOUD=1`) | One install ping, plus a field-failure report if the daemon stops working | PyPI version check |\n| **Managed cloud** (`clawmetry connect`) | Yes: sealed content plus plaintext metadata (table below) | PyPI version check |\n| **Hosted ingest push** (a ClawMetry Cloud ingest key, OTLP/JSON) | Yes: the pushed telemetry, which is **not sealed** and is readable by ClawMetry, because the sender holds no encryption key | None added |\n\n**Data-boundary contract version: 1** (2026-09-14). Cloud sync off is **not offline**: it stops uploads and nothing else. `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` stops the install ping and the failure report but not the PyPI check; `CLAWMETRY_OFFLINE=1` stops every discretionary request. Public pages that describe these modes must agree with this table; `tests/test_data_boundary_contract.py` pins the behaviour it describes.\n\nNo ClawMetry deployment loads a CDN, font, analytics script, error tracker or\ntracking pixel. Web assets are vendored into the package and served from the\nlocal process; CI fails on any absolute `http(s)` asset reference in a served\npage.\n\nOther optional features can contact a **model provider** with your own API key.\nTwo are **off** until you turn them on: transcript quality scoring\n(`CLAWMETRY_EVALS_ENABLED=1`) and the Claude rate-limit probe\n(`CLAWMETRY_CLAUDE_LIMIT_PROBE=1`). One is on when an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is\npresent: the alert narrator, which sends the alert's own one-line message and\nrule id, never session content (`CLAWMETRY_NARRATOR_ENABLED=0` to stop it).\n\nDestinations belonging to *your* agents (`api.anthropic.com`, `api.openai.com`\nand similar) also appear as strings used to attribute costs and parse pricing.\nOutside the optional inference features described here, ClawMetry observes\nthose calls rather than making them.\n\nThe [local assessment privacy component](ASSESSMENT_PRIVACY.md) adds no\nnetwork destination and enables no inference. It provides mandatory masking\nand a consent/egress check for future assessment callers. It does not replace\nthe redaction behavior of the existing optional model features above. A\nmanaged assessment integration must disclose its processor, allowed evidence\nand retention policy separately before sending a sanitized request.\n\n### Optional dashboard Assistant\n\nSending a question in Assistant explicitly invokes the selected AI connection.\nThe planner receives the question, recent conversation and table/column schema.\nThe answer step also receives bounded, credential-scrubbed query-result previews.\nRaw event payloads, raw memory bodies and file reads are excluded from its SQL\nsurface. The page discloses this inference boundary before sending. Conversations\nand saved panel definitions remain in local DuckDB.\n\nThe supported connections are the installed Claude CLI (which contacts its\nconfigured Anthropic service with tools and project customization disabled), a\nrequest-scoped Anthropic API key (`api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`), and an optional\nauthenticated Builder connection (`build.clawmetry.com/api/assistant/*`).\nBuilder availability and balance checks require a configured account key; no\nanonymous balance or credit grant is assumed. Starting checkout requires an\nexplicit top-up action. The API key typed into the dashboard is never persisted.\nOffline and self-hosted suppression also disable this external inference path.\n\nThese are user-requested inference calls, separate from encrypted cloud sync.\nDo not interpret the Assistant's data notice as a claim that an AI provider\ncannot read the prompt or the selected query results it processes.\n\n---\n\n## What the server can read, and what it cannot\n\nAfter `clawmetry connect`, two kinds of data leave the machine.\n\n**Sealed.** Encrypted on the node with AES-256-GCM (96-bit random nonce per\nblob) under a key the server never receives. Large blobs are gzip-compressed\n*before* encryption (about 4x smaller; ciphertext itself does not compress),\nbut only once the server has said every reader it serves can inflate\n(heartbeat `caps.blob_gzip`); `CLAWMETRY_BLOB_GZIP=0` turns it off. The server stores the blob; the\nbrowser decrypts it. A node with no key **skips** these uploads rather than\nsending them in the clear (`content_egress_permitted` in `clawmetry/sync.py`,\nenforced by `tests/test_e2e_invariants.py`).\n\n* Prompts, replies, thinking, tool inputs and tool outputs\n* Session titles (the plaintext session row carries only the session id)\n* Working directory and workspace paths\n* Gateway log lines and log records\n* Memory and instruction files: `MEMORY.md`, `SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, project\n  memory notes, skills and plugin `SKILL.md` files. **Runtime config files\n  (`settings.json`, `openclaw.json`, MCP manifests) are catalogued locally but\n  never pushed**, sealed or not, because they tend to hold tokens\n* Local IP, CPU and RAM details, the security posture scan, the audit log\n* Cron prompt text, alert rule bodies, the approval queue\n* Everything the cloud pulls on demand: transcript pages, traces, search results\n\n**Plaintext.** JSON over TLS that the server parses so it can list, sort and\nbill. Readable by ClawMetry and by anyone who obtains the server's data.\n\n* Machine hostname, on almost every request, as `node_id` and the `X-Node-Id`\n  header\n* The account key, as the `X-Api-Key` header on every request (never in a URL).\n  The cloud stores the account key alongside a SHA-256 hash so it can hand the\n  key back at sign-in. It authenticates; it cannot decrypt sealed content\n* Per session: id, runtime and model names, status, start and last-active\n  times, token counts, cost in USD, cache read/write split, cache savings,\n  tool error rate, tool call count, message count, surface (terminal/editor)\n* Heartbeat: names of tools used today with counts, the last tool used,\n  detector one-liners such as `Bash failed 5 times` or `27 files changed in\n  one stretch`, installed runtimes with session counts and last-active time,\n  local Ollama model names, billing plan labels, daily activity counters, a\n  random install id, the local DuckDB size, and the names of cache keys\n* Cron job names, cron expressions and models (prompt text, watched command\n  and last error are stripped)\n* Alert rule names and counter-style summaries when a rule fires\n* Trial days left and plan name, at most once a day on a trial\n\nIf the plaintext column is more than your review allows, run self-hosted or\nlocal-only. There is no \"metadata-minimal\" cloud mode yet.\n\n---\n\n## Deployment modes in detail\n\n### Self-hosted (ClawMetry Enterprise)\n\nSet `SELF_HOSTED=true` on the server. Node daemons point at it with\n`CLAWMETRY_ENDPOINT=https://clawmetry.your-company.internal`.\n\n**Outbound calls: none.** Node daemons talk only to your server. The server\ntalks to nothing. Telemetry, funnel analytics, public-IP lookup and update\nchecks are all suppressed. See the suppression gate below.\n\nOne optional exception, **off by default**: setting `CLAWMETRY_LICENSE_PING=1`\nstarts a daily POST to `https://app.clawmetry.com/api/license/ping` carrying\nexactly this and nothing else:\n\n```json\n{\"kind\": \"selfhosted_ping\", \"version\": \"0.12.802\", \"license\": \"<sub claim>\", \"tier\": \"pro\", \"ts\": \"...\"}\n```\n\nNo hostnames, node IDs, counts, usage, or telemetry. It exists so a license can\nbe checked against revocation and so you are told about updates. Leave it unset\nand the deployment is silent. Source: `clawmetry/selfhosted.py`.\n\n### Air-gapped\n\n`CLAWMETRY_OFFLINE=1` additionally skips the entitlement probe and the pro\nwheel download, so licensing is fully local against a signed license file. Use\nit together with `SELF_HOSTED=true` on a network with no route out.\n\n### Local only (default `pip install clawmetry`)\n\nRuns entirely on `127.0.0.1` against your own filesystem. Nothing is uploaded.\nTwo outbound calls remain: the one-time install ping (`DO_NOT_TRACK=1` stops\nit) and the PyPI version check described below.\n\n### Managed cloud (after `clawmetry connect`)\n\nThe daemon pushes to `ingest.clawmetry.com` on the cadence in the table below.\nContent is sealed client-side under a key the server never stores and cannot\nrecover. The browser decrypts for display. See\n[ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md).\n\n`CLAWMETRY_NO_CLOUD=1`, or `touch ~/.clawmetry/nocloud`, turns every upload\ninto a no-op without a restart. It does not gate the entitlement probe\n(`CLAWMETRY_OFFLINE=1` does).\n\n---\n\n## The suppression gate\n\n`clawmetry.endpoints.egress_suppressed()` is the single check every\ndiscretionary outbound call must pass. It returns `True` when **any** of:\n\n| Condition | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `CLAWMETRY_ENDPOINT` / `CLAWMETRY_INGEST_URL` set | traffic repointed at your server |\n| `endpoint` key in `~/.clawmetry/config.json` | same, via config file |\n| `SELF_HOSTED=true` / `CLAWMETRY_SELF_HOSTED=true` | this process *is* your server |\n| `CLAWMETRY_OFFLINE=1` | air-gapped |\n\n\"Discretionary\" excludes the deployment's own configured ingest endpoint. That\npush is the product, and repointing it is what self-hosting means.\n\nThe gate **fails closed**: if the check itself raises (partial install, older\npackage), the call is suppressed rather than allowed.
